Initially created: 2025-11-23T03:23:43.282+09:00 by CHYou are a precise translator from Classical Chinese to $lang. Your task is to produce faithful, fluent $lang translations while preserving all formatting constraints exactly. Translate the following text from Classical Chinese into $lang.
Requirements: 1. The text contains page numbers in square brackets, such as [01], [02], etc. - These must be passed through unchanged. - Each page number must appear in exactly the same position in the translation as in the source. - The number of page markers in the output must match the input exactly.
2. Personal names, place names, titles, and other proper nouns should be rendered in Hànyǔ Pīnyīn with tone marks.
3. Do NOT transcribe the full Classical Chinese text into Pinyin.
4. Do NOT include explanatory notes, annotations, or commentary — output only the $lang translation.
5. The target language is $lang.

p.seg: In the past, the Tathāgata was at Qízhéjué Mountain,
together with the great Āluóhàn Āruò Jiāochénrú,
Móhējiāyè and countless others,
expounding the True Sūtra of the Great Vehicle,
named the Wúliàng Yì.
At that time, celestial jewels and flowers rained down, spreading everywhere and filling all space;
the light of wisdom manifested auspicious signs, illuminating both hidden and manifest;
the worlds of all buddhas were shaken in six ways;
all people and gods experienced something unprecedented,
all rejoicing and praising,
regarding this sūtra as the secret treasury of the buddhas and Tathāgatas,
divine and wondrous, unfathomable,
vast and difficult to name,
therefore able to lift those stuck and drowning in the deep current,
to rescue the lost and deluded from confusion,
with merit vast and distant, without limit or boundary.
Tracing its origin,
it first flowed from Zhújiàn in India into Zhèndàn.
From the time of the Western Jìn, the śramaṇa Zhú Fǎhù first engaged in translation,
naming it *Zhèng Fǎ Huá*;
then, during the Eastern Jìn, the Kuízī Tripiṭaka master, Jiūmóluóshí, retranslated it,
naming it *Miào Fǎ Lián Huá*;
and in the Suí era, the Indian śramaṇa Shénà Jíduō also translated it,
also titled *Miào Fǎ*.
Although the three sūtras’ texts and principles are layered and interwoven,
only the Tripiṭaka master truly grasped its essence.
Yet, over time, errors cannot be avoided,
and without correction, doubts gradually increase,
so special effort was made in careful collation,
and it was further commissioned for woodblock printing to widely disseminate it.
Alas!
The Tathāgata, out of compassion for all beings’ various natures,
various desires,
various actions,
various memories and discriminations,
bound up through countless eons with no end in sight,
thus appeared in the world for this great cause,
expansively expounding the subtle meaning,
devising unsurpassed skillful means,
so that all may attain liberation and rise to perfect enlightenment.
Truly, this is a raft for crossing the sea and a torch of wisdom illuminating the obscure.
O good men
and good women,
all sentient beings,
those who can hold this sūtra in heart with utmost sincerity—reciting, wearing, honoring, and making offerings—
will at once be freed from all suffering and distress,
all karmic obstacles will be eliminated,
and all perils of birth and death will be resolved.
It is like the hungry obtaining food,
like the thirsty obtaining drink,
like the cold obtaining fire,
like the hot obtaining coolness,
like the poor obtaining treasure,
like the sick obtaining a healer,
like a child meeting its mother,
like a traveler finding a boat to cross;
the happiness and joy
are beyond words.
Ah!
Without sūtras, the Way cannot be conveyed;
without sūtras, the Dharma cannot be transmitted.
Through sūtras one seeks the Dharma,
through the Dharma one realizes the Way,
thereby discerning that the essence of this sūtra is pure, subtle, supreme and rare.
Those who follow it will attain physical health and peace,
all kinds of wholesome roots complete in fullness,
like a lotus emerging from water, unstained by the mud,
instantly realizing the emptiness of the five aggregates,
the six faculties purified,
quickly ascending to supreme goodness and easily attaining enlightenment.
But if one is mired in delusion and obstinacy,
willingly falling, severing all wholesome roots,
the body must endure the suffering destinations
revolving in the domains of birth and death—
is there any limit?
Nevertheless, good and evil both depend on each person’s choices:
to do good brings blessing,
to do evil brings calamity,
the retribution of darkness and light never errs by even a hair’s breadth.
Those who contemplate this sūtra
should be especially vigilant!
Should especially strive!
On the seventeenth day of the fourth month in the eighteenth year of Yǒnglè
Shì Dàoxuān of Zhōngnán Mountain, Táng, composed this introduction to the Miào Fǎ Lián Huá Jīng,
which encompasses the origin of the descent of all buddhas.
Its virtues have gathered in Great Xià,
passing through those thousand years.
Transmitted east to Zhèndàn,
over three hundred years.
In the Yǒngkāng years of Emperor Huì of Western Jìn,
in Cháng’ān, Qīngmén, the Bodhisattva of Dūnhuáng, Zhú Fǎhù,
first translated this sūtra,
titled *Zhèng Fǎ Huá*.
In the Lóng’ān years of Emperor Ān of Eastern Jìn,
Hóngshǐ of Later Qín,
the Kuízī śramaṇa Jiūmóluóshí next translated this sūtra,
called *Miào Fǎ Lián Huá*.
In Rénshòu of the Suí dynasty,
at Dàxīngshàn Monastery, the Indian śramaṇa Shénà Jíduō's later translation
was likewise called *Miào Fǎ*.
The three sūtras are layered,
their texts and meanings interwoven.
The version honored in those times,
all widely followed the Qín edition.
As for other branches and sections,
as well as separate gāthās,
some versions indeed circulated,
as recorded in historical catalogues,
and so will not be discussed here.
When the divine peaks received spirits,
only a great sage could initiate the transformation;
as for those transformed,
only past causes could direct their minds.
And so the Immortals’ Gardens were completed,
suiting the difference of faculties great and small;
at Golden River, a final command was given,
distinguishing the grades of partial and full realization.
Was this not a teaching fit for the era,
impossible to gauge its ultimate wisdom?
Thus, five thousand left their seats,
being those who advanced in arrogance;
five hundred received predictions,
all held as traces of esoteric transformation.
Therefore the Buddha emitted light and revealed auspicious signs,
opening the source of teachings requested;
emerging from samādhi, proclaiming virtue,
fully expressing the vast outline of Buddha wisdom.
The decaying house is opened to the great path,
the illusory city draws in past causes so they’re not lost,
the threaded pearls reveal the constant presence of true nature,
the well’s excavation displays the many ways to awakening.
The words and meaning are clear,
the analogies set forth are far-reaching.
Had it not been for great, universal compassion
to lift up the stuck and drowning from the deep current,
infinite sympathy
to save those lost and confused—we would not have received it.
From Hàn to Táng over six hundred years,
covering more than four thousand fascicles of scripture,
none were more revered in practice than this sūtra.
Is it not because the teachings are just right for the faculties?
Their brilliance surpasses the scattered dust of lesser wisdom;
when heard, they inspire deep reverence,
altogether continuing the merit of the mighty kings.
Thus, at the head of the sūtra,
I compile this preface in summary.
May all quickly purify the six faculties,
look up to the Tathāgata’s joyous gathering;
swiftly accomplish the four virtues,
and take delight in the subtle path of the Pure Land.
May the praise and support be boundless,
an everlasting legacy for generations to come.
So it is.
The Wondrous Dharma Lotus Sūtra, Scroll One
Translated by the Kuízī Tripiṭaka Master Jiūmóluóshí during Later Qín by imperial decree
Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying at Qízhéjué Mountain in Rājagṛha,
together with a great assembly of twelve thousand bhikṣus,
all of whom were Āluóhàn,
their outflows already ended,
no more afflictions,
having attained their own benefit,
completely severed all bonds of becoming,
and their minds were liberated.
Their names were: Āruò Jiāochénrú,
Móhējiāyè,
Yōulóupínluó Jiāyè,
Jiāyé Jiāyè,
Nàtí Jiāyè,
Shèlìfú,
Mahāmóujiānlián,
Móhējiāzhānyán,
Ānluóutuo,
Jiébīnnà,
Jiāofánbōtí,
Líbóduō,
Bìlíngjiāpóchùo,
Bójūluó,
Móhējiūchīluó,
Nánduō,
Sūntuóluónánduō,
Fùlóunàmíduōluónízi,
Xūpútí,
Ānán,
Luóhóuluó.
These were the renowned great Āluóhàn in the assembly.
There were also two thousand who were still learning and those with nothing left to learn.
Mahāprajāpatī Bhikṣuṇī, together with a retinue of six thousand,
and Luóhóuluó’s mother Yēshūtuóluó Bhikṣuṇī,
were also present with their attendants.
Eighty thousand Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
all have reached non-retrogression with respect to Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi;
all have attained dhāraṇī;
they delight in eloquent speech,
and turn the wheel of the Dharma of non-retrogression;
they have made offerings to innumerable hundreds of thousands of Buddhas,
and at the feet of those Buddhas have planted all roots of virtue;
they are always praised by the Buddhas;
cultivating themselves by means of compassion,
they skillfully enter the Buddha-wisdom;
they thoroughly understand great wisdom,
and reach the other shore;
their names are heard throughout countless worlds,
and they are able to deliver innumerable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings.
Their names are: Wénshūshīlì Bodhisattva,
Guānshìyīn Bodhisattva,
Dedàshì Bodhisattva,
Chángjīngjìn Bodhisattva,
Bùxiūxī Bodhisattva,
Bǎozhǎng Bodhisattva,
Yàowáng Bodhisattva,
Yǒngshī Bodhisattva,
Bǎoyuè Bodhisattva,
Yuèguāng Bodhisattva,
Mǎnyuè Bodhisattva,
Dàlì Bodhisattva,
Wúliànglì Bodhisattva,
Yuèsānjiè Bodhisattva,
Bádàpóluó Bodhisattva,
Mílè Bodhisattva,
Bǎojī Bodhisattva,
Dǎoshī Bodhisattva,
and so on, with such Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas numbering eighty thousand together.
At that time, Shìdíhuányīn, together with his retinue of twenty thousand devas,
and also Míngyuè Deva Prince,
Pǔxiāng Deva Prince,
Bǎoguāng Deva Prince,
the Four Great Heavenly Kings,
together with their retinue of ten thousand deva princes.
Zìzài Deva Prince,
Dàzìzài Deva Prince,
together with their retinue of thirty thousand deva princes.
The lord of the Sābā World,
Brahmā King—
Shīqì Dàfàn,
Guāngmíng Dàfàn, and so forth,
together with their retinue of twelve thousand deva princes.
There were eight Dragon Kings—
Nántuó Dragon King,
Bánántuó Dragon King,
Suōqiéluó Dragon King,
Héxiūjí Dragon King,
Déchājiā Dragon King,
Ānàpódàduō Dragon King,
Mónàsī Dragon King,
Yōupótúluó Dragon King, and others,
each with their respective hundreds of thousands of retinue.
There were four Kinnarā Kings—
Fǎ Kinnarā King,
Miàofǎ Kinnarā King,
Dàfǎ Kinnarā King,
Chífǎ Kinnarā King,
each with their respective hundreds of thousands of retinue.
There were four Gandharva Kings—
Yuè Gandharva King,
Yuèyīn Gandharva King,
Měi Gandharva King,
Měiyīn Gandharva King,
each with their respective hundreds of thousands of retinue.
There were four Asura Kings—
Pózhì Asura King,
Qūluóqiàntuó Asura King,
Pímózhíduōluó Asura King,
Luóhóu Asura King,
each with their respective hundreds of thousands of retinue.
There were four Garuḍa Kings—
Dàwēidé Garuḍa King,
Dàshēn Garuḍa King,
Dàmǎn Garuḍa King,
Rúyì Garuḍa King,
each with their respective hundreds of thousands of retinue.
Vaitéhī's son, Ājiāshì King,
with his own hundreds of thousands of retinue.
Each paid homage at the Buddha's feet, and withdrew to sit at one side.
At that time, the World-Honored One,
was surrounded by the four assemblies,
offering, honoring,
respecting, and praising him.
For the bodhisattvas he preached the Mahāyāna sūtra,
named Immeasurable Meaning,
teaching the Bodhisattva Path,
protected and remembered by the Buddhas.
When the Buddha had finished preaching this sūtra,
he entered into cross-legged sitting,
and entered the samādhi of the realm of Immeasurable Meanings.
His body and mind were unmoving.
At this time, from the heavens rained mandarava flowers,
great mandarava flowers,
mahaman-jushaka flowers,
great mahaman-jushaka flowers,
which were scattered over the Buddha and the great congregation.
Throughout the Buddha world, six kinds of tremors occurred.
At that time, in the assembly, there were bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās,
devas, dragons, yaksas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, human and non-human beings,
as well as minor kings and wheel-turning sage kings:
all these great multitudes experienced something unprecedented,
joyfully pressed their palms together, and with a single mind gazed at the Buddha.
At that time, the Buddha emitted light from the white hair-mark between his eyebrows,
illuminating eighteen thousand worlds to the east;
there was none it did not reach,
from below in the Avīci Hell,
upward to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven.
In that world, all the beings of the six destinies there were fully visible;
also seen were the Buddhas currently present in those lands,
as well as the scriptures and Dharma spoken by those Buddhas.
Also seen were their bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, and all practitioners who had attained the way.
Also seen were Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas there, with their various causal conditions, understandings, and appearances, practicing the Bodhisattva Path.
Also seen were Buddhas who had entered parinirvāṇa.
Also seen were, after the Buddhas had entered parinirvāṇa, stūpas of seven precious substances being erected for their relics.
Then Mílè Bodhisattva had this thought:
“Now the World-Honored One is displaying supernormal transformations;
for what reason does such an auspicious sign appear?
Now the Buddha, the World-Honored One, has entered samādhi;
this is inconceivable and a rare occurrence.
Whom should I ask?
Who can answer?”
He further thought:
“This Wénshūshīlì, son of the Dharma King,
has, in the past, personally attended and made offerings to countless Buddhas;
he surely must have seen this rare sign.
I should now ask him.”
At that time, the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, as well as all devas, dragons, spirits, and so forth,
all had this thought:
“This marks the Buddha’s power of light and spiritual abilities;
whom should we now ask?”
At this time, Mílè Bodhisattva, wishing to resolve his own doubts,
also contemplated the thoughts of the four assemblies—bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, as well as devas, dragons, spirits, and the assembled multitude,
and inquired of Wénshūshīlì, saying:
“For what reason does such an auspicious spiritual sign appear—
great light being released, illuminating eighteen thousand lands to the east,
so that one sees the adornments of those Buddha realms?”
Then Mílè Bodhisattva, wishing to restate this meaning,
questioned him in verse, saying:
Wénshūshīlì!
Why does the Teacher, from the white hair-mark between his eyebrows,
emit great light that universally shines?
Heavenly mandarava and mahaman-jushaka flowers rain down;
sandalwood-scented winds delight all present.
Because of this, the earth becomes beautifully adorned and pure,
and this world experiences six kinds of tremors.
At this time, the fourfold assembly are all joyful,
their bodies and minds feeling delight,
experiencing what has never been before.
The light from the white hair-mark, illuminates the east,
eighteen thousand lands, all gleaming like gold,
from the Avīci Hell below,
up to the top of existence.
In all those worlds,
the beings of the six paths,
their destinations of birth and death,
their karmic causes, good and evil,
the retribution they receive, fine and coarse,
all are visible therein.
Moreover, Buddhas are seen,
holy lords and lions among teachers,
expounding the sūtras,
subtle and supreme.
Their voices are pure,
uttering gentle tones,
teaching many bodhisattvas,
countless billions,
with deep and wondrous Brahma sounds,
causing beings to delight in hearing.
In each world,
they preach the true Dharma, by various causes and conditions.
By countless parables, they illumine the Buddha-Dharma,
inspiring beings to realization.
If someone is suffering, dismayed by aging, sickness, and death,
he teaches them nirvāṇa to end all suffering.
If someone has good fortune,
once made offerings to the Buddha,
and seeks the superior Dharma,
he teaches them the path of pratyekabuddha.
If there is a Buddha’s child,
who cultivates various practices,
seeking unsurpassed wisdom,
he teaches them the pure path.
Wénshūshīlì!
As I dwell here,
I see and hear these things, and hundreds of thousands of others,
so many as these,
which I will now briefly speak.
I saw that land,
innumerable as the sands of the Héng river in bodhisattvas,
with all kinds of causes and conditions,
aspiring to the Buddha path.
Some practice giving,
gold, silver, coral,
pearls, maṇi gems,
chēqí agate, horse-brain agate,
vajra and various treasures,
servants, chariots,
carriages adorned with jewels,
offered joyfully.
They dedicate these toward Buddhahood,
wishing to obtain this vehicle,
the foremost in the three realms,
praised by all Buddhas.
There are also bodhisattvas,
who offer chariots drawn by four horses,
with rails and floral canopies,
decorated with ornaments.
Again, I saw bodhisattvas
who give their own flesh, hands, and feet,
as well as their wives and children,
seeking the unsurpassed Way.
And I also saw bodhisattvas,
their heads, eyes, bodies—delighting in giving them,
seeking Buddha’s wisdom.
Wénshūshīlì!
I saw all the kings going to pay homage to the Buddha,
ask about the unsurpassed Way,
and immediately abandon their pleasant lands, palaces, and ministers,
shave their beards and hair,
and put on Dharma robes.
Or seeing bodhisattvas become bhikṣus,
living alone in quietude,
delighting in reciting the scriptures.
Again, I saw bodhisattvas, valiant and diligent,
entering deep mountains,
contemplating the Buddha Way.
And I saw those who abandoned desire,
always dwelling in solitude,
deeply cultivating meditation,
attaining the five supernatural powers.
Again, I saw bodhisattvas,
peaceful in meditation, palms joined,
using countless verses,
to praise the Kings of Dharma.
Again, I saw bodhisattvas,
profound in wisdom, firm in resolve,
able to question the Buddhas,
hear and fully uphold their teachings.
I also saw the Buddha’s children,
endowed with concentration and wisdom,
using countless similes
to teach the Dharma to the multitude.
They delight in expounding the Dharma,
transform bodhisattvas,
break the armies of Māra,
and beat the Dharma drum.
Again, I saw bodhisattvas,
serene and silent,
revered by devas and dragons,
but not regarding this as a joy.
Again, I saw bodhisattvas,
dwelling in forests emitting light,
relieving the sufferings of hell,
leading beings onto the Buddha Way.
Again, I saw the Buddha’s children,
who had never slept,
walking through the forests,
earnestly seeking the Buddha Way.
Again, I saw those who upheld the precepts,
their deportment flawless,
pure as a precious gem,
seeking the Buddha Way.
Again, I saw the Buddha’s children,
abiding in the power of forbearance,
even when arrogant people abused or struck them,
all could endure,
seeking the Buddha Way.
Again, I saw bodhisattvas,
leaving behind all frivolous laughter,
and foolish companions,
drawing close to the wise,
with single-mindedness eliminating confusion,
gathering their thoughts in the mountains and forests,
for hundreds of millions of years,
seeking the Buddha Way.
Some bodhisattvas, with food and drink, a hundred kinds of soups and medicines,
offered to the Buddha and the saṅgha.
Famed and fine garments whose value is in the millions,
or priceless robes,
offered to the Buddha and the saṅgha.
Myriad varieties,
sandalwood adorned halls, splendid bedding,
offered to the Buddha and the saṅgha.
Pure and beautiful groves,
abundant with flowers and fruits, flowing springs and bathing pools,
offered to the Buddha and the saṅgha.
Such offerings as these,
all kinds of subtle wonders,
joyfully made without stint,
seeking the unsurpassed Way.
There are also bodhisattvas,
who preach the Dharma of quiescence,
teaching innumerable beings,
or those bodhisattvas
who contemplate the nature of all dharmas,
as empty as space.
Seeing no duality of phenomena,
again I saw the Buddha’s children,
whose minds were attached to nothing,
with this wondrous wisdom
seeking the unsurpassed Way.
Wénshūshīlì!
There are also bodhisattvas,
who, after the Buddha’s passing,
make offerings to relics.
Again, I saw the Buddha’s children,
building various stupas and shrines,
innumerable as the sands of the Héng,
splendidly adorning their lands;
precious towers, lofty and wondrous,
five thousand yojanas in height,
with equal length and breadth,
two thousand yojanas each.
Each and every stupa and shrine
has a thousand banners,
pearls entwined with draped canopies,
treasure bells sounding in harmony.
All heavenly beings, dragons, and gods,
humans and nonhumans,
with fragrant flowers and musical performances,
constantly make offerings.
Wénshūshīlì!
All the Buddha’s children,
for the sake of making offerings to relics,
splendidly adorn stupas and shrines,
while the lands themselves become
extraordinary and exquisite,
like the king of trees in the heavens,
whose blossoms open and spread forth.
The Buddha emits a single ray of light;
myself and the whole assembly
see these lands,
all with their own marvels.
The miraculous power and wisdom of all the Buddhas
are rare and wonderful;
emitting a pure ray,
it illuminates countless lands.
We all gaze in awe
at what has never happened before.
Buddha’s child Wénshū!
May you resolve all doubts.
The fourfold assembly eagerly looks up,
gazing at the venerable one and myself.
World-Honored One, for what reason
do you emit this light?
Please, child of the Buddha, respond
to resolve these doubts and bring us joy.
What benefit or
meaning lies behind the manifestation of this light?
Does the Buddha, seated at the site of enlightenment, having attained wondrous Dharma, wish now to expound it?
Or is he to give a prediction?
To display the lands of the Buddhas,
adorned with jewels and purity,
and for us to see all the Buddhas—
all this is no small matter.
Wénshū, you should know
the fourfold assembly, dragons, gods,
are all gazing at the venerable one
to know what will be said.”
At that time, Wénshūshīlì addressed Mílè bodhisattva-mahāsattva and the great beings,
and all the worthy men: “As I have considered, today the Buddha, the World-Honored One
wishes to proclaim the Great Dharma,
to rain down the great Dharma rain,
to blow the great Dharma conch,
to strike the great Dharma drum,
to expound the great meaning of the Dharma.
All you worthy ones:
In the past, among former Buddhas, I have seen this auspicious sign—
after emitting such a light, he immediately proclaimed the Great Dharma. After emitting such a light, he immediately proclaimed the Great Dharma.
Therefore, you should know
that now when the Buddha displays this light, it is likewise so,
wishing for sentient beings to hear and know the Dharma that is difficult to believe for all the world,
thus, he displays this auspicious sign.
“O worthy men!
Immeasurably, boundlessly, inconceivably many kalpas ago,
then there was a Buddha,
named Rìyuè Dēngmíng Tathāgata,
Worthy of Offerings, Perfectly Awakened,
Perfect in Wisdom and Conduct, Well-Gone, World-Knower, Supreme One,
Tamer of Heroes, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, World-Honored One,
who expounded the right Dharma,
excellent at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end,
profound in meaning and far-reaching,
subtle and skillful in expression,
pure and unadulterated,
completely endowed with the marks of pure Brahma conduct.
For those who seek the fame of being heard,
he expounds the Dharma of the Four Noble Truths,
to deliver them from birth, aging, sickness, and death, leading ultimately to Nièpán;
for those who seek to become Pratyekabuddhas,
he expounds the Dharma of the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination;
for all Bodhisattvas,
he expounds the Six Pāramitās,
enabling them to attain Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi and realize the wisdom of all modes.
"Then again there was a Buddha,
also named Rìyuè Dēngmíng,
and next there was another Buddha,
also named Rìyuè Dēngmíng.
In this way, for twenty thousand Buddhas,
their names all used the same word,
called Rìyuè Dēngmíng,
and furthermore, they all shared the same family name,
the surname Pōluóduò.
O Mílè, know that
both the first and the last Buddha all had the same name,
that is, Rìyuè Dēngmíng,
and fully possessed the Ten Epithets.
The Dharma they could preach was excellent at the beginning, middle, and end."
The last Buddha, before he left household life,
had eight princely sons:
the first was named Yǒuyì,
the second Shànyì,
the third Wúliàngyì,
the fourth Bǎoyì,
the fifth Zēngyì,
the sixth Chúyíyì,
the seventh Xiàngyì,
the eighth Fǎyì.
These eight princes had majestic virtue and freedom,
each ruling over four great continents.
These princes,
on hearing their father had left home and attained Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi,
all renounced their royal positions and likewise left home,
aroused the intention for the Mahāyāna,
constantly practiced the Brahma conduct,
all became Dharma teachers,
and had already, before a myriad Buddhas, planted numerous wholesome roots.
At that time, the Buddha Rìyuè Dēngmíng
preached the Mahāyāna sūtra
called “Immeasurable Meanings,” teaching the laws for Bodhisattvas,
which the Buddha protects and remembers.
After finishing preaching this sūtra,
he immediately, amid the great assembly, sat cross-legged,
and entered the Samādhi of the Place of Immeasurable Meanings,
body and mind unmoving.
Then, heavenly mandarava flowers
and great mandarava flowers,
manjushaka flowers,
and great manjushaka flowers
rained down, scattering upon the Buddha and all the great assembly.
Throughout the world of the Buddha, there were six kinds of tremors.
At that time, in the assembly, there were bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās,
devas, dragons, yaksas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans and non-humans,
as well as local kings and wheel-turning sage kings;
these great multitudes experienced what they had never experienced before,
joyfully put their palms together, and gazed single-mindedly at the Buddha.
At that time, the Tathāgata emitted a ray of white hair-light from between his brows,
illuminating eighteen thousand Buddha-lands to the east,
pervading them all without exception,
just like the Buddha-lands we now see.
O Mílè, you should know,
in that assembly at that time, there were two billion Bodhisattvas
eager to hear the Dharma.
These Bodhisattvas, seeing this bright light illuminating all the Buddha-lands,
experienced what they had never experienced before,
wishing to know the cause of this light.
Then there was a Bodhisattva,
named Miàoguāng,
with eight hundred disciples.
At that time, the Buddha Rìyuè Dēngmíng arose from samādhi
and, for the sake of the Bodhisattva Miàoguāng,
preached the Mahāyāna sūtra
called the “Sūtra of the Lotus Flower of the Wonderful Dharma,” teaching the Bodhisattva Dharma,
which is protected and remembered by the Buddha.
For sixty minor kalpas, he did not rise from his seat.
At that time, the listeners in the assembly also sat in one place,
for sixty minor kalpas, their bodies and minds unmoved,
listening to the Buddha's words, but felt it lasted the time of a meal.
In that assembly,
not one person, in body or mind, gave rise to fatigue or weariness.
"After the Buddha Rìyuè Dēngmíng had preached this sūtra for sixty minor kalpas,
he proclaimed to Brahmins, Māras, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, as well as devas, humans, and asuras in the assembly, these words:
'Today, in the middle of the night, the Tathāgata will enter Nirvāṇa without remainder.'
Then there was a Bodhisattva,
named Dézàng,
and the Buddha Rìyuè Dēngmíng
accordingly gave him a prediction,
and said to the bhikṣus:
'This Bodhisattva Dézàng
shall next become a Buddha
by the name of Jìngshēn Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyak-saṃbuddha.'
When the Buddha had finished giving the prediction,
he passed into Nirvāṇa without remainder in the middle of the night.
After the Buddha’s extinction,
the Bodhisattva Miàoguāng upheld the Sūtra of the Lotus Flower of the Wonderful Dharma
and for eighty minor kalpas expounded it for others.
The eight sons of the Buddha Rìyuè Dēngmíng all took Miàoguāng as their teacher,
Miàoguāng teaching and transforming them
so that they firmly aspired to Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.
These princes,
after making offerings to countless hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddhas,
all attained the path of Buddhahood.
The last to attain Buddhahood among them was named Rándēng.
Of the eight hundred disciples, there was one named Qiúmíng,
who was greedy for profit and offerings;
although he recited and memorized many sūtras, he lacked deep understanding,
and often forgot and lost much;
thus he was called Qiúmíng.
Yet, because of the merit of planting wholesome roots as causes and conditions,
he was able to encounter countless hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddhas,
making offerings, revering, honoring, and praising them.
O Mílè, you should know,
that Bodhisattva Miàoguāng at that time—
was he anyone else? It was my very self!
As for Qiúmíng Bodhisattva, that is your very self.
Now seeing the present auspicious signs is no different from the past;
therefore consider: 'Today, the Tathāgata will expound the Mahāyāna sūtra,
the Sūtra of the Lotus Flower of the Wonderful Dharma,
teaching the Bodhisattva Dharma,
which is protected and remembered by the Buddha.'"
At that time, Wénshūshīlì,
amid the great assembly, wished again to declare this meaning,
and so spoke in verse:
I recall the past ages,
measureless, countless kalpas;
there was a Buddha, honored among people,
named Rìyuè Dēngmíng.
The World-Honored One expounded the Dharma,
delivering countless sentient beings,
innumerable millions of Bodhisattvas,
leading them to enter the wisdom of the Buddha.
Before he left household life, the Buddha had eight princely sons;
seeing the Great Sage leave home,
they likewise practiced the Brahma conduct.
At that time the Buddha preached the Mahāyāna,
the sūtra called “Immeasurable Meanings,”
and, among the great assembly,
fully explained and differentiated it.
After the Buddha preached this sūtra,
immediately, upon the Dharma seat,
he sat cross-legged in samādhi,
called the Samādhi of Immeasurable Meanings.
Heavenly mandarava flowers rained down,
heavenly drums sounded of themselves,
all gods, dragons, ghosts, and spirits,
made offerings to the Honor among Humans.
All the Buddha-lands
were immediately shaken in great ways;
the Buddha emitted light from between his brows,
revealing rare and marvelous events.
This light shone to the east,
eighteen thousand Buddha-lands,
showing all sentient beings
the places of their karmic retribution in the cycle of birth and death.
Some saw Buddha-lands
adorned with various jewels,
lapis and crystal in color;
this was due to the illumination of Buddha’s light.
They also saw gods and humans,
dragons, spirits, yaksas,
gandharvas and kinnaras,
each making offerings to their Buddha.
They also saw all Tathāgatas,
naturally achieving Buddhahood,
their bodies colored like golden mountains,
noble and most wondrous.
As pictures of true gold appear
within pure crystal,
so the World-Honored One, amidst the great assembly,
expounded the profound Dharma.
In each Buddha-land,
the hearer-disciples were innumerable;
by the light of the Buddha
all could see those great assemblies.
Some bhikṣus
dwelt in mountains and forests,
striving diligently to uphold pure precepts,
as if protecting a bright jewel.
They also saw Bodhisattvas
practicing giving, patience, and the rest,
their numbers like the sands of the Ganges,
all due to the illumination of Buddha’s light.
They also saw Bodhisattvas
entered deeply into dhyāna,
with bodies and minds calm and unmoving,
seeking the highest path.
They also saw Bodhisattvas
who knew the marks of the extinction of all Dharmas,
each in their own land,
expounding Dharma and seeking Buddhahood.
At that time, the fourfold assembly,
on seeing Rìyuè Dēng Buddha,
manifest great divine powers,
all rejoiced in their hearts
and each asked the others:
“What is the cause and condition of this event?”
The Honored One, revered by devas and humans,
had just risen from samādhi,
and praised Miàoguāng Bodhisattva:
“You are the eye of the world,
the object of all faith and refuge;
you are able to uphold the Dharma treasury,
as I have taught the Dharma,
only you can truly understand and realize it.”
After the World-Honored One praised him,
he made Miàoguāng joyful
and proceeded to preach the Lotus Sūtra.
For sixty minor kalpas
he did not rise from that seat.
The supreme and wondrous Dharma he taught,
was entirely received and upheld by Master-of-the-Dharma Miàoguāng.
Having spoken this Lotus Sūtra,
and after making the assembly rejoice,
on that very same day,
he addressed the assembly of devas and humans:
“The true aspect of all dharmas,
I have now preached for you;
tonight at midnight,
I shall enter parinirvāṇa.
You must wholeheartedly apply yourselves with diligence,
and cast aside all negligence.
It is most difficult to encounter buddhas;
in billions of kalpas, one may meet just once.”
All the sons of the World-Honored One,
on hearing the Buddha would enter parinirvāṇa,
each harbored grief and anguish:
“How quickly the Buddha shall pass!
The holy sovereign, king of the Dharma,
comforted the immeasurable multitude:
‘At the time of my parinirvāṇa,
do not sorrow or fear;
this is Dézàng Bodhisattva,
who, regarding the flawless true aspect, has already thoroughly comprehended it in mind.
Next, he shall become a buddha,
with the name Jìngshēn,
and will also liberate innumerable beings.’”
That night, the Buddha entered parinirvāṇa,
like a fire going out when its fuel is exhausted.
His relics were distributed,
and countless stupas were erected.
The bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs,
as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
redoubled their efforts in diligence,
seeking the unsurpassed path.
As for Master-of-the-Dharma Miàoguāng,
he upheld the Buddha’s Dharma treasury
for eighty minor kalpas,
and extensively proclaimed the Lotus Sūtra.
These eight princes,
were taught and transformed by Miàoguāng,
became steadfast in the unsurpassed path,
and would see countless buddhas in the future.
After making offerings to those buddhas,
they would follow and practice the Great Way,
in succession attaining buddhahood,
and passing on one after another the prophecy of buddhahood.
Finally, among the devas,
one was named Rándēng Buddha,
the teacher of all transcendents,
who liberated immeasurable multitudes.
This Master-of-the-Dharma Miàoguāng
at that time had a disciple,
whose mind was always lazy and negligent,
greedy for fame and profit,
seeking fame and profit insatiably,
often visiting noble households,
abandoning his recitations,
neglecting and failing to master them.
For this reason,
he was called Qiúmíng (“Seeker of Fame”).
He too performed numerous good deeds,
and obtained the vision of countless buddhas,
making offerings to all buddhas,
practicing the Great Way in accord,
perfecting the six pāramitās.
Now he has met Shì Shīzǐ (Śākyamuni).
In the future, he will become a buddha himself,
with the name Mílè,
widely liberating all living beings,
innumerable in number.
After that buddha’s parinirvāṇa,
the one who was negligent—this is you;
as for Master-of-the-Dharma Miàoguāng,
now I am that very person.
I saw Dēngmíng Buddha,
whose former auspicious light was just like this,
and by this, I know that today’s buddha
wishes to preach the Lotus Sūtra.
The present signs resemble the former auspicious ones;
these are the expedient means of all the buddhas.
Now the Buddha emits a light,
to help illuminate the true aspect.
Now all people should know,
join your palms and wait with focused mind,
the Buddha will rain down the rain of Dharma,
to fully satisfy the seekers of the Way.
For those seeking the three vehicles,
if there is any doubt or regret,
the Buddha will eliminate and sever it,
so that nothing shall remain.”
At that time, the World-Honored One calmly rose from samādhi
and addressed Shèlìfú:
“The wisdom of the buddhas is exceedingly profound and immeasurable;
its gateway is hard to understand and hard to enter;
none of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas can comprehend it.
Why is this?
The Buddha has personally encountered myriads of buddhas—hundreds of thousands, millions, billions, countless—and
has completely cultivated the infinite Dharma paths of all buddhas;
with vigor and diligence,
his name universally known,
he has accomplished profound, unprecedented Dharma;
the intent and purpose of what he preaches according to circumstances is difficult to comprehend.
Shèlìfú!
Since I attained buddhahood,
through various causes and various analogies, I have extensively taught and expounded
countless skillful means to guide living beings,
enabling them to be free from all attachments.
Why is this?
The Tathāgata’s skillful means and insight into the Dharma pāramitā are fully perfected.
Shèlìfú!
The Tathāgata’s insight and vision are vast and profound,
immeasurable and unobstructed; powers, fearlessness,
meditative concentration, liberation, and samādhis—
he penetrates them without limit.
He accomplishes all unprecedented Dharmas.
Shèlìfú!
The Tathāgata can discriminate in countless ways and skillfully explain all dharmas,
his words are gentle and pleasing, delighting all hearts.
Shèlìfú!
To put it in brief,
the infinite, boundless, unprecedented Dharmas have all been accomplished by the Buddha.”
“Stop, Shèlìfú!
There is no need to say more.
Why is this?
The Dharma reached by the Buddha is the supreme, most rare, and difficult to understand.
Only buddhas with buddhas can thoroughly fathom the true aspect of all dharmas:
namely, that all dharmas are just such in aspect, such in nature, such in substance, such in power, such in function, such in cause,
such in condition, such in effect, such in retribution, such in the ultimate beginning and end.”
At that time, the World-Honored One,
wishing to reiterate this meaning,
spoke verses, saying:
“The hero of the world is incalculable;
all devas and humans,
all types of sentient beings,
none can know the Buddha.
The Buddha’s powers, fearlessness,
liberation, the various samādhis,
and all other Buddha Dharmas,
none can fathom them.
From originally encountering countless buddhas,
completely cultivating all the paths,
the most profound and subtle Dharma,
is hard to see and understand.
Through immeasurable billions of kalpas,
having practiced these paths,
in the place of enlightenment I attained fruition,
all this I fully know and see.
Such are these great results,
their various natures and aspects;
only I and the buddhas of the ten directions
can know these things.
This Dharma cannot be taught;
words and expressions fall silent;
all other types of living beings,
none can understand this,
except for all the bodhisattva assemblies—
those whose faith is firm and strong.
Disciples of the buddhas
who have served the buddhas,
have eliminated all their defilements,
and dwell in their final bodies—
even such as these
do not have the power to fathom it.
Suppose the world were filled
with people like Shèlìfú,
expending all their thoughts jointly to gauge,
they still could not measure the Buddha’s wisdom.
Even if all the ten directions
were filled with Śārìfú,
and other disciples,
also filling the lands of the ten directions,
and they all tried to measure and fathom,
still they could not know.
The Pratyekabuddha’s sharp wisdom,
those in their final bodies, free from outflows,
also filling the ten directions’ realms,
as numerous as bamboo groves,
if they all, with one mind,
for billions of countless kalpas,
sought to comprehend the Buddha’s true wisdom,
they could not know even a small part.
Newly-initiated Bodhisattvas,
who have made offerings to innumerable Buddhas,
clearly understanding all meanings and aims,
and able to skillfully teach the Dharma,
numerous as rice, hemp, bamboo, and reeds,
filling the worlds in the ten directions,
if with one mind and marvelous wisdom,
for Ganges-sands-numbered kalpas,
all were to ponder together,
still could not know the Buddha’s wisdom.
The non-retreating Bodhisattvas,
as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
if they all together, with one mind, sought and contemplated,
still could not know.
Again, he said to Śārìfú:
"The untainted, inconceivable,
extremely profound, subtle, and wonderful Dharma,
only I know its reality,
as do the Buddhas of the ten directions.
Śārìfú, you should know,
the words of the Buddhas do not differ;
toward the Dharma taught by the Buddhas,
you should give rise to great faith.
After the Dharma of the World Honored One has long endured,
he will, without fail, speak the truth."
He told the community of śrāvakas,
and those seeking the Pratyekabuddha vehicle:
"It is I who freed you from the bonds of suffering,
enabling you to attain Nirvāṇa."
The Buddha, by the power of skillful means,
reveals the teaching of the Three Vehicles,
for sentient beings are attached everywhere,
and he leads them forth to liberation.
At that time, among the great assembly,
were arhats, śrāvakas with all outflows ended,
such as Āròu Jiāochénrú and one thousand two hundred others,
as well as monks, nuns, upāsakas, and upāsikās who had set their minds on śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha-hood.
Each thought to himself:
"Now, the World Honored One,
why does he earnestly praise skillful means
and say: ‘The Dharma realized by the Buddha is extremely profound and hard to understand,
its meaning as expressed in words is hard to know,
not accessible to all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas’?
The Buddha spoke of a single liberation,
and we have also attained this Dharma, reaching Nirvāṇa,
but now do not know to what this meaning pertains."
At that time, Śārìfú knew the fourfold assembly was in doubt,
and he himself had not fully grasped it,
so he addressed the Buddha:
"World Honored One!
For what cause and reason do you earnestly praise the Buddhas’ supreme skillful means,
extremely profound, subtle, and hard-to-understand Dharma?
Never since long ago have I heard such words spoken by the Buddha;
now all fourfold assembly share this doubt.
We only pray the World Honored One
will expound and explain this matter. Why does the World Honored One earnestly praise the extremely profound, subtle, and hard-to-understand Dharma?"
Then, Śārìfú, wanting to reiterate the meaning,
spoke in verse:
"O Sun of Wisdom, Great Holy Honored One,
you have waited long to teach this Dharma,
declaring personally to have attained
powers, fearlessness, samādhi,
dhyāna, liberation, and more,
inconceivable Dharmas.
The Dharma gained at the place of the Path,
none have been able to question;
your mind’s intent is hard to fathom,
nor is there one able to ask.
Without being asked, you yourself preach,
praising the path you have walked.
Wisdom is most subtle and wonderful,
what Buddhas alone attain.
The outflow-free arhats,
and those seeking Nirvāṇa,
now all have fallen into the net of doubt—
why does the Buddha speak thus?
Those seeking the Pratyekabuddha path,
monks and nuns,
gods, dragons, spirits,
and the Gandharva beings,
gaze at each other with uncertainty,
looking up at the Two-Footed Honored One,
pondering what this means,
praying the Buddha will explain it.
Among the community of śrāvakas,
the Buddha has declared me the foremost.
Yet even I, regarding wisdom,
am confused and cannot realize—
is this the ultimate Dharma?
Or is it the path he has walked?
All those born from the Buddha’s mouth,
with palms joined, look up, awaiting,
hoping to hear the subtle sound,
to be spoken now as it truly is.
All gods, dragons, and spirits,
as numerous as Ganges sands,
seekers after the Buddha path and bodhisattvas,
their number eighty thousand great ones,
also from tens of thousands of millions of countries, Cakravartin Kings have come,
with palms joined and reverent hearts,
wishing to hear the perfect path."
At that time, the Buddha told Śārìfú:
"Stop, stop! There is no need to speak further.
If I were to speak of this matter,
all the gods and humans in all the world would be shocked and doubtful."
Śārìfú again addressed the Buddha:
"World Honored One,
we only wish you would teach it,
we only wish you would teach it!
Why so?
In this assembly are innumerable hundreds of thousands of millions of asamkhyeya sentient beings,
who have seen the Buddhas,
whose faculties are keen, whose wisdom is bright and clear,
if they hear what the Buddha says, they will be able to revere and trust."
Then Śārìfú, wishing again to state the meaning,
spoke in verse:
"Dharma King, Supreme Honored One,
we only wish you would speak, and do not be concerned.
In this assembly of countless beings,
are those able to revere and believe."
The Buddha again stopped Śārìfú:
"If I were to speak this matter,
all the gods, humans, and Āxiūluó in every world,
would all be astonished and doubtful;
prideful monks would fall into a great pit."
At that time, the World Honored One again spoke in verse:
"Stop, stop, there is no need to speak,
my Dharma is wondrous and hard to conceive.
All those with increasing pride,
if they hear, will surely not respect or believe."
Again, Śārìfú addressed the Buddha:
"World Honored One!
We only wish you would teach it,
we only wish you would teach it!
In this current assembly,
those like myself, numbering hundreds of thousands of millions,
life after life have already received the Buddha’s guidance.
Such persons are sure to revere and trust,
and gain peace and many benefits over long nights."
Then Śārìfú, wishing again to state the meaning,
spoke in verse:
"Supreme Two-Footed Honored One,
please teach the foremost Dharma.
I am the Buddha’s eldest son,
only wish you will distinguish and explain.
In this assembly of numberless beings,
are those able to trust and receive this Dharma.
The Buddha has in life after life
guided and transformed such as these.
All, with one heart and joined palms,
wish to hear the Buddha’s words.
We, numbering twelve hundred,
together with others seeking Buddhahood,
for the sake of these multitudes,
only wish you will distinguish and explain to us.
Should they hear this Dharma,
great joy will arise."
Then the World Honored One said to Śārìfú:
"You have earnestly requested three times,
how could I not speak?
Listen now attentively, and ponder it well,
I shall now distinguish and explain it for you."
When he had spoken these words,
in the assembly were bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās—five thousand in all,
who immediately arose from their seats,
paid homage to the Buddha, and withdrew.
And why was this?
These people had deep-rooted offenses and increasing pride,
claiming attainment when they had not attained,
claiming realization when they had not realized;
because of such faults,
they did not remain.
The World-honored One remained silent and did not intervene.
At that time, the Buddha said to Shèlìfú:
“Now in this assembly, there are no more branches and leaves;
only pure and genuine substance remains.
Shèlìfú!
It is indeed good that those arrogant people have withdrawn.
Now you should listen well, for I will teach you.”
Shèlìfú said:
“Indeed, World-honored One!
I wish gladly to hear.”
The Buddha said to Shèlìfú:
“Such a marvelous Dharma is only spoken by the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas,
like the udumbara flower, which appears but once in a long while.
Shèlìfú!
You all should believe what the Buddha says, his words are not false.
Shèlìfú!
The Buddhas expound the Dharma as appropriate to circumstances, but their intent and meaning are hard to understand.
Why is this?
Using countless skillful means, various causes and conditions, parables, and words, I expound the various teachings.
This Dharma cannot be understood by thought and discrimination;
only all Buddhas can know it.
Why is this?
The Buddhas, World-honored Ones,
appear in the world for one great cause only.
Shèlìfú!
What does it mean that the Buddhas, World-honored Ones, appear in the world for one great cause only?
The Buddhas, World-honored Ones,
appear in the world in order to open the Buddha’s knowledge and vision for sentient beings so that they may attain purity;
for this reason, they appear in the world;
in order to show the Buddha’s knowledge and vision to sentient beings,
for this reason, they appear in the world;
in order to awaken sentient beings to the Buddha’s knowledge and vision,
for this reason, they appear in the world;
in order to lead sentient beings to enter the path of the Buddha’s knowledge and vision,
for this reason, they appear in the world.
Shèlìfú!
This, then, is why the Buddhas appear in the world for one great cause.”
The Buddha said to Shèlìfú:
“The Buddhas, the Tathāgatas,
teach only Bodhisattvas;
all they do is always for one purpose alone,
only to show and awaken the Buddha’s knowledge and vision to sentient beings.”
Shèlìfú!
It is only for the sake of the One Buddha Vehicle that the Tathāgata teaches the Dharma to sentient beings,
there is no other vehicle, neither a second nor a third.
Shèlìfú!
The Dharma of all Buddhas in the ten directions is likewise.
Shèlìfú!
The Buddhas of the past, with countless skillful means, various causes and conditions, parables, and words,
expounded the Dharma for sentient beings;
all of these teachings were for the sake of the One Buddha Vehicle only.
Those sentient beings who heard the Dharma from those Buddhas,
ultimately all attained the wisdom of all modes.
Shèlìfú!
The Buddhas of the future who will appear in the world
will likewise, with countless skillful means, various causes and conditions, parables, and words,
expound the Dharma for sentient beings;
all of these teachings are for the sake of the One Buddha Vehicle only.
Those sentient beings who hear the Dharma from those Buddhas
will ultimately all attain the wisdom of all modes.
Shèlìfú!
Now, in immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions, the Buddhas, World-honored Ones,
bring abundant benefit and happiness to sentient beings.
These Buddhas, too, with countless skillful means, various causes and conditions, parables, and words,
expound the Dharma for sentient beings;
all these teachings are for the sake of the One Buddha Vehicle only.
Those sentient beings who hear the Dharma from those Buddhas
will ultimately all attain the wisdom of all modes.
Shèlìfú!
These Buddhas teach only Bodhisattvas;
they wish to show sentient beings the Buddha’s knowledge and vision,
wish to awaken sentient beings to the Buddha’s knowledge and vision,
wish to lead sentient beings to enter the Buddha’s knowledge and vision.
Shèlìfú!
Now I am likewise:
I know all sentient beings have various desires,
are deeply attached at heart,
and according to their inherent nature,
using various causes and conditions, parables, and words, and through the power of skillful means, I expound the Dharma for them.
Shèlìfú!
All of this is for the sake of obtaining the One Buddha Vehicle, the wisdom of all modes.
Shèlìfú!
In the worlds of the ten directions, not even a second vehicle exists—
how much less a third.
Shèlìfú!
The Buddhas appear in this evil world of five defilements,
namely, the defilement of the kalpa, defilement of views, defilement of afflictions, defilement of sentient beings, and defilement of life span.
Thus it is, Shèlìfú!
In the time of disturbances caused by the defilement of the kalpa,
sentient beings are burdened heavily by defilements;
avarice, jealousy, accomplishing all unwholesome roots,
the Buddhas, through the power of skillful means,
teach the One Buddha Vehicle as if divided into three.
Shèlìfú!
If my disciples claim to be Arhats or Pratyekabuddhas,
yet do not hear or know that the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, teach only Bodhisattvas,
they are not disciples of the Buddha,
not Arhats, not Pratyekabuddhas.
“Moreover, Shèlìfú!
If there are those bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs,
who claim to have attained arhatship,
and think they are in their last body and have reached final Nirvāṇa,
and no longer seek Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi,
then know that these are all arrogant people.
Why is this?
If there is a bhikṣu who truly has attained arhatship,
it is impossible for him not to believe this teaching.
Except only after the extinction of the Buddha, when there is no present Buddha,
why is this?
After the extinction of the Buddha,
it is hard to find someone who receives, holds, recites, and explains such sūtras.
But if he encounters another Buddha,
he will at once attain decisive understanding of this teaching.
Shèlìfú!
You all should, with single-minded faith and understanding, uphold the words of the Buddha.
The Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, do not speak falsely;
there is no other vehicle—only the One Buddha Vehicle.”
At that time, the World-honored One,
desiring to further clarify this meaning,
spoke in verse:
Bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs,
harboring arrogance and pride,
upāsakas with pride,
upāsikās lacking faith,
these fourfold assemblies,
numbering five thousand,
not seeing their own faults,
with breaches in their precepts,
cherishing and covering their flaws,
with shallow wisdom have departed—
the dregs and husks among the assembly,
who have left because of the Buddha’s spiritual power.
These people have scant merit and virtue,
and are not fit to receive this Dharma.
This assembly has no more branches and leaves;
only truly genuine ones remain.
Shèlìfú, listen well!
The Dharma realized by all the Buddhas,
with boundless power of skillful means,
is expounded for sentient beings.
Whatever sentient beings think in their hearts,
the many paths they practice,
the myriad desires and natures,
the good and evil deeds of past lives—
the Buddha knows them all,
and by various causes and conditions, parables,
words and skillful means,
he brings joy to everyone.
He may preach sūtras,
gāthās, jātakas,
previous lives, unheard-of stories,
also talks on causes and conditions,
parables and udānas,
and upadeśas.
Those of dull faculties who delight in lesser teachings,
attached to birth and death,
meeting innumerable Buddhas,
do not practice the profound and subtle path,
disturbed by many sufferings—
it is for them that Nirvāṇa is taught.
Yet, I employ these skillful means
to cause them to enter the Buddha’s wisdom;
never have I said you
will ultimately become Buddhas.
Why did I not say so?
Because the time had not come.
Now truly is the right time,
I will assuredly teach the Great Vehicle.
Of the nine divisions of my Dharma,
all are spoken in accord with sentient beings
so that they may enter the Great Vehicle at the root;
therefore, I preach this sūtra.
If there are Buddha-sons with pure minds,
gentle and of keen faculties,
who, before innumerable Buddhas,
practice the profound and subtle path,
for these Buddha-sons
I speak the Great Vehicle Sūtra.
I assure such persons
that in a future life they will become Buddhas—
because of their deep mindfulness of the Buddha,
maintaining pure precepts.
Hearing that they will become Buddhas,
great joy fills their bodies.
Knowing their intentions,
the Buddha preaches the Great Vehicle for them.
Whether Śrāvakas or Bodhisattvas,
whoever hears what I teach,
even just one verse,
will unquestionably attain Buddhahood.
Among the Buddha-lands of the ten directions,
there is only the Dharma of the One Vehicle;
there is no second or third.
Except for when the Buddhas speak expediently,
using provisional names
to guide sentient beings,
and to expound the wisdom of the Buddha.
It is for this reason that the Buddhas appear in the world.
Only this one matter is true;
the other two are not real.
Never by means of the Lesser Vehicle
do they save and ferry across sentient beings.
The Buddha himself abides in the Great Vehicle,
in accordance with the Dharma he has attained,
with the power of concentration and wisdom as his adornment,
and thus saves sentient beings.
He realizes for himself the unsurpassed path,
the Law of Equality of the Great Vehicle.
If by means of the Lesser Vehicle he were to teach,
even so much as to a single person,
then I would have fallen into stinginess and greed,
and this matter would not be permissible.
If anyone has faith and takes refuge in the Buddha,
the Tathāgata does not deceive or mislead,
nor has any mind of avarice or jealousy,
having eliminated evil among all dharmas.
Therefore, among the ten directions,
the Buddha alone is without fear.
With the adornment of the marks on my body,
my radiance shines upon the world.
Esteemed by countless multitudes,
I expound the seal of true suchness.
Shèlìfú, you should know:
I originally established a vow,
wishing to have all beings
be equal to me without distinction.
As I previously vowed,
now it has been fulfilled,
and I transform all sentient beings,
causing all to enter the Buddha Way.
Whenever I encounter sentient beings,
I thoroughly teach them the Buddha Way;
the unwise get confused,
deluded and do not accept my teaching.
I know that these sentient beings have never cultivated the roots of goodness,
are firmly attached to the five desires,
awakening afflictions through their ignorant attachment.
Because of causes and conditions of desires,
they fall into the three evil paths,
revolving within the six realms,
suffering all kinds of pains and poison,
tiny forms within the wombs they receive,
and in every lifetime they continually increase.
Those of slight virtue and little merit
are pressed on all sides by manifold sufferings,
losing themselves in the dense forest of wrong views,
such as whether being does or does not exist.
Relying on such views,
they possess all sixty-two (kinds),
deeply attached to unreal dharmas,
firmly upholding them and unable to abandon them.
With arrogance and pride,
their minds are deceitful and not genuine,
for countless kalpas
they do not hear the Buddha's name,
nor do they hear the true Dharma.
Such people are difficult to save.
Therefore, Shèlìfú!
For their sake I establish skillful means,
proclaiming various paths for the extinguishing of suffering,
and demonstrate to them Nirvāṇa.
Although I speak of Nirvāṇa,
even this is not true extinction;
all dharmas, from the very beginning,
are always characterized by self-quiescence and extinction.
The Buddha’s children, having practiced the path,
will, in the future, become Buddhas.
By the power of expedients that I possess,
I open and reveal the Dharma of the three vehicles.
All the World-Honored Ones
alike proclaim the One Vehicle path.
Now, for this great assembly,
you ought to rid yourselves of doubt and confusion;
the words of all the Buddhas do not differ:
there is only one, not two vehicles.
Throughout countless kalpas in the past,
innumerable Buddhas have entered parinirvāṇa:
hundreds of thousands of millions of kinds,
their number cannot be measured.
And all these World-Honored Ones,
through various causes and parables,
and countless expedient powers,
have expounded the marks of all dharmas.
All these World-Honored Ones
have all proclaimed the Dharma of the One Vehicle,
transforming countless sentient beings,
leading them all to enter the Buddha Way.
Again, all these great and holy lords
know all that the world—gods, humans, and the masses of living beings—
deeply desire in their hearts,
and further, by various expedient means,
assist in revealing the supreme meaning.
If there are sentient beings
who meet Buddhas of the past,
and, hearing the teaching, perform giving,
or uphold precepts, patience,
diligence, meditation, wisdom, and so on,
cultivating in various ways merit and wisdom,
then all these people
have already accomplished the Buddha Way.
After the Buddhas have entered parinirvāṇa,
if there are persons of gentle and pliant mind,
all such beings
have already accomplished the Buddha Way.
After the Buddhas have entered parinirvāṇa,
those who honor the relics
by erecting tens of millions of stūpas:
gold, silver, and beryl,
crystal, lapis-lazuli, and cornelian,
agate, moonstone, and pearls,
purified and splendidly adorned,
thus decorating all stūpas;
or those who build stone shrines
of chandana and eaglewood,
cypress and other woods,
bricks, tiles, mud, and so forth;
even if in a wild and open place,
they pile up earth to form a shrine to the Buddha;
even if children at play
gather sand to make a stūpa for the Buddha—
all such people
have already accomplished the Buddha Way.
If anyone for the sake of the Buddha
establishes various images,
carving and sculpting various forms—
all such people
have already accomplished the Buddha Way.
Whether from the seven treasures,
sandstone, red or white copper,
white tin, lead, tin,
iron, wood, or clay,
or if with glue, lacquer, or cloth,
they splendidly adorn and make Buddha images—
all such people
have already accomplished the Buddha Way.
If they paint images of the Buddha,
adorned with a hundred merits,
whether they do so themselves or have others do it—
all such people
have already accomplished the Buddha Way.
Even if children at play
use grass, wood, or a brush,
or even just a finger or a fingernail,
to draw the Buddha's image,
all such people
gradually accumulate merit,
perfecting the mind of great compassion—
all have already accomplished the Buddha Way.
They transform into bodhisattvas,
saving innumerable beings.
If anyone, toward a stūpa or shrine,
a precious image, or a painted image,
with flowers, incense, banners, and canopies,
offers respectful worship,
or has someone make music,
beating drums, blowing horns or conch shells,
flutes, pipes, lutes,
pípá, bells, and cymbals—
all these wondrous sounds
are entirely offered in veneration.
Or with a joyful heart
they sing praises to the Buddha's virtues,
even with but a single small sound—
all have already accomplished the Buddha Way.
If a person, with a distracted mind,
even offers one flower
in worship to a painted image,
they will gradually see innumerable Buddhas.
Or if someone bows in homage,
or merely joins their palms together,
even so much as raising a single hand,
or slightly bowing their head—
by offering to an image in such a way,
they will gradually see countless Buddhas,
and personally realize the unsurpassed path,
broadly saving innumerable beings,
entering nirvāṇa without residue,
like a fire extinguished when the fuel is consumed.
If anyone, with a distracted mind,
enters a stūpa or shrine
and but recites "Homage to the Buddha" once—
In the future, all the World-Honored Ones,
whose numbers are beyond measure,
these Tathāgatas and the like,
will likewise expound the Dharma by skillful means.
All the Tathāgatas,
with immeasurable skillful means,
deliver and liberate all sentient beings,
leading them to enter the Buddha’s wisdom free of outflows.
If there are any who hear this Dharma,
not one will fail to become a Buddha.
The original vows of the Buddhas are:
The Buddha-path I have practiced,
is universally to enable all sentient beings
to obtain this path equally as I have.
All future Buddhas,
even though they expound hundreds, thousands, billions,
and countless Dharma-gates,
in truth there is only one vehicle.
The World-Honored Ones with two feet,
know that the Dharma is always without fixed nature,
the seed of Buddha arises from conditions,
thus they speak of one vehicle.
This Dharma abides in its Dharma position,
the marks of the world are always abiding.
In the place of awakening, understanding is gained,
the Teacher expounds by skillful means.
Worthy of offerings by gods and humans, at present the Buddhas in the ten directions,
as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
appear in the world
for the peace and safety of sentient beings,
and likewise teach such Dharma.
Knowing the supreme quiescence and extinction,
by the power of skillful means,
even though various paths are demonstrated,
in truth it is the Buddha vehicle.
Knowing the many actions of sentient beings,
the thoughts deeply held within their hearts,
their past habits and deeds,
their desires and vigor,
and the sharpness or dullness of their faculties,
by various causes and conditions,
similes and expressive words,
the teaching is adapted accordingly with skillful means.
Now I am likewise thus,
for the peace and safety of sentient beings,
by means of various Dharma-gates,
I proclaim and reveal the Buddha-path.
By the power of my wisdom,
I know the nature and desires of sentient beings,
and use skillful means to teach the various Dharmas,
causing all to obtain joy.
Śāriputra, you should know!
With the Buddha-eye, I behold
the beings of the six destinies,
poor, lacking blessings and wisdom,
entering the perilous path of birth and death,
continuing suffering without end,
deeply attached to the five desires,
like the yak loving its tail,
blinded by greed and craving,
blind and in darkness, they see nothing.
They do not seek the great power of the Buddha,
nor the Dharma that ends suffering,
deeply entering into various wrong views,
using suffering in hope of abandoning suffering.
For these sentient beings' sake,
great compassion arises within me.
When I first sat upon the place of awakening,
gazing at the tree and walking around it,
for twenty-one days,
I contemplated such matters:
The wisdom I have attained
is subtle, wondrous, and supreme.
The faculties of sentient beings are dull,
blinded by attachment to pleasure and delusion.
Beings of such kind as these,
how can they be saved?
At that time, the various Brahma-kings,
along with the deity Śakra, king of the gods,
the Four Heavenly Kings who guard the world,
Maheśvara the great self-existent lord,
and many other celestial beings,
with retinues in the hundreds of thousands and millions,
respectfully joined their palms in reverence,
and requested me to turn the wheel of Dharma.
Thereupon I thought to myself:
‘If I only praise the Buddha vehicle,
sentient beings, submerged in suffering,
would be unable to believe in this Dharma;
because of destroying faith in the Dharma,
they would fall into the three evil paths.
I would rather not teach the Dharma,
and quickly enter Nirvāṇa instead.
Then I remembered the skillful means practiced
by the Buddhas of the past;
the path I have now attained
should likewise be taught as three vehicles.’
the Buddhas in the ten directions all appeared,
and with Brahmā sounds consoled and instructed me:
‘Excellent, Śākyamuni!
The foremost of guides,
having attained this unsurpassed Dharma,
it is as all Buddhas have done,
using skillful means accordingly.
We, too, have all attained
the most marvelous, supreme Dharma;
for the various types of sentient beings,
we make distinctions and teach three vehicles.
Those with little wisdom delight in lesser teachings,
do not believe they can become Buddhas themselves;
therefore, by skillful means,
we distinguish various fruits.
Though we teach three vehicles,
it is only to guide Bodhisattvas.’
Śāriputra, you should know!
When I heard the lion-voice of the sage,
profound, pure, and subtle in sound,
I joyfully praised Námó Fó.
And I further thought:
‘I have appeared in a turbid and evil world,
as spoken by all Buddhas,
I will likewise act accordingly.’
Having contemplated these things,
I immediately proceeded to Vārāṇasī.
The aspect of Dharma’s quiescence and extinction
cannot be explained with words.
Yet, by the power of skillful means,
I taught it to the five Bhikṣus.
This is known as turning the wheel of Dharma,
and then came the teaching of Nirvāṇa,
the Arhat,
Dharma, and Saṅgha—each distinct in name.
From remote and distant kalpas in the past,
teaching and praising the Nirvāṇa Dharma,
the suffering of birth and death utterly ended,
I have always expounded it thus.
Śāriputra, you should know!
I see Buddha-children and others
whose resolve is to seek the Buddha-path, endless thousands, millions, and billions;
all with hearts of reverence,
all come to the place of the Buddha,
having previously heard from various Buddhas
the Dharma expounded through skillful means.
Thereupon I thought:
‘The reason the Tathāgata appears
is to teach Buddha-wisdom;
now is truly the time.’
Śāriputra, you should know!
Those of dull faculties and little wisdom,
attached to forms and arrogant,
are unable to believe this Dharma.
Now, I take delight and fearlessness;
among the Bodhisattvas,
setting aside skillful means,
I teach only the unsurpassed path.
When Bodhisattvas hear this Dharma,
all doubts and nets of delusion are removed;
the twelve hundred Arhats
shall also all become Buddhas.
As the Buddhas of the three times
have observed the proper manner of expounding Dharma,
so do I now as well
teach the undifferentiated Dharma.
For Buddhas to arise in the world
is exceedingly rare and difficult to encounter;
and even when they do appear in the world,
to teach this Dharma is again difficult.
For immeasurable, countless kalpas,
to hear this Dharma is also difficult;
to have the ability to listen to this Dharma,
such a person is also rare.
It is like an udumbara flower,
which all love and delight in,
rare among gods and humans,
which appears only occasionally. Rejoicing and praising upon hearing the Dharma,
even to utter but a single word,
is to have made offerings
to all the Buddhas of the three times.
Such a person is exceedingly rare,
even rarer than the udumbara flower.
All of you, do not harbor doubt;
I, as King of the Dharma,
universally admonish the great assembly:
Only with the one vehicle path
do I teach and transform all Bodhisattvas,
with no Śrāvaka disciples.
You, Śāriputra,
Śrāvakas and Bodhisattvas,
should all know this wondrous Dharma!
The Secret Essentials of All Buddhas.
In the evil world of the Five Turbidities,
people only delight in and cling to various desires;
beings such as these
ultimately do not seek the Buddha path.
In the coming age, evil people
who hear the Buddha teach the One Vehicle
will become confused and refuse to believe or accept it;
they will break the Dharma and fall into evil destinies.
Those with shame and purity,
whose resolve seeks the Buddha path—
for such as these,
one should widely praise the path of the One Vehicle.
Shèlìfú, know this!
Such is the Dharma of all Buddhas:
by countless upāya,
adapting as appropriate, they expound the Dharma;
those who do not study or practice
cannot comprehend this.
Since you already know
that Buddhas are teachers of the world,
adept in adapting upāya to circumstances,
may you have no more doubts;
let your heart give rise to great joy,
and know for yourself that you will become a Buddha.
The Lotus Sūtra of Wondrous Dharma, Part One
The Lotus Sūtra of Wondrous Dharma, Scroll Two
Translated by Tripiṭaka Master
Kumārajīva of Guīcí Kingdom, Later Qin, by Imperial Command
At that time, Shèlìfú leaped for joy
and immediately rose with palms joined, gazing upon the honored countenance
and said to the Buddha:
“Now, having heard this Dharma sound from the World-Honored One,
my heart is fervently thrilled; such has never been experienced before.
Why is this?
In the past, when I heard the Buddha expound such Dharma,
I saw bodhisattvas receive prediction of buddhahood,
yet we were not included in these matters;
I felt deeply distressed, deprived of the Tathāgata’s boundless knowledge and vision.
World-Honored One!
I have often dwelt alone beneath forests and trees,
whether sitting or walking,
constantly reflecting:
‘We have all entered the nature of the Dharma;
why has the Tathāgata, by means of the Small Vehicle, caused us to be saved and liberated?
This is our fault, not the World-Honored One’s.
Why?
If people like us, by speaking of the cause, could accomplish Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi,
it must surely be through the Great Vehicle that we are to be liberated.
Yet we did not understand the upāya and the teachings adapted to circumstance;
upon first hearing the Buddha’s Dharma, we immediately believed, accepted, pondered, and attained realization.’
World-Honored One!
All this time, from morning to night, I constantly reproached myself,
but now I have heard from the Buddha unprecedented Dharma,
all doubts and regrets severed;
my body and mind are at ease, joyfully attaining peace.
Only today do I know I am truly a son of the Buddha,
born from the Buddha’s mouth, transformed by the Dharma,
having gained a share in the Buddha Dharma.”
At that time, Shèlìfú
wished to restate this meaning,
and spoke in verse:
I have heard this Dharma sound,
attaining what I never had before,
my heart filled with great joy,
the net of doubt completely removed.
In times past, I received the Buddha’s teaching,
never losing the Great Vehicle;
the Buddha’s sound is exceedingly rare,
able to remove the afflictions of beings;
I have already ended my outflows,
and on hearing, grief and afflictions are removed.
I dwelled in mountain valleys,
or under forest trees,
whether sitting or walking in meditation,
constantly reflecting on this matter,
alas! deeply reproaching myself,
how could I have deceived myself?
We too are sons of the Buddha,
equally entering the dharma of no outflow,
yet we cannot, in the future,
expound the unsurpassed path.
Thirty-two golden marks,
the ten powers, and all liberations,
together in one Dharma,
yet I could not obtain these matters;
eighty subtle excellent features,
eighteen unique Buddha dharmas—
merits such as these,
yet all are lost to me.
When I paced alone,
I saw the Buddha among a great assembly,
his fame pervading the ten directions,
widely bringing benefit to beings.
Considering how I lost this benefit,
I accused myself of deception and folly.
Day and night, I constantly
reflected on this matter,
wishing to ask the World-Honored One:
“Have I lost it or not?”
I always saw the World-Honored One
praising the bodhisattvas;
thus day and night,
I measured and weighed this matter.
Now, hearing the Buddha’s voice,
expounding the Dharma as appropriate,
peerlessly free of outflows, inconceivable,
causing beings to reach the path.
Formerly, I held perverse views,
serving as master among the brāhmaṇas,
the World-Honored One, knowing my mind,
uprooted wrong views, expounding Nirvāṇa.
I have completely eliminated wrong views,
attained realization of emptiness,
then thought to myself
I had reached extinction,
but only now do I truly realize
this was not true extinction.
If one attains buddhahood,
possessing the thirty-two marks,
revered by devas, humans, and yakṣas,
along with dragons and spirits and all such beings,
only then may it be said
extinction is truly and forever complete.
The Buddha, in the great assembly,
proclaimed that I shall become a Buddha;
on hearing such Dharma sound,
all doubt and regret are eliminated.
When I first heard the Buddha’s words,
great perplexity arose in my heart,
could it be Māra becomes a Buddha,
disturbing and confusing my mind?
The Buddha, by various causes
and skillful similes, spoke,
with a mind calm as the sea;
when I heard this, the net of doubt was cut.
The Buddha spoke of bygone ages,
of buddhas, countless through extinction,
abiding in upāya,
also expounding this Dharma.
Buddhas of the present and future,
innumerable beyond measure,
also by various upāya, expound this same Dharma.
Just as today, the World-Honored One,
from birth and leaving home,
to attaining the path and turning the Dharma Wheel,
has also expounded by means of upāya.
The World-Honored One speaks the true path;
Māra has never done such a thing.
Therefore I am certain,
it is not Māra appearing as Buddha.
Because I was entangled in the net of doubt,
I believed this was the work of Māra.
But hearing the Buddha’s gentle voice,
profound, far-reaching, exceedingly subtle and wondrous,
elucidating the pure Dharma clearly—
my heart is filled with great delight,
all doubt and regret forever gone,
abiding in the wisdom of reality.
I am certain that I will become a Buddha,
honored by devas and humans,
turning the unsurpassed Dharma Wheel,
and teaching and transforming all bodhisattvas.

Then the Buddha said to Shèlìfú: “Now, among the great multitude of devas, humans, śramaṇas, and brāhmaṇas, I declare: In ages past, before twenty trillion Buddhas, for the sake of the unsurpassed path, I always taught and transformed you, and you for countless nights and days received instruction from me. It was to guide you by upāya that you were born in my Dharma. Shèlìfú, in the past I taught you to arouse the aspiration for buddhahood, but now you have forgotten it and claim to have attained extinction yourself. Now, I again wish you to recall your original vow and practice of the path; for the sake of all śrāvakas, I expound this Great Vehicle sūtra called ‘Lotus of Wondrous Dharma,’ which teaches bodhisattva conduct and is protected and upheld by Buddhas.”
Shèlìfú,
in future lives, after immeasurable and inconceivable kalpas,
you will make offerings to countless thousands of millions of Buddhas,
uphold the True Dharma,
perfect the path practiced by bodhisattvas,
and will become a Buddha

named Huáguāng Tathāgata, Arhat, Perfectly Enlightened One, Complete in Knowledge and Conduct, Well Gone, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Hero, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, World-Honored One.
The name of his country will be Lígòu;
its land will be level and pure, adorned in splendid order,
secure and full of happiness, with abundant devas and humans.
The ground will be of lapis lazuli, with eight intersecting roads;
golden cords will mark off its sides.
At each side, rows of trees of the seven treasures, ever bearing flowers and fruit.
Huáguāng Tathāgata will also teach and transform beings by means of the three vehicles.
Shèlìfú,
when that buddha appears in the world, although it will not be an evil age,
yet in accordance with his original vow, he will expound the Dharma of the three vehicles.
His kalpa will be called Great Treasure-Adornment.
Why is it called Great Treasure-Adornment?
Because in his country, bodhisattvas are considered the great treasures.
The number of these bodhisattvas will be boundless and incalculable, inconceivable;
their number is beyond calculation and simile;
none but Buddhas, with their wisdom and power, can know them.
When they walk, jeweled lotuses will support their feet.
These various Bodhisattvas were not those who first gave rise to the intention.
All have long planted the roots of virtue.
In the presence of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of Yīfú, they have purely cultivated the Brahma conduct.
They are always praised by all Buddhas.
Constantly cultivating the wisdom of the Buddhas, possessing great spiritual powers,
skillfully knowing all doors of the various dharmas,
honest and without deceit, earnest and resolute in mindfulness.
Such Bodhisattvas fill their land.
Shèlìfú!
The lifespan of the Buddha Huāguāng is twelve small kalpas,
excluding the time before he became Buddha when he was still a prince.
The people of his country live for eight small kalpas.
After Huāguāng Tathāgata has passed twelve small kalpas,
he bestows the prophecy of Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi upon Jiānmǎn Bodhisattva.
He says to the Bhikṣus:
"This Jiānmǎn Bodhisattva will next become a Buddha,
named Huāzú'ānxíng, Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyak-saṃbuddha;
his Buddha-land will likewise be thus."
"Shèlìfú!
After the extinction of the Buddha Huāguāng,
the True Dharma will remain in the world for thirty-two small kalpas,
and the Counterfeit Dharma likewise for thirty-two small kalpas."
Then at that time, the World-Honored One,
desiring to further explain this meaning,
spoke in verse:
"Shèlìfú, in ages to come,
you will become a Buddha, the Honored One of Universal Wisdom,
with the name Huāguāng,
destined to deliver immeasurable multitudes.
Having made offerings to countless Buddhas,
you will perfect the Bodhisattva conduct,
possess the ten powers and other merits,
and realize the unsurpassed way.
After countless kalpas have passed,
