There will be many gods, human beings, and assemblies of śrāvakas,
as well as bodhisattvas, and myriad cotis, uncountably adorning his country.
The Buddha’s lifespan will be twelve minor kalpas;
the True Dharma will abide for twenty minor kalpas;
the Semblance Dharma will also abide for twenty minor kalpas.”
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to further clarify this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
“O assembly of bhikṣus,
with single mind attend,
as I have said,
truthfully and without variance.
This Kātyāyana
will with all manner
of marvelous and fine offerings
make offerings to the Buddhas.
After the Buddhas pass into nirvāṇa,
he will erect jeweled stūpas,
also using flowers and incense
to honor their relics.
In his final existence,
he will attain Buddha wisdom
and achieve supreme, perfect enlightenment.
His land will be pure,
delivering boundless
myriads of kotis of beings,
all to be honored and served in the ten directions.
The Buddha’s radiance
none will surpass.
That Buddha will be named
Yánfú Jīnguāng.
Bodhisattvas and śrāvakas
will sever all entanglements of becoming,
innumerable and numberless,
adorn his country.”
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the great assembly:
“I now tell you,
this great Mùjiānlián [Mahāmaudgalyāyana],
with all kinds of offerings, will serve and honor eight thousand Buddhas
with utmost reverence.
After those Buddhas pass into parinirvāṇa,
stūpas and shrines will be raised for each, a thousand yojanas in height,
length and breadth exactly five hundred yojanas,
all composed of gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, agate, pearl, rose quartz, and seven precious gems fused together,
adorned with masses of flowers, necklaces, incense paste, powdered incense, burning incense, silk canopies, banners, and pennants,
all used for offerings.
After this,
he will again make offerings to two hundred thousand kotis of Buddhas,
just as before.
He will then attain Buddhahood,
with the name Duōmóluóbá Zhāntánxiāng Tathāgata,
Worthy of Offerings, Perfectly Enlightened, Complete in Wisdom and Conduct, Well-Gone, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Hero, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, World-Honored One.
The kalpa will be called Xǐmǎn,
and the country named Yìlè.
His land will be smooth and even,
beryl for ground, adorned with jeweled trees,
raining down pearl flowers, pure throughout,
causing delight to all who see it.
Filled with gods, humans, bodhisattvas, and śrāvakas, innumerable in number.
The Buddha’s lifespan will be twenty-four minor kalpas;
the True Dharma will abide for forty minor kalpas;
the Semblance Dharma will also abide for forty minor kalpas.”
At that time, the World-Honored One,
wishing to further clarify this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
“My disciple here,
great Mùjiānlián,
after leaving this body,
shall meet eight thousand
and two hundred thousand kotis
of Buddhas, World-Honored Ones.
For the sake of the Buddha Way,
he will respectfully make offerings,
uphold pure conduct always at the Buddhas’ sides,
practicing the Brahma-path constantly.
For countless kalpas,
he will uphold the Buddha-dharma.
After the Buddhas’ parinirvāṇa,
he will build jeweled stūpas,
adorn them with tall golden spires,
flowers, incense, and music,
to venerate and serve,
the Buddhas’ stūpas and shrines.
Gradually perfecting
the bodhisattva path,
in the land of Yìlè
he will become a Buddha
named Duōmóluó,
Zhāntán’s Fragrance.
That Buddha’s lifespan
will be twenty-four kalpas,
ever teaching gods and humans
the Buddha’s path.
His śrāvakas are numberless,
as sands of the Ganges,
possessing Triple Insight and Six Powers,
of great spiritual strength.
Bodhisattvas, countless
in firm resolve and diligence,
regarding the Buddha’s wisdom
never turn back.
After the Buddha’s nirvāṇa,
the True Dharma will abide
for forty minor kalpas;
the Semblance Dharma likewise.
My disciples all
fully endowed with virtue and might,
five hundred in number,
all shall be prophesied.
In ages to come,
all will attain Buddhahood.
Both I and you, by past life conditions,
I now declare—
you should heed it well.
The Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:
“In the remote past—immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable asamkhyeya kalpas ago—
at that time there was a Buddha

named Dàtōng Zhìshèng Tathāgata, Worthy of Offerings, Perfectly Enlightened, Complete in Wisdom and Conduct, Well-Gone, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Hero, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Men, Buddha, World-Honored One.
His land was called Hǎochéng,
and the kalpa was called Dàxiàng.
Bhikṣus!
Since the parinirvāṇa of that Buddha, a vastly long time has passed.
It is like all the earth particles in the trichiliocosm: suppose someone ground them to ink.
Passing a thousand lands to the east, only then would he leave a drop,
as small as a mote of dust.
Again, passing another thousand lands,
he would leave another drop.
In this way, he would continue until all earth particles were made into ink.
What do you think?
All these lands,
whether expert mathematicians or their disciples,
could they determine their limit and know their number?
“No, World-Honored One!”
“Bhikṣus! The lands traversed by this person,
whether marked or unmarked by ink,
ground utterly to dust,
counting each mote as one kalpa;
the time since that Buddha’s parinirvāṇa has again surpassed this number
by innumerable, boundless hundreds of thousands of millions of nayuta asaṃkhyeya kalpas.
By the Tathāgata’s power of knowledge and vision,
I contemplate that distant time as if it were today.”
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to reiterate this meaning,
spoke a verse:
“I recall ages past,
innumerable, boundless kalpas,
when there was a Buddha, honored of two feet,
named Dàtōng Zhìshèng.
As if by effort one ground
the earth of a trichiliocosm,
all those earth particles
entirely made into ink.
Passing a thousand lands,
then leaving a speck of dust,
in this way continuing
until all those dust-ink specks were used up.
All those lands,
whether marked or unmarked,
ground entirely to dust,
counting one mote as one kalpa:
the number of these motes,
the kalpas again surpass this,
since that Buddha's parinirvāṇa,
through such immeasurable kalpas.
The Tathāgata’s unhindered wisdom
knows the parinirvāṇa of that Buddha,
and of the śrāvakas and bodhisattvas,
as clearly as witnessing the present extinction.
Bhikṣus, you should know!
The Buddha’s wisdom is pure and subtle,
free from outflows and without obstruction,
penetrating incalculable kalpas.”
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:
“Dàtōng Zhìshèng Buddha
had a lifespan of five trillion four hundred million nayuta kalpas.
When that Buddha first sat on the seat of awakening,
having subdued the armies of Māra,
about to attain Anuttarā Samyaksaṃbodhi,
yet the Buddha-dharma did not appear before him.
In this way, for a minor kalpa up to ten minor kalpas,
he sat cross-legged in samādhi, body and mind unmoving,
and still the Buddha-dharma did not manifest before him.
At that time, the devas of Trāyastriṃśa
prepared for the Buddha, beneath the bodhi-tree, a lion-throne a yojana high.
Upon this seat,
the Buddha was to attain Anuttarā Samyaksaṃbodhi.
Just as he sat upon this throne,
the various Brahma-kings caused heavenly flowers to rain down,
covering hundreds of yojanas.
A fragrant breeze blew at intervals, sweeping away wilted blossoms,
making way for fresh ones to fall.
Thus, ceaselessly for ten minor kalpas, they made offerings to the Buddha;
even after his parinirvāṇa, these flowers continued to fall.
The Four Heavenly Kings and their devas,
in order to make offerings to the Buddha, constantly struck heavenly drums,
while other devas played celestial music,
throughout the ten minor kalpas
and even up until his parinirvāṇa,
still did likewise.
“Bhikṣus!
It was only after ten minor kalpas that Dàtōng Zhìshèng Buddha
had the Buddha-dharma manifest before him, attaining Anuttarā Samyaksaṃbodhi.
Before the Buddha left home life,
he had sixteen sons,
the first of whom was named Zhìjī.
Each of the sons possessed rare and precious playthings;
hearing that their father had attained Anuttarā Samyaksaṃbodhi,
they all relinquished their treasured possessions and went to the Buddha.
Their mothers wept and followed after them.”
Their grandfather, the Wheel-Turning Sage King,
with a hundred great ministers and countless multitudes of people,
all surrounded them, accompanying them to the place of awakening.
All wished to draw near to Dàtōng Zhìshèng Tathāgata,
to make offerings with reverence, honor, and praise.
Arriving, they bowed their heads at his feet and circled the Buddha.
Wholeheartedly, with palms joined, they gazed up at the World-Honored One,
reciting these verses:
“Greatly powerful World-Honored One,
for the sake of liberating beings,
through countless millions of kalpas,
at last attained Buddhahood.
All vows are now fulfilled,
splendid indeed, the supreme and auspicious.
How rare is the World-Honored One:
one sitting for ten minor kalpas,
his body, hands, and feet
utterly still, at peace and unmoving.
His mind ever serene and unafraid,
never distracted or scattered,
utterly extinguished in final quiescence,
abiding in the dharma of no outflows.
Now we see the World-Honored One,
peaceful and accomplished in the Buddha’s path;
thus do we obtain great benefit,
and our joy and happiness are immense.
Beings constantly suffer afflictions,
blind and without a guide,
ignorant of the way beyond suffering,
not knowing to seek liberation.
Through the long night, their evils increase,
the multitudes of devas ever diminish;
from darkness into darkness,
they never hear the name of Buddha.
Now the Buddha has attained the utmost,
peaceful and outflow-free path;
we, together with gods and men,
gain the greatest benefit.
Therefore, all prostrate
and take refuge in the supreme venerable.”
When the sixteen royal sons had thus praised the Buddha in verse,
they all entreated the World-Honored One to turn the Dharma-wheel,
saying together:
“May the World-Honored One preach the Dharma, giving peace, compassion, and vast benefit to devas and humans.”
Again, they spoke in verse:
“Hero of the world, none can compare,
adorned by a hundred blessings,
having attained unsurpassed wisdom,
may you teach for the world.
Deliver us
and all sentient beings,
expound and reveal
so we may attain this wisdom.
If we attain Buddhahood,
so, too, will sentient beings.
World-Honored One, you know the deepest thoughts of beings,
as well as the paths they travel,
you know the power of their wisdom,
their desires and cultivation of merit,
and their karmic actions of former lives.
Having known all this,
may the World-Honored One turn the supreme wheel.”
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:
“When Dàtōng Zhìshèng Buddha
attained Anuttarā Samyaksaṃbodhi,
the worlds in each of the ten directions, five hundred million in each, experienced six kinds of tremors.
In the dark and hidden regions of those lands,
where even the suns and moons could not shine,
all became greatly illumined; the sentient beings dwelling there could all see one another.
All exclaimed:
‘How is it that so many beings have suddenly appeared here?
Moreover, the lands, celestial palaces,
up to the palaces of Brahma, shook in six ways;
a great light shone everywhere, filling the worlds,
surpassing even the light of the gods.’”
Then, in five hundred million lands to the east,
the palaces of the Brahmā gods grew brighter, far surpassing their normal light.
Each of the Brahma kings thought:
‘Now these palaces are shining as never before.
For what reason does this sign appear?’
At that time, each of the Brahma kings
went to gather and discuss this matter.
Among them was a great Brahma king
named Jiùyīqiè,
who for the assembly of Brahmas
spoke this verse:
‘All our palaces,
have never shone thus,
what is the reason for this?
Let us each seek it out.
Is it that a great deva has descended,
or that a Buddha has appeared in the world,
and thus this great light
shines throughout all ten directions?’
Then, the five hundred million Brahma kings,
each with their palaces,
filled their divine garments with many heavenly flowers
and together traveled west in search of the cause.
There, they saw Dàtōng Zhìshèng Tathāgata at the seat of awakening
under the bodhi-tree, seated on the lion-throne,
surrounded in reverent homage by devas, nāga kings, gandharvas, kiṁnaras, mahoragas, humans and non-humans,
and also saw the sixteen royal sons inviting the Buddha to turn the Dharma-wheel.
At that moment, all the Brahmā Kings
bowed their heads at the feet of the Buddha,
circumambulated him hundreds and thousands of times,
and immediately scattered heavenly flowers upon the Buddha— —
the flowers they scattered were as great as Mount Xūmí;
and also offered them to the Buddha’s bodhi tree— —
the bodhi tree was ten yojanas high.
When the offering of flowers was finished,
each presented their palaces to the Buddha,
and spoke as follows:
“We only beseech compassion and benefit for us.
May you kindly accept the palaces we offer.”
Then, all the Brahmā Kings,
before the Buddha, with one mind and one voice, recited these verses:
“The World-Honored One is most rare,
difficult to meet or encounter;
possessed of immeasurable merit,
able to rescue and protect all.
Great teacher of gods and humans,
compassionate to the world,
all sentient beings in the ten directions
universally receive your benefit.
We have come here, over five trillion lands,
abandoning profound meditative bliss,
for the sake of making offerings to the Buddha.
Our past good fortune
has resulted in splendid palaces,
now offered to the World-Honored One—
we only ask that you compassionately accept them.”
Then all the Brahmā Kings,
after praising the Buddha with verses,
each said:
“We only wish that the World-Honored One turns the Dharma Wheel,
liberates sentient beings, and opens the path to Nirvāṇa.”
Then all the Brahmā Kings,
with one mind and one voice, recited verses as follows:
“Hero of the world, honored among the two-legged,
we only wish for you to expound the Dharma,
with great power of compassion,
to liberate suffering sentient beings.”
At that time, Dàtōng Zhìshèng Tathāgata
silently gave his consent.
“Again, Bhikṣus! In the southeast, in five trillion countries,
the great Brahmā Kings each saw their own palaces
shining with unprecedented light.
Overjoyed and elated, feeling awe and wonder,
they each came together and discussed these matters.
Among their assembly,
there was one great Brahmā King,
named Dàbēi,
who, for the Brahmā assembly,
spoke verses as follows:
‘What cause or condition
has produced such a sign?
The palaces of us all
shine with a light never seen before.
Is it that a great deva has been born?
Or that a Buddha has appeared in the world?
Never have we seen such a sign,
let us with one mind seek together.
Passing through billions of lands,
let us pursue and trace this light,
most likely a Buddha has appeared in the world,
to save suffering sentient beings.’
At that time, the five trillion Brahmā Kings
together with their palaces,
each gathering heavenly flowers in their garments,
journeyed toward the northwest to trace the sign.
They saw Dàtōng Zhìshèng Tathāgata abiding at the site of awakening,
beneath the bodhi tree, seated on the lion’s throne,
with gods, nāga kings, gandharvas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans and nonhumans gathered in reverent attendance,
and saw the sixteen princes requesting the Buddha to turn the Dharma Wheel.
Then all the Brahmā Kings
bowed their heads at the Buddha’s feet and circumambulated him hundreds and thousands of times,
and immediately scattered heavenly flowers upon the Buddha— —
the flowers they scattered were as great as Mount Xūmí,
also offering them to the Buddha’s bodhi tree.
When the offering was finished,
each presented their palaces to the Buddha,
and spoke as follows:
‘We only beseech compassion and benefit for us.
May you kindly accept the palaces we offer.’
At that moment, all the Brahmā Kings
before the Buddha, with one mind and one voice,
recited verses as follows:
‘Holy Lord and King of the Gods,
whose voice is like that of a kálaviṅka bird,
compassionate toward sentient beings—
we now respectfully pay homage.
The World-Honored One is most rare,
appearing but once in vast ages,
for one hundred and eighty kalpas,
there passed emptily, with no Buddha appearing.
The three evil realms were filled,
the ranks of gods declined,
now a Buddha has appeared in the world,
to be the eyes for all sentient beings.
Refuge for the world,
savior and protector of all,
father to sentient beings,
compassionate and beneficial to all.
It is by our accumulated good fortune
that we now can encounter the World-Honored One.’
Having thus praised the Buddha with verses,
each spoke as follows:
‘We only wish the World-Honored One, out of compassion for all,
to turn the Dharma Wheel,
and liberate sentient beings.’
Then all the Brahmā Kings,
with one mind and one voice,
made verses saying:
‘Great Sage, turn the Dharma Wheel,
reveal the marks of all dharmas,
rescue suffering sentient beings,
bring them great joy.
Behaviors who hear this Dharma,
attain the path or rebirth in the heavens,
the evil realms are diminished,
those patient in virtue increase.’
Then Dàtōng Zhìshèng Tathāgata
silently gave his consent.
Again, Bhikṣus!
In the south, in five trillion countries there were great Brahmā Kings,
each saw their own palace
shining with unprecedented light.
Rejoicing and marveling, they became filled with awe and wonder,
and came together to discuss these matters:
‘For what reason do our palaces have this radiance?’
Among their assembly,
there was one great Brahmā King,
named Miàofǎ,
who, for the Brahmā assembly,
spoke verses as follows:
‘The palaces of us all,
shine with awesome radiance,
this is not without cause or condition,
such a sign ought to be sought.
Through hundreds of thousands of kalpas,
never have we seen such a sign,
Is it that a great deva has been born?
Or that a Buddha has appeared in the world?’
At that time, the five trillion Brahmā Kings
together with their palaces,
each gathering heavenly flowers in their garments,
journeyed to the north to trace this sign.
They saw Dàtōng Zhìshèng Tathāgata abiding at the site of awakening,
beneath the bodhi tree, seated on the lion’s throne,
with gods, nāga kings, gandharvas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans and nonhumans gathered in reverent attendance,
and saw the sixteen princes requesting the Buddha to turn the Dharma Wheel. At that time, all the Brahmā Kings
bowed their heads at the Buddha’s feet and circumambulated him hundreds and thousands of times,
immediately scattered heavenly flowers upon the Buddha— —
the flowers they scattered were as great as Mount Xūmí,
and they were also offered to the Buddha’s bodhi tree.
When the flowers had been offered,
each presented their palaces to the Buddha,
and spoke as follows:
‘We only beseech compassion and benefit for us.
May you kindly accept the palaces we offer.’
At that time, all the Brahmā Kings,
before the Buddha, with one mind and one voice,
recited verses as follows:
‘The World-Honored One is most difficult to see,
destroyer of all afflictions,
through one hundred and thirty kalpas,
only now have we attained one vision.
For all famished and thirsty sentient beings,
you provide a rain of Dharma to fill them.
Never seen before,
one of boundless wisdom—
like the udumbara flower,
today at last we encounter.
Our palaces,
become splendid due to this light,
by the World-Honored One’s great compassion,
we only wish you kindly accept them.’
Then, all the Brahmā Kings, after praising the Buddha with verses,
each said:
‘We only wish the World-Honored One would turn the Dharma Wheel,
so that all worlds, gods, Māras, Brahmās, śramaṇas, and brāhmaṇas,
may all obtain peace and be liberated.’
Then all the Brahmā Kings,
with one mind and one voice,
recited verses as follows:
“We only wish that the honored one among gods and humans may turn the unsurpassed Dharma wheel,
strike the great Dharma drum,
and blow the great Dharma conch,
universally cause a rain of the great Dharma to fall,
and deliver immeasurable sentient beings.
We all return and request,
+ENDVERSE and will proclaim the profound and far-reaching sound.”
At that time, Dàtōng Zhìshèng Tathāgata
silently gave his consent.
From the southwest to the lower directions, it was likewise so.
Then, the great Brahma kings of five hundred million eons of realms in the upper direction,
all saw their own palace residences
radiating a wondrous brilliance and majesty, never seen before.
Joyful and exultant, they gave rise to a rare thought,
and each approached the others, discussing this matter together:
“For what reason do our palaces have this light?”
Among that assembly, there was a great Brahma king,
named Shīqì,
who, for the sake of all the Brahma assembly,
spoke these verses:
“Now, for what reason
do all our palaces
possess majesty and radiant light,
adorned in a way never seen before?
Such wonderful aspects,
neither heard nor seen in the past,
have they arisen from the birth of a great virtuous deity?
Or, has a Buddha appeared in the world?”
Then, the five hundred million Brahma kings,
along with their palaces,
each taking celestial flowers in their robes,
together proceeded to the lower direction to inquire about this sign.
They saw Dàtōng Zhìshèng Tathāgata abiding in the place of awakening,
beneath the bodhi tree, seated upon a lion throne,
surrounded respectfully by various gods, dragon kings, gandharvas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans,
and saw sixteen royal sons requesting the Buddha to turn the Dharma wheel.
Then, the Brahma kings
bowed their heads and prostrated to the Buddha, circumambulating him a hundred thousand times,
and immediately scattered celestial flowers over the Buddha—
the flowers scattered piled as high as Mount Sumeru,
and were also offered to the bodhi tree.
Having made these flower offerings,
each one presented their palace to that Buddha,
saying:
“We only hope for compassion and abundant benefit to us.
May you deign to accept the palace we offer.”
At that time, the Brahma kings,
right in front of the Buddha, with single-mindedness and in unison,
pronounced these verses:
“How wonderful it is to see the Buddhas,
the holy honored ones who save the world,
capable within the prison of the three realms, to strive to deliver sentient beings.
The universally wise honored one among gods and humans,
compassionately regards all kinds,
is able to open the gate of nectar,
widely delivering all beings.
For countless eons in the past,
all passed in emptiness without a Buddha,
before the World-honored One appeared,
the ten directions were constantly shrouded in darkness,
the three evil paths were increasing,
the Asuras were also flourishing,
while the population of gods was increasingly decreasing,
and upon death, many fell into the evil paths.
Not hearing the Dharma from a Buddha,
they constantly performed unwholesome deeds,
their appearance, strength, and wisdom,
all declined,
due to karmic causes of evil actions,
happiness and the thought of happiness were lost,
adhering to the Dharma of deviant views,
not recognizing rules of wholesome conduct,
not receiving transformation by the Buddha,
always falling into evil paths.
The Buddha acts as the eye of the world,
only after a very long time does he appear,
compassionately regarding all sentient beings,
and therefore manifests in the world.
Having transcended and attained perfect enlightenment,
we rejoice greatly,
as do all other beings,
joyfully praising this unprecedented event.
All our palaces,
have been wondrously adorned due to this light;
now we respectfully offer them to the World-honored One,
only wishing for compassionate acceptance.
May this merit,
pervade all beings,
so that we together with other sentient beings,
may all realize the Buddha path together.”
Then the five hundred million Brahma kings, having thus praised the Buddha in verse,
each addressed the Buddha, saying:
“We only wish that the World-honored One
may turn the Dharma wheel,
bringing peace to many,
and delivering many beings.”
At that time, the Brahma kings
recited verses, saying:
“World-honored One, turn the Dharma wheel,
strike the nectar drum of Dharma,
save beings suffering and afflicted,
and open and reveal the path to nirvāṇa.
We only wish you would accept our request,
with your vast and wondrous sound,
compassionately expound and
proclaim the Dharma practiced through immeasurable eons.”
At that time, Dàtōng Zhìshèng Tathāgata,
having received the request of the Brahma kings of the ten directions and the sixteen princes,
immediately turned the Dharma wheel three times in twelve aspects—
which neither śramaṇas nor brāhmaṇas,
nor gods, māras, Brahmas, nor any in the world can turn—
namely: “This is suffering,
this is the accumulation of suffering,
this is the cessation of suffering,
this is the path to the cessation of suffering”;
and broadly expounded the twelvefold chain of dependent origination—
ignorance conditions volitional formations,
volitional formations condition consciousness,
consciousness conditions name-and-form,
name-and-form conditions the six sense bases,
the six sense bases condition contact,
contact conditions feeling,
feeling conditions craving,
craving conditions grasping,
grasping conditions becoming,
becoming conditions birth,
birth conditions old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, and affliction.
When ignorance ceases, volitional formations cease,
when volitional formations cease, consciousness ceases,
when consciousness ceases, name-and-form ceases,
when name-and-form ceases, the six sense bases cease,
when the six sense bases cease, contact ceases,
when contact ceases, feeling ceases,
when feeling ceases, craving ceases,
when craving ceases, grasping ceases,
when grasping ceases, becoming ceases,
when becoming ceases, birth ceases,
when birth ceases, then old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, and affliction also cease.
When the Buddha preached this Dharma among the great assembly of gods and humans,
sixty million nayuta beings,
by virtue of their non-attachment to all dharmas,
became liberated in mind from outflows,
all attaining profound and wondrous meditative states,
the three insights and six superknowledges,
fully endowed with the eight liberations.
During the second, third, and fourth turnings of the Dharma,
trillions upon trillions of nayuta, numbering as the sands of the Ganges,
also, due to their non-attachment to all dharmas,
attained liberation of mind from outflows.
From then onward,
the assembly of Śrāvakas
became innumerable and boundless.
At that time, the sixteen royal princes—
all as young boys left home and became śrāmaṇeras,
their faculties sharp and wisdom clear,
having already offered service to hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddhas,
purely cultivating the brahmacarya,
seeking anuttarā-samyak-sambodhi—
all together addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-honored One!
These incalculable, immeasurable great śrāvakas,
have all now been accomplished.
World-honored One,
you also ought to expound for us the Dharma of anuttarā-samyak-sambodhi,
so that when we have heard it, we may all study and practice it together.
World-honored One!
Our highest aspiration is for the Tathāgata’s wisdom and insight;
what is deeply contemplated in our hearts, the Buddha naturally knows.”
At that time, among the company led by the Wheel-turning Sacred King, eighty billion people
saw the sixteen princes go forth from home,
and also sought ordination. The king permitted them.
“At that time, that Buddha, having accepted the śrāmaṇeras’ request,
after twenty thousand kalpas had passed,
among the fourfold assembly
expounded this Mahāyāna sutra,
named the ‘Sublime Dharma Lotus Flower’, teaching the Dharma of bodhisattvas,
protected and upheld by the Buddhas.
After expounding this sutra,
the sixteen śrāmaṇeras
for the sake of anuttarā-samyak-sambodhi,
all together accepted it, recited it fluently,
and while the sutra was being expounded,
the sixteen bodhisattva śrāmaṇeras all faithfully accepted it;
some of the assembly of śrāvakas also believed and understood;
among the rest of the multitude, countless billions were filled with doubt and confusion.
The Buddha preached this sutra
for eight thousand kalpas without pause or cessation.
After expounding this sutra, he immediately entered a quiet room,
abiding in meditative absorption for eighty-four thousand kalpas.
At that time, the sixteen bodhisattva śrāmaṇeras,
knowing the Buddha had entered the room and was serenely dwelling in meditation, each ascended the Dharma seat, and for eighty-four thousand kalpas
for the fourfold assembly, extensively explained and distinguished the Sublime Dharma Lotus Sutra.
Each delivered sixty million nayuta Ganges-sands of sentient beings, instructing, benefiting, and causing joy,
enabling them to give rise to the mind of anuttarā-samyak-sambodhi.
“Dàtōng Zhìshèng Fó,
after more than eighty-four thousand kalpas had passed,
arose from samādhi,
went to the Dharma seat, and sat in serene composure.
He proclaimed to the great assembly:
‘These sixteen bodhisattva novices
are truly rare.
Their faculties are keen and sharp,
their wisdom clear and bright.
They have already made offerings to innumerable hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddhas. In the presence of these Buddhas, they constantly cultivated the pure practice,
upheld the wisdom of the Buddhas,
expounded and revealed it to sentient beings, leading them to enter therein.
You all should frequently draw near to them and make offerings.
Why is this?
If śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas
can believe the teachings of the sūtras spoken by these sixteen bodhisattvas,
and uphold them without disparagement,
such people shall all attain Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi and the wisdom of the Thus Come One.’”
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:
“These sixteen bodhisattvas always delight in preaching this wondrous Dharma Flower Sūtra.
Each one of the bodhisattvas transforms six hundred myriad koṭis of nayutas of Ganges-sands-numbered sentient beings.
In every birth, wherever they are born, they are always together with the bodhisattvas,
and on hearing the Dharma from them, all believe and understand it.
Through this condition,
they encounter four hundred myriad koṭis of World-honored Buddhas, and even now it is not exhausted.
Bhikṣus!
I now tell you:
‘Those sixteen novices, disciples of the Buddha,
have all now attained Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi,
and in the lands of the ten directions
are presently teaching the Dharma,
each with innumerable hundreds of thousands of millions of bodhisattvas and śrāvakas as their retinue.
Of these, two novices became Buddhas in the east:
one named Āchù, in the Land of Joy,
the second named Xūmídǐng;
in the southeast, there were two Buddhas:
one named Shīzǐyīn,
the second named Shīzǐxiàng;
in the south, two Buddhas:
one named Xūkōngzhù,
the second named Chángmiè;
in the southwest, two Buddhas:
one named Dìxiàng,
the second named Fànxiàng;
in the west, two Buddhas:
one named Āmítuó,
the second named Dùyīqièshìjiān kǔnǎo;
in the northwest, two Buddhas:
one named Duōmáluóbá-Chándānxīang Shéntōng,
the second named Xūmíxiàng;
in the north, two Buddhas:
one named Yúnzìzài,
the second named Yúnzìzài Wáng;
in the northeast, a Buddha
named Huài Yīqiè Shìjiān Bùwèi.
The sixteenth is myself, Shìjiāmóuní Fó,
who attained Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi in the Sahā world.
Bhikṣus!
When we were novices,
each of us taught and transformed innumerable hundreds of thousands of millions of Ganges-sands-numbered sentient beings,
who heard the Dharma from me for the sake of Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Among these sentient beings,
even now, some dwell at the stage of śrāvakas.
I constantly teach and transform them toward Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.
These people,
by means of this Dharma, should gradually enter the Buddha Way.
Why is this?
The wisdom of the Thus Come One is difficult to believe and difficult to understand.
The countless Ganges-sands-numbered beings we transformed at that time
are you bhikṣus, and my śrāvaka disciples in future ages after my extinction.
After my extinction,
there will again be disciples who do not hear this sūtra,
who neither know nor realize the practices of the bodhisattvas,
and in regard to the merit and virtue they have obtained themselves, they give rise to the thought of extinction,
and will enter Nirvāṇa.
In other lands where I become a Buddha,
I have different names.
These people, though in their minds they give rise to the thought of extinction and enter Nirvāṇa,
in those lands seek the Buddha’s wisdom,
and are able to hear this sūtra;
it is solely by means of the Buddha Vehicle (One Vehicle) that they attain extinction,
there is no other vehicle,
except for the various skillful means of the Thus Come Ones speaking expediently.
Bhikṣus!
When the Thus Come One knows that the time of Nirvāṇa has come,
and the assembly is also pure, their faith and understanding firm,
they see through the Dharma of emptiness, and have deeply entered meditative absorption,
he then gathers together the bodhisattvas and śrāvakas, and expounds this sūtra for them.
In the world, there is no attaining extinction by the two vehicles;
it is only by the One Buddha Vehicle that extinction is attained.
Bhikṣus, you should know!
The Thus Come One, by skillful means, deeply enters the natures of sentient beings,
knows their inclination toward lesser teachings and their deep attachment to the five desires,
and for the sake of these, speaks of Nirvāṇa.
If such people hear this, then they will immediately accept and believe it.
It is like a dangerous, evil road, five hundred yojanas in length, desolate and without people—a place of fear and dread.
If there is a large group of people
wishing to travel this road to reach a place of precious treasures,
and there is a guide,
wise and perspicacious, skilled in recognizing the features of peril and passage on the dangerous road,
leading the crowd as they seek to cross this hardship.
Among those being led,
midway they become weary and wish to turn back, telling the guide:
‘We are exhausted, and moreover afraid;
we cannot proceed further.
The road ahead is yet far,
and now we wish to turn back.’
The guide, applying many skillful means
and thinking to himself:
‘How pitiful they are!
Why abandon this great store of treasures and wish to turn back?’
After thinking thus,
by the power of skillful means,
in the middle of the dangerous road, three hundred yojanas along,
he manifests a great city,
and tells the crowd:
‘Do not be afraid or wish to turn back.
Now, here is a great city,
where you may stay and do as you please.
If you enter this city, you will quickly gain peace and security.
If you are able to proceed to the place of treasures, you may also go there.’
Then the crowds, exhausted and spent,
became greatly joyous at heart, exclaiming at such unprecedented events:
‘We are now delivered from this evil path and have quickly reached peace and security.’
Then the people
entered the conjured city ahead,
giving rise to the thought of having crossed over,
the thought of safety.
Then, the guide,
knowing that these people have found rest and are no longer weary,
eliminates the conjured city,
and tells the crowd:
‘Go forward now—the place of treasures is near.
That great city before was a manifestation conjured by me, solely for the sake of rest.’
“Bhikṣus!
The Thus Come One is likewise so.
Now, for your sake, he is the great guide,
knowing how the evil path of birth and death, with all its afflictions, is perilous, long, and should be transcended and crossed over.
If, upon hearing only of the One Buddha Vehicle,
sentient beings would not wish to see the Buddha nor draw near to him,
and think to themselves:
‘The Buddha Way is long and far; to attain it, one must endure much toil
over a long time before it can be accomplished.’
The Buddha, knowing such hearts to be timid and lacking,
by the power of skillful means, for the sake of rest along the way, speaks of two Nirvāṇas in the midst of the path.
If sentient beings abide in the two vehicles,
then the Thus Come One immediately tells them:
‘Your task is not yet completed;
the ground upon which you abide is close to Buddha’s wisdom,
you should carefully reflect and ponder
whether the attained Nirvāṇa
is genuine or not.
This is but the skilful means power of the Thus Come One,
wherein the One Buddha Vehicle is variously spoken of as three.’
Just like that guide, who, for the sake of rest, conjured a great city.
When he knows they have rested,
he tells them: ‘The place of treasures is near,
this city is unreal,
I only conjured it.’”
Then the World Honored One, wishing to further clarify this meaning,
spoke in verse:
Dàtōng Zhìshèng Fó,
for ten kalpas sat at the place of enlightenment,
yet the Dharma of Buddhas did not manifest before him,
and he was unable to achieve the Buddha Way.
The multitudes of gods, dragon kings,
and asuras
constantly rained heavenly flowers
as offerings to that Buddha.
All the gods beat heavenly drums,
and performed various musical dances;
the fragrant breezes withered the flowers,
and again new and splendid ones rained down.
After ten minor kalpas had passed,
only then did he attain the Buddha Way,
and all the gods and humans of the world
were elated at heart.
That Buddha had sixteen sons,
all with their retinues,
surrounded by thousands of myriads of koti,
who went together to the Buddha’s place,
bowed their heads to the Buddha’s feet,
and requested him to turn the Dharma wheel:
‘O Holy Lion, rain down the Dharma,
to satisfy us and all beings.’
The World Honored One is most difficult to encounter—
only once in a very long time does he appear,
so as to awaken all living beings,
shaking all worlds far and wide.
In the eastern worlds,
across five hundred myriad koṭis of countries,
the Brahma palaces shone with marvellous radiance,
such as had never been seen before.
All the Brahmas, seeing this sign,
soon came to the Buddha’s place,
scattered flowers as offerings,
presented their palaces as gifts,
requested the Buddha to turn the Dharma wheel,
and extolled him in verse.
The Buddha knew the time had not yet arrived,
so he accepted the invitation and sat in silence.
Those from the three directions and the four quarters,
above and below, did likewise.
They scattered flowers, honoring the palace,
and invited the Buddha to turn the Dharma Wheel:
“Shìzūn is extremely difficult to encounter;
we wish, with great compassion,
that you broadly open the door to nectar,
and turn the unsurpassed Dharma Wheel.”
The World-Honored One of boundless wisdom,
accepted the people’s invitation,
and taught various dharmas:
“The Four Noble Truths, the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination,
from ignorance to old age and death,
all arise from the conditions of birth.
Thus are the various afflictions;
you ought to know them.”
As he expounded these teachings,
six hundred million koṭis
put an end to all suffering,
all attained Arhatship.
At the second teaching,
countless multitudes as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
were unattached to all dharmas,
and likewise attained Arhatship.
After that, those who attained the Path
were uncountable,
their number could not be gauged
even by calculation over myriads of aeons.
At that time, the sixteen royal princes
left home to become śrāmaṇeras,
and together invited that Buddha
to expound the Mahāyāna Dharma:
“We and our attendants
will all attain Buddhahood;
may we gain wisdom like the World-Honored One, whose insight is foremost and pure.”
The Buddha knew the intent of the youths’ hearts,
as well as their practices in past lives,
and with countless causes and conditions,
and various parables,
explained the six pāramitās
and the various feats of supernatural power.
He distinguished the true Dharma,
the path practiced by bodhisattvas,
and expounded this Lotus Sūtra,
in verses as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
After that Buddha finished preaching the sūtra,
he entered a quiet chamber for meditation,
remaining single-minded in one place,
for eighty-four thousand kalpas.
These śrāmaṇeras
knew the Buddha had not yet emerged from meditation,
so for countless koṭis of people
they taught the unsurpassed wisdom of the Buddha.
Each took his place on a Dharma seat,
expounding this Mahāyāna sūtra,
and after the Buddha’s Parinirvāṇa,
spread and supported the Dharma.
Each śrāmaṇera, the beings they guided,
numbered six hundred million koṭis, crowds equal to the sands of the Ganges.
After that Buddha’s extinction,
those who had heard the teachings,
in every buddha land,
were always born together with their teacher.
These sixteen śrāmaṇeras
fulfilled the bodhisattva path,
and now exist in the ten directions,
each has attained perfect enlightenment.
Those who heard the teachings at that time,
remain in the presence of various Buddhas;
those abiding in the path of śrāvakas,
are gradually instructed in the Buddha Way.
I was among the sixteen,
and I also taught you then.
Therefore, by skillful means,
I lead you toward the Buddha’s wisdom.
Because of these original causes and conditions,
now I preach the Lotus Sūtra,
to enable you to enter the Buddha Way,
so be careful not to harbor fear or dread.
It is like a hazardous, evil road,
utterly remote, full of poisonous beasts,
where there is neither water nor grass—
a place people dread and fear.
Countless thousands of people
wish to pass through this perilous path;
the road is extremely vast and far,
stretching five hundred yojanas.
At that time, there is a guide,
strong, knowledgeable, and wise,
clear and resolute in mind,
saving the others amidst danger.
Everyone becomes weary and exhausted,
and they say to the guide:
‘We are suddenly worn out,
here we wish to turn back.’
The guide thinks to himself:
‘How pitiable these people are;
why do they wish to turn back
and miss the great treasure ahead?’
Immediately he considers skillful means,
and uses supernormal powers,
to conjure up a great city,
adorned with splendid dwellings,
surrounded by gardens and groves,
canals and bathing pools,
with several gates and high towers,
full of men and women.
After conjuring this,
he reassures the people:
‘Enter this city,
each may enjoy as he wishes.’
After entering the city,
all the people are greatly joyful,
feeling safe and secure,
thinking they have already been rescued.
When the guide sees they have rested,
he gathers them and says:
‘You should move forward;
this is only a conjured city.
I saw you exhausted,
wanting to turn back halfway,
so through skillful means,
I conjured this city as an expedient.
You must strive with diligence,
and reach the place of treasure together.’
I am just the same:
as the guide for all,
I see seekers halfway
become lax or abandon practice,
unable to escape birth and death,
and the perilous road of afflictions.
So with skillful means,
for rest, I speak of Nirvāṇa,
saying, ‘You have ended suffering,
and what needed to be done has been accomplished.’
Once they know they have reached Nirvāṇa,
and all attained Arhatship,
then I bring together the great assembly,
and teach them the true Dharma.
Through the skillful power of all Buddhas,
the Three Vehicles are explained in detail,
but really there is only the One Buddha Vehicle;
for the sake of rest, two are taught.
Now I tell you the truth:
what you have attained is not extinction,
but is the all-knowing wisdom of Buddha;
therefore, strive greatly.
When you realize all-knowing wisdom,
the ten powers and other Buddha-dharmas,
perfect the thirty-two marks—
this is true extinction.
Buddhas, as guides,
for the sake of rest, speak of Nirvāṇa;
once that rest is known,
they lead into Buddha’s wisdom.
*The Wonderful Dharma Lotus Sūtra*
Volume Four of *The Wonderful Dharma Lotus Sūtra*
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Kuṣā, Guīcí, in Late Qín, Kumārajīva,
at imperial order.
At that time, Fùlóunà Mítuóluónízi,
having heard from the Buddha about skillful means, wisdom, and adept teaching,
heard as well the predictions of anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi given to the great disciples,
and heard the stories of past-life causes and conditions,
and also heard of the great supernatural power and sovereignty of the Buddhas.
What he gained was unprecedented, and his mind became pure and joyful.
He rose from his seat, approached the Buddha, and bowed, touching his head to the Buddha’s feet,
then stood to one side,
gazing reverently at the honored face, not letting his eyes leave it for a moment,
and he thought to himself:
“How extraordinary is the World-Honored One!
What he has accomplished is rare indeed!
According to the many types of beings in the world,
he teaches with skillful insight,
and draws all beings out of their attachments everywhere.
Of the Buddha’s merits and virtues, I cannot fully express them;
only the World-Honored Buddha
can know the profound roots of our aspirations.”
At that time, the Buddha said to the bhikṣus:
“Do you see this Fùlóunà Mítuóluónízi?
I have always said, among expounders of the Dharma, he is foremost,
and have constantly praised the various virtues he possesses:
his diligence in upholding and spreading my Dharma,
his ability to instruct, benefit, and gladden the fourfold assembly,
his complete explanation of the correct Dharma of the Buddha,
bringing great benefit to those who practice purity.
Apart from a Tathāgata, no one can match his eloquence.
You must not think that Fùlóunà only upholds and proclaims my Dharma;
before ninety koṭis of buddhas in the past,
he upheld and spread the correct Dharma of the Buddhas,
and among their Dharma teachers, he too was always foremost.”
Moreover, regarding the teachings on emptiness given by the Buddhas, he understands them clearly and thoroughly,
attains the four unobstructed knowledges,
and is always able to teach the Dharma with careful discernment and purity,
without any doubt or confusion,
possessing the full power of the supernormal abilities of a Bodhisattva.
According to his lifespan, he constantly practices the Brahma conduct;
in the world of that Buddha,
all people call him truly a Śrāvakā;
yet Fùlóunà, using such skillful means,
benefits countless hundreds of thousands of living beings,
and also transforms innumerable Asaṃkhyeya people,
enabling them to establish Anuttarā Samyak-saṃbodhi.
For the sake of purifying the Buddha land,
he constantly performs Buddha deeds, teaching and transforming sentient beings.
“Bhikṣus,
Fùlóunà was foremost among the expounders of the Dharma under the seven Buddhas,
and now, among those expounding the Dharma under me, he is also foremost.
In the Bhadrakalpa, among all future Buddhas, among those expounding the Dharma, he will likewise be foremost,
and in every case will protect, uphold, and proclaim the Buddha Dharma.
In the future as well, he will protect and proclaim the Dharma of numberless, boundless Buddhas,
teaching and benefiting countless sentient beings,
enabling them to establish Anuttarā Samyak-saṃbodhi.
For the sake of purifying the Buddha land,
he is ever diligent in guiding sentient beings,
gradually fulfilling the Bodhisattva path.
After measureless Asaṃkhyeya kalpas,
in this very land, he will attain Anuttarā Samyak-saṃbodhi,

with the title Fǎmíng Tathāgata, Worthy of Offerings, Perfectly Omniscient, Possessed of Wisdom and Practice, Well Gone, Knower of the World, Supreme Person, Tamer of Beings, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, World-Honored One.
That Buddha will use a triple chiliocosm as numerous as Ganges sands as a single Buddha land,
with the ground made of the seven treasures,
as flat as a palm,
with no mountains, gorges, streams, or ravines.
Multitudes of pavilions and towers made of the seven treasures will fill it,
and the palaces of the gods will be close in the sky.
Humans and gods will intermingle and be able to see each other.
There will be no evil realms, nor any women.
All beings there are born by transformation,
with no lustful desires.
They attain great supernatural powers,
their bodies radiate light, moving and flying at will,
their minds are steadfast, strong in diligence and wisdom,
and universally golden in color, adorned with the thirty-two marks.
The beings of that land constantly sustain themselves with two kinds of food:
first, the food of Dharma joy;
second, the food of meditative delight.
There will be innumerable Asaṃkhyeya thousands of millions of Nayuta Bodhisattvas,
attaining great supernatural power and the four unobstructed knowledges,
skilled in teaching and transforming all kinds of sentient beings.
The Śrāvakā assembly will be incalculable by count or computation;
all will have fully attained the six supernatural abilities, three insights, and eight liberations.
The Buddha land
is thus replete with all such innumerable adornments and accomplishments of virtue.
The kalpa is called Bǎomíng,
and the land is called Shànjìng.
The lifespan of that Buddha
will be countless Asaṃkhyeya kalpas,
and the Dharma will endure for an exceedingly long time.
After the Buddha’s nirvāṇa,
jeweled stūpas of seven treasures will arise, filling the land.”
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to reiterate this teaching,
spoke in verse, saying:
“Bhikṣus, listen attentively!
The path walked by the son of the Buddha,
skillfully learned in expedient means,
cannot be conceived or measured.
Knowing that the multitudes enjoy lesser teachings
and fear great wisdom,
for this reason Bodhisattvas
take the form of Śrāvakās and Pratyekabuddhas,
using countless expedient means
to transform various types of beings.
They say of themselves that they are Śrāvakās,
far removed from the Buddha path,
but ferry across countless beings,
enabling them all to attain accomplishment.
Though they appear to have small desires and slackness,
they shall gradually be made to attain Buddhahood.
Inwardly hiding the conduct of Bodhisattvas,
outwardly manifesting as Śrāvakās,
with little desire and weariness of birth and death,
in truth they purify Buddha lands themselves.
They show the people the three poisons,
and also manifest the marks of wrong views;
my disciples are like this,
using skillful means to ferry sentient beings.
If I were to speak in detail
of the various manifestations and transformations,
beings who heard this
would develop doubts and confusion.
Now, this Fùlóunà,
throughout the past with thousands of billions of Buddhas, diligently cultivated the path he walked,
protected and proclaimed the Buddha Dharma.
For the sake of seeking supreme wisdom,
he appeared among the Buddhas
as a foremost disciple,
learned and wise.
His teachings are fearless,
and he can bring joy to the multitude;
he has never been weary or indolent,
fully supporting Buddha deeds.
He has already attained great supernatural powers,
perfected the four unobstructed knowledges,
knows the sharpness and dullness of faculties,
and always preaches pure Dharma.
He expands on such meanings,
teaching thousands of billions in the assembly,
enabling them to remain in the Mahāyāna Dharma,
and himself purifying the Buddha land.
In the future he will also venerate and make offerings
to numberless Buddhas,
support, proclaim, and uphold the true Dharma,
and likewise purify his own Buddha land.
Always with skillful means,
fearlessly preaching the Dharma,
he ferries and saves countless beings,
perfecting all-encompassing wisdom.
He venerates the Tathāgatas,
and upholds the treasury of the Dharma jewel.
Subsequently, he shall attain Buddhahood,
with the name Fǎmíng.
His land is named Shànjìng,
composed of the seven treasures,
and the kalpa is called Bǎomíng.
The Bodhisattva multitude will be extremely numerous,
incalculable in number,
all having attained great supernatural powers,
perfectly endowed with majestic virtue and strength,
filling the whole Buddha land.
The Śrāvakā assembly will also be numberless,
with the three insights and eight liberations,
attaining the four unobstructed knowledges,
serving as the Saṃgha community.
The living beings of that land
will have completely cut off lustful desires,
purely born by transformation,
adorned with perfect marks on their bodies.
Their food is Dharma joy and meditative delight,
with no thought of other food.
There will be no women,
nor any evil destinies.
Bhikṣu Fùlóunà,
with all merit perfectly accomplished,
will obtain that pure land,
with a multitude of sages and saints.
Of such countless matters,
I now merely speak briefly.
Then, the one thousand two hundred Arhats who were at ease in mind had this thought:
“How wonderful and unprecedented this joy of ours!
If the World-Honored One would give each of us a prophecy as he does for the great disciples,
would this not be delightful indeed!”
The Buddha, knowing the thoughts in their minds,
said to Mahākāśyapa,
“These one thousand two hundred Arhats,
I shall now, before all, bestow on them, in order, the prophecy of Anuttarā Samyak-saṃbodhi.
Among this assembly,
my great disciple Jiāochénrú Bhikṣu,
will make offerings to sixty-two thousand billion Buddhas,
and then will become a Buddha,

with the title Pǔmíng Tathāgata, Worthy of Offerings, Perfectly Omniscient, Possessed of Wisdom and Practice, Well Gone, Knower of the World, Supreme Person, Tamer of Beings, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, World-Honored One.
As for the five hundred Arhats:
Yóulóupínluó Jiāshè, Jiāyé Jiāshè, Nàtí Jiāshè,
Jiālióutuóyí, Yóutuóyí, Ānlóutúo, Lípóduō, Jiébīnnà,
Bójiūluó, Zhōutuó, Shājiātuó and so on,
all will attain Anuttarā Samyak-saṃbodhi,
with the same title,
called Pǔmíng.”
At that time, the World-Honored One,
wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse, saying:
“Jiāochénrú Bhikṣu,
shall see measureless Buddhas,
and after Asaṃkhyeya kalpas have passed,
shall then attain perfect enlightenment.
Ever radiating great light,
fully possessed of all spiritual powers,
his name will be known throughout the ten directions,
receiving universal reverence,
constantly preaching the supreme path,
therefore called Pǔmíng.
His Buddha land will be pure,
with Bodhisattvas all courageous and vigorous,
all ascending wondrous pavilions,
traveling through the lands of the ten directions,
bringing unsurpassed offerings
to the Buddhas.
Having made such offerings,
with hearts full of great joy,
they will instantly return to their own land,
having such spiritual power.
The Buddha’s lifespan will be sixty thousand kalpas,
and the true Dharma will endure twice as long,
the semblance Dharma again twice as that,
and when the Dharma perishes, gods and humans will grieve.
Those five hundred Bhikṣus
shall also, in turn, become Buddhas,
all sharing the title Pǔmíng,
receiving prophecies in succession.
After my extinction,
a certain person, Jiǎ, will become a Buddha;
the world he transforms
will also be as it is for me today.
The adornment and purity of the land,
as well as the various powers of miraculous abilities,
the assembly of Bodhisattvas and Śrāvakas,
the True Dharma and the Counterfeit Dharma,
and the number of kalpas for their lifespans—
all will be as stated above.
Kāśyapa, you already know;
of the five hundred self-masters,
and the other assemblies of Śrāvakas,
it shall also be thus for them again.
For those not present at this assembly,
you should expound this to them.
At that time, the five hundred Arhats
having received predictions before the Buddha,
were filled with joy and exultation,
immediately rose from their seats, approached the Buddha,
bowed their heads and paid homage at his feet,
confessed and reproached themselves:
“Bhagavān! We have always thought thus,
each believing we had attained final extinction.
Now we realize it, as if we had no wisdom.
Why is this?
We ought to have attained the Tathāgata’s wisdom,
yet contented ourselves with lesser wisdom.
Bhagavān! Like one who goes to a close friend’s house and, drunken, lies down to sleep.
At that time, the close friend has official business to attend,
and, tying a priceless jewel in the hem of his clothing, gives it to him and departs.
That man, sleeping in his drunkenness, is utterly unaware.
Upon arising, he wanders to another country.
For food and clothing,
he labors diligently to seek, undergoing great hardship;
if he obtains even a little, he considers it sufficient.
Later, his close friend happens to meet him,
and speaks to him, saying:
‘Alas, good man!
Why do you toil to this extent for food and clothing?
Long ago I wished you to attain ease and enjoy the five desires at will;
on such-and-such year, day, month,
I tied a priceless jewel into the hem of your robe.
Even now it remains there,
yet you do not know it.
Tiring yourself with hardship and worry to sustain your life,
truly, this is folly.
Now, with this jewel, you may trade for whatever you require,
always obtain your desire, lacking nothing.’
So it is, too, with the Buddha;
when he was a Bodhisattva, he taught and transformed us,
causing us to aspire to the mind of omniscience.
But soon after, we forgot, unknowing and unaware.
Having attained the Arhat path,
we considered ourselves extinguished;
struggling to sustain our lives,
finding little and thinking it sufficient.
Yet the aspiration for omniscience remains, not lost.
Now the Bhagavān awakens us,
saying:
‘O Bhikṣus!
What you have attained is not ultimate extinction.
For a long time have I enabled you to plant the roots of good for Buddhahood,
through expedient means manifesting the aspect of nirvāṇa,
while you
took this to be true extinction.’
Bhagavān!
Now I know
that truly I am a Bodhisattva,
and have received the prediction of Anuttarā Samyaksaṃbodhi.
By this cause and condition, we are greatly joyful, as never before.”
Then Ānanda Kāuṭinya and the others,
wishing to reiterate this meaning, spoke in verse:
Hearing the unsurpassed, secure prediction bestowed,
we are filled with unprecedented joy,
and pay homage to the Buddha of boundless wisdom.
Now before the Bhagavān,
we repent our manifold faults,
among measureless Buddha-treasures,
having gained a fraction of nirvāṇa,
like unwise and foolish men,
and considered ourselves fulfilled.
It is as a poor and destitute man
who goes to a close friend’s house;
the house is extremely wealthy,
replete with all kinds of delicacies;
a priceless jewel
is tied inside his garment,
quietly given, then the host departs;
while he sleeps, he is unaware.
When the man awakens,
he travels to another country,
seeking food and clothing to sustain himself,
struggling with much hardship,
finding little, thinking it enough,
never wishing for better things.
He does not realize within his garment
there is a priceless jewel.
Later, the close friend meets this poor man,
after bitterly reproaching him,
shows him the jewel that was tied there.
When the poor man sees the jewel,
his heart is filled with vast joy;
he becomes rich with all possessions,
and indulges freely in the five desires.
So it is for us as well;
the Bhagavān, through long kalpas,
has constantly pitied, shown, and instructed us,
enabling us to plant the unsurpassed aspiration.
Because of our lack of wisdom,
we did not realize nor know it,
having gained but a fraction of nirvāṇa,
thinking it sufficient, seeking nothing more.
Now the Buddha has awakened us,
saying, it is not true extinction;
by attaining the Buddha’s unsurpassed wisdom
one then achieves true extinction.
Now we have heard from the Buddha
the prediction of splendid adornment,
and in turn receive this assurance;
our bodies and minds are full of joy.
Then Ānanda and Rāhula reflected thus:
“We often think to ourselves:
‘If only we could receive prediction, how delightful that would be!’”
Immediately, they rose from their seats,
approached the Buddha, bowed their heads to the feet,
and together addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Bhagavān!
We, too, should have a share in this;
only the Tathāgata is our refuge.
Moreover, we are recognized in the whole world of gods, humans, and asuras:—
Ānanda is ever the attendant, guardian of the Dharma treasury;
Rāhula is the Buddha’s son—
if the Buddha would now give the prediction of Anuttarā Samyaksaṃbodhi,
our own wishes would be fulfilled and the hopes of the multitude satisfied.”
At that time, two thousand disciples, learned and beyond learning,
also rose from their seats, bared their right shoulders, and approached the Buddha;
single-mindedly joined palms, gazed reverently at the Bhagavān,
and, like Ānanda and Rāhula, expressed the same wish,
standing in attendance to one side.
Then the Buddha said to Ānanda:
“In a future existence you will become a Buddha,

named Shān Hǎi Huì Zìzài Tōngwáng Tathāgata, Worthy of Offerings, Perfect Enlightenment, Complete in Wisdom and Conduct, Well-Gone, World-Knower, Unexcelled Man, Tamer, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, Bhagavān.
You will worship sixty-two billion Buddhas, guardians of the Dharma treasury,
and then attain Anuttarā Samyaksaṃbodhi.
You shall transform twenty thousand myriad koṭis of Ganges sands of Bodhisattvas,
causing them to attain Anuttarā Samyaksaṃbodhi.
The country will be called Chánglì Shèngfān,
and its land will be pure, with lapis lazuli as ground.
The kalpa will be named Miàoyīn Biànmǎn.
The Buddha’s lifespan there
shall be measureless thousands of millions of asaṃkhyeya kalpas;
even if one were to calculate for thousands of millions of uncountable asaṃkhyeya kalpas, it could not be known.
The True Dharma will abide in that world twice the Buddha’s lifespan, and the Counterfeit Dharma twice that.
Ānanda!
This Shān Hǎi Huì Zìzài Tōngwáng Buddha
will be praised and revered by Buddhas as countless as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions,
renowned for his virtuous merits.”
Then the Bhagavān
wishing to reiterate this meaning,
spoke in verse:
Now, among the saṅgha I proclaim,
Ānanda the protector of the Dharma
shall worship all Buddhas
and then attain perfect awakening,
to be called: Shān Hǎi Huì
Zìzài Tōngwáng Buddha.
His country will be pure,
named Chánglì Shèngfān;
he will teach and guide Bodhisattvas,
as numerous as Ganges sands.
This Buddha will possess great virtue,
and his fame will fill the ten directions.
His lifespan cannot be measured;
out of compassion for living beings,
the True Dharma will last twice his lifespan,
and the Counterfeit Dharma twice that.
As numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
measureless sentient beings
will sow the causes of the Buddha-path
in this Buddha’s Dharma.”
At that time, among the gathered assembly, eight thousand newly resolved Bodhisattvas
all thought thus:
“We have not even heard such a prediction bestowed upon the great Bodhisattvas;
for what reason
do the Śrāvakas receive such predictions?”
At that time, the World-Honored One
knew the thoughts in the minds of all the bodhisattvas,
and addressed them, saying:
“Noble sons!
Ānán and I,
in the presence of Kong Wáng Fó,
at the same time aroused the aspiration for anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Ānán always delighted in broad learning;
I constantly practiced diligent effort.
Therefore, I have already attained anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi,
while Ānán upholds and protects my Dharma,
also preserving the Dharma treasury of future Buddhas,
teaching and accomplishing the multitude of bodhisattvas;
such was his original vow,
thus he has received this prediction.”
Ānán, facing the Buddha,
hearing the prediction and the adornment of his land,
his wishes fulfilled,
his heart was deeply joyful, attaining what he had never experienced before.
Thereupon he recalled the Dharma treasuries of countless hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddhas of the past,
penetrating them without obstruction, just as he now hears,
and also remembered his original vow.
Then Ānán
spoke in verse, saying:
The World-Honored One is most rare,
causing me to remember the past,
the Dharma of innumerable Buddhas,
just as I hear it today.
Now I have no further doubt,
I abide in the path of the Buddha,
skillfully serve as attendant,
and uphold the Dharma of the Buddhas.
At that time, the Buddha said to Luóhóuluó:
“In the future, you will become a Buddha,

named Dàoqī Bǎohuá Tathāgata, Worthy of Offerings, Perfectly Enlightened, Accomplished in Wisdom and Conduct, Well-Gone, Knower of the World, Supreme Man, Unsurpassed Hero, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, World-Honored One.
You shall make offerings to as many Tathāgatas as there are dust-particles in ten worlds,
always acting as the eldest son to all Buddhas,
just as you do now.
This Dàoqī Bǎohuá Buddha, whose land is adorned,
whose lifespan is countless kalpas,
whose disciples to be transformed,
and whose True and Counterfeit Dharma ages
will be no different from those of Shānhǎi Huìzìzài Tōngwáng Tathāgata,
in which you will also serve as the eldest son of that Buddha.
After that, you will attain anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
At that time, the World-Honored One,
wishing to reiterate this meaning,
spoke in verse:
When I was a prince,
Luóhó was my eldest son;
now that I have attained Buddhahood,
he receives the Dharma as my Dharma son.
In the future,
he shall see innumerable millions of Buddhas,
and serve as their eldest son,
single-mindedly seeking the Buddha path.
The secret practices of Luóhóluó
only I am able to know;
now he appears as my eldest son,
to demonstrate for sentient beings.
Countless hundreds of thousands and millions,
their merit is beyond reckoning,
abiding in the Buddha’s Dharma,
seeking unsurpassed enlightenment.
At that time, the World-Honored One
saw two thousand of the learners and those beyond learning, their minds gentle, serene, and pure, single-mindedly contemplating the Buddha.
The Buddha said to Ānán:
“Do you see these two thousand, learners and accomplished ones?”
“Yes, I have seen them.”
“Ānán!
These people,
will make offerings to as many Tathāgatas as there are dust-particles in fifty worlds,
showing reverence and honor,
upholding the Dharma Treasury.
At the end, at the same time, each in lands throughout the ten directions, will attain Buddhahood,
all bearing the same title,
named Bǎoxiàng Tathāgata, Worthy of Offerings, Perfectly Enlightened,
Accomplished in Wisdom and Conduct, Well-Gone, Knower of the World, Supreme Man, Unsurpassed Hero, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha,
World-Honored One.
Their lifespan shall be one kalpa.
Their lands will be adorned, with śrāvakas and bodhisattvas, True Dharma
and Counterfeit Dharma, all equal and undifferentiated.”
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to reiterate this meaning,
spoke in verse:
These two thousand śrāvakas
now abide before me;
to all I bestow prediction
that in the future they will become Buddhas.
The Buddhas whom they worship
shall be as numerous as aforementioned dust-particles;
upholding their Dharma treasuries,
afterward they shall attain perfect enlightenment.
Each in lands of the ten directions
will all bear the same title,
and simultaneously sit at the enlightenment seat,
realizing unsurpassed wisdom,
all called Bǎoxiàng.
Their lands and disciples,
True Dharma and Counterfeit Dharma,
will all be equal without difference.
All with spiritual powers
will save beings in the ten directions,
their fame pervading everywhere,
gradually entering Nirvāṇa.
Then those two thousand, the learners and the accomplished,
hearing the Buddha’s prediction,
were joyful and jubilant,
and spoke in verse:
The World-Honored One, light of wisdom,
I hear the sound of this prediction,
my heart fills with happiness,
like sweet dew received in abundance.
Then the World-Honored One, for the sake of the Medicine King Bodhisattva,
said to the eighty thousand great beings:
“Yàowáng!
Do you see within this great assembly,
the countless devas, dragon kings, yaksas, gandharvas,
asuras, garudas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans and non-humans,
as well as bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās, those who seek the path of śrāvakas,
those who seek the path of pratyekabuddhas, and those who seek the Buddha way—
all these types,
all before the Buddha,
hearing even a verse or a sentence of the wondrous Dharma Flower Sūtra,
even with a single moment of rejoicing,
I grant predictions to them all:
they shall attain anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi!”
The Buddha said to Yàowáng:
“Again, after the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa,
if someone hears the wondrous Dharma Flower Sūtra,
even a single verse or sentence,
and rejoices even for a moment,
I also grant them prediction for anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Should there be others
who uphold, recite, explain, or copy the wondrous Dharma Flower Sūtra,
even a single verse,
regard the scrolls of this sūtra with respect as if they were the Buddha,
making all kinds of offerings—flowers, incense, necklaces,
finely crushed incense, ointments, burning incense, banners, canopies, flags and pennants, garments, music,
even pressing palms together in reverence.
Yàowáng!
You should know these persons
have already made offerings to hundred thousand millions of Buddhas,
and in the presence of Buddhas have accomplished great vows,
arising in this human world due to their compassion for sentient beings.
Yàowáng!
If someone asks, ‘Which beings, in the future, will become Buddhas?’
You should show that these persons, in future lives, will certainly become Buddhas.
Why?
If a good man or good woman,
towards the Dharma Flower Sūtra, even a single sentence, upholds, recites, explains, or copies it,
and makes various offerings to the sūtra scroll—flowers, incense, necklaces, finely crushed incense, ointments, burning incense, banners, canopies, flags and pennants, garments, music,
and presses palms together reverently;
such a person should be venerated by all the world,
and offerings should be made to them as to a Tathāgata.
You should know that this person is a great bodhisattva,
accomplished in anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi,
pitying sentient beings,
wishing to be born in this world,
broadly proclaiming and distinguishing the wondrous Dharma Flower Sūtra.
How much more so those who can fully uphold and make various offerings!
Yàowáng!
You should know, these people,
although forsaking the retribution of their pure karma,
after my parinirvāṇa,
out of compassion for sentient beings,
are born in this evil world,
proclaiming this sūtra far and wide.
If such good men or good women,
after my parinirvāṇa,
are able to explain the Dharma Flower Sūtra to even one person in secret,
even a single sentence,
you should know that such a person is a messenger of the Tathāgata,
sent by the Tathāgata, carrying out the Tathāgata’s work.
How much more so those who widely explain it to great assemblies!
Yàowáng!
If there are evil people, with unwholesome intent,
who, through one kalpa, appear before the Buddha and continually slander him,
their offense is still slight;
but if someone, with a single evil word,
slanders laypeople or monastics who recite the Dharma Flower Sūtra,
their offense is truly grave.
Yàowáng!
If there is one who reads and recites the *Fǎhuá Jīng*,
you should know that this person adorns himself with the adornments of the Buddha,
and thus shoulders the responsibility borne by the Tathāgata.
In whatever places he goes,
all should bow toward him,
join their palms single-mindedly,
respectfully offer offerings,
honor and praise him with flowers, incense, and necklaces,
powdered incense, anointing incense, burning incense, banners of adorned silk, canopies, flags and pennants, clothing and delicacies, perform various kinds of music,
make the finest offerings among people, and make offerings to him.
One should offer celestial treasures and scatter them,
and gather the most precious things in the heavens to present to him.
And why is that?
Because this person gladly proclaims the Dharma,
and if one hears it even for a moment,
one will immediately attain the ultimate Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi.
At that time, the World-honored One wished to further clarify this meaning,
and spoke in verse:
If one wishes to abide in the Buddha way,
and accomplish innate wisdom,
one should always diligently make offerings
to those who uphold the *Fǎhuá Jīng*.
If there are those who wish to swiftly attain
all-knowledge wisdom,
they should uphold this sūtra
and also make offerings to its upholders.
If there is someone able to uphold
the wondrous *Fǎhuá Jīng*,
you should know this is one sent by the Buddha,
mindful with compassion for all living beings.
Whoever is able to uphold
the wondrous *Fǎhuá Jīng*,
forsakes the pure lands,
and, out of compassion for the masses, is born here.
Know that such a person
is reborn freely as he wishes,
able, in this evil world,
to widely proclaim the supreme Dharma.
Offer him heavenly flowers and incense,
as well as celestial precious garments,
and the most marvelous treasures of the heavens;
make offerings to the one who expounds the Dharma.
In the evil world after my extinction,
whoever is able to uphold this sūtra
should be revered with joined palms,
as if making offerings to the World-honored One.
The finest delicacies and all manner of fine clothing
should be offered to this child of the Buddha,
hoping to hear even for a moment.
If, in future generations,
one is able to uphold this sūtra,
I will send him among people
to carry out the Tathāgata’s work.
Even if, for an entire kalpa,
someone constantly harbors an unwholesome mind,
scowls and reviles the Buddha,
he will incur boundless and weighty offenses.
If one reads, recites, and upholds
this *Fǎhuá Jīng*,
and utters a single harsh word out of momentary anger,
his offense will be even graver than the previous one.
If someone seeks the Buddha way
and, for an entire kalpa,
joins his palms before me
and praises me with countless verses,
by praising the Buddha thus,
he acquires immeasurable merit and virtue, but praising the upholder of the sūtra,
his blessings will surpass even that.
Through eighty billion kalpas,
by offering the most marvelous sights and sounds,
and fragrances, tastes, and touch,
to the upholder of the sūtra,
after making such offerings,
if he is able to hear it even for a moment,
he should rejoice and be glad,
saying, “Now I have gained immense benefit.”
Yàowáng, I now tell you,
among all the sūtras I have preached,
within this sūtra,
the *Fǎhuá* is the very best.
At that time, the Buddha further spoke to Yàowáng Púsà Móhēsà:
The sūtras I have preached are countless millions of billions—
those already preached, being preached now, and to be preached in the future. Among them, this *Fǎhuá Jīng* is the hardest to believe and the hardest to understand.
Yàowáng!
This sūtra is the secret treasury of all Buddhas,
and is not to be dispersed or heedlessly given to others.
It is protected and guarded by all Buddhas, World-honored Ones,
and from the past up to now, it has never been openly preached.
Even now, while the Tathāgata dwells in the world, this sūtra arouses much resentment and jealousy;
how much more so after my extinction?
Yàowáng!
You should know that after the Tathāgata’s extinction,
those able to transcribe, uphold, read, recite, make offerings, and expound it to others,
will be covered by the Tathāgata’s robe,
and will also be protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the present in other worlds.
Such a person possesses great power of faith,
as well as strength of resolve and of wholesome roots.
Know that this person dwells together with the Tathāgata,
and is as if caressed on the head by the hand of the Tathāgata.
Yàowáng!
Wherever and in whatever place—whether it is spoken, read, recited, or written—
wherever the scroll of this sūtra abides, one should erect a stūpa of seven treasures,
making it utmost lofty, spacious, and exquisitely adorned,
without any need to enshrine relics.
And why?
Because here already abides the entire body of the Tathāgata.
This stūpa should be honored with every kind of flower, incense, necklace, silk canopy,
banners, pennants, music, and hymns, offered with reverence,
respect, and praise.
If there are those who see such a stūpa, worship it, and make offerings,
you should know that they are all close to attaining Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi.
Yàowáng!
There are many people, whether householders
or those who have left home to practice the bodhisattva path. If they cannot see, hear, read, recite, copy, or uphold,
or make offerings to this *Fǎhuá Jīng*, you should know that such people have not skillfully practiced the bodhisattva path;
but if there are those who hear this sūtra, they are truly able to carry out the bodhisattva way.
If there are living beings seeking the Buddha way, whether they see or hear this *Fǎhuá Jīng*,
and upon hearing it believe, understand, accept, and uphold it, you should know that such people are close to Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi.
Yàowáng!
It is like someone parched and desperately needing water,
who digs for it upon a high plain,
yet still sees only dry earth and knows that water is far away;
but if he perseveres without giving up,
he begins to see damp soil,
and then gradually reaches mud,
his mind becoming certain
that water is now near.
So it is with the bodhisattva;
if he has not yet heard, understood,
nor is able to practice the *Fǎhuá Jīng*,
know that he is still far from Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi;
but if he hears, understands, reflects upon, and practices it,
he should know for certain that he is close to Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi.
And why is that?
The Anuttarā-Samyak-Saṃbodhi of all bodhisattvas belongs to this sūtra.
This sūtra opens the expedient gates and shows the true aspect.
This treasury of the *Fǎhuá Jīng* is deep, firm, remote, and mysterious, and none can reach it;
now the Buddha teaches and transforms, perfects bodhisattvas and reveals it to them.
Yàowáng!
If there are bodhisattvas who, upon hearing this *Fǎhuá Jīng*,
feel startled, doubtful, or fearful,
know that they are recently resolved bodhisattvas;
if the voice-hearers hear this sūtra
and feel startled, doubtful, or fearful,
know that these are those possessed of arrogant pride.
Yàowáng!
If there are good men or good women,
after the Tathāgata’s extinction,
who wish to expound the *Fǎhuá Jīng* for the fourfold assembly,
how should they do so?
Such good men and women should enter the Tathāgata’s chamber,
put on the Tathāgata’s robe, and sit on the Tathāgata’s seat;
only then should they widely expound this sūtra for the fourfold assembly.
The Tathāgata’s chamber is
the great mind of compassion among all living beings;
the Tathāgata’s robe is the gentle and patient mind;
the Tathāgata’s seat is the emptiness of all dharmas.
Stabilized in these,
then, with an indolence-free mind,
one should expound this *Fǎhuá Jīng* broadly to bodhisattvas and the fourfold assembly.
“Yàowáng!
In other lands, I send conjured people to assemble an audience to hear the Dharma,
and conjured bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās to listen to the preaching.
These conjured people, on hearing the Dharma, believe, accept, and follow without going against it.
If the preacher is in a secluded place,
I greatly dispatch devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, and so forth, to listen to the Dharma.
Even though I am in another country,
from time to time I enable the preacher to see my body.
If they forget or lose a phrase or passage of this sūtra, I return to teach it again,
so that they gain completeness.”
At that time, the World-honored One, wishing to further clarify this meaning,
spoke in verse:
If one wishes to cast off all laziness,
one should listen to this sūtra,
for this sūtra is hard to hear,
and it is also hard to believe and accept.
Like someone parched and needing water,
who digs on a high plain,
at first seeing only dry and parched earth,
knowing water is still far away;
gradually seeing damp earth and mud,
he is certain that water is near.
Yàowáng, you should know!
Likewise, all such people
who do not hear the *Fǎhuá Jīng*
are far indeed from the wisdom of the Buddha;
but those who hear this profound sūtra
will firmly resolve the way of the voice-hearers.
This is the king of all sūtras;
after hearing, deeply reflect,
and know that these people
are near to the wisdom of the Buddha.
If a person expounds this sūtra,
