"As the World-Honored One has instructed, we shall completely carry it out.
Yes, World-Honored One! We wish the World-Honored One not to worry."
The great assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas repeated thus three times,
and together voiced these words:
"As the World-Honored One has instructed, we shall completely carry it out.
Yes, World-Honored One! We wish the World-Honored One not to worry."
At that time, Shìjiāmóuní Fó ordered the various emanated Buddhas from the ten directions to return to their original lands,
and spoke these words:
"Budhas may each dwell where they are at ease,
and let Duōbǎo Fó’s stūpa be as before."
When these words were spoken,
the immeasurable emanated Buddhas from the ten directions—who sat beneath treasure trees upon lion seats—
and Duōbǎo Fó,
together with Wàng Xíng Bōdísà and the boundless asamkhyeyas of Bodhisattva assemblies,
and the fourfold assembly of śrāvakas, headed by Shèlìfú,
and all heavenly beings, humans, asuras, etc.,
upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching,
were all greatly rejoiced.
Then Sù Wáng Huá Púsà respectfully addressed the Buddha:
"World-Honored One!
How does Yàowáng Púsà travel in the Sahā world?
World-Honored One!
Has this Yàowáng Púsà undergone innumerable hundreds of thousands of millions of nayuta difficult ascetic practices?
Excellent, World-Honored One!
I pray you explain and clarify a little."
The gods, dragons, spirits, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras,
garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans and non-humans,
the other Bodhisattvas who had come from other lands, and the śrāvaka assembly there,
all heard this and rejoiced.
Then the Buddha said to Sù Wáng Huá Púsà:
"In the inconceivably distant past, over immeasurable Ganges sands of kalpas,
there was a Buddha named Rìyuè Jìngmíngdé Tathāgata,
Worthy of Offerings, Perfect in Omniscience,
Accomplished in Wisdom and Conduct, Well Gone, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer, Teacher of gods and humans, Buddha, World-Honored One.
That Buddha had eighty billion great Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas
and an assembly of śrāvakas as numerous as seventy-two Ganges rivers of sands.
The Buddha's lifespan was forty-two thousand kalpas,
and the lifespans of the Bodhisattvas were likewise so.
That land had no women, no hell-beings, hungry ghosts, animals, asuras, etc.,
nor any disasters;
the ground was as level as the palm of a hand,
composed of lapis lazuli, adorned with jeweled trees,
with canopies of precious banners above,
hung with jeweled flower-streamers,
precious vases and censers throughout the land,
terraces made of the seven treasures,
one tree for each terrace,
each tree distant from its terrace exactly one arrow's flight.
Under each of these jeweled trees, sat Bodhisattvas and śrāvakas.
On top of each jeweled terrace, there were a hundred million devas playing divine music,
singing and praising the Buddha as an offering.
Then that Buddha, for the sake of Yīqièzhòngshēn Xǐjiàn Púsà,
the other Bodhisattvas and śrāvakas,
expounded the Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra.
This Yīqièzhòngshēn Xǐjiàn Púsà delighted in practicing asceticism,
and under the Dharma of Rìyuè Jìngmíngdé Fó,
diligently walked in meditation,
single-mindedly seeking Buddhahood; after twelve thousand years,
he attained the samādhi of manifesting all forms.
Having attained this samādhi,
his heart was filled with great joy, and he thought:
'I have attained the samādhi of manifesting all forms, all due to the power of hearing the Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra;
I shall now make offerings to Rìyuè Jìngmíngdé Fó and the Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra.'
Immediately he entered this samādhi,
in empty space it rained mandāra flowers, great mandāra flowers,
finely powdered, firm and black candana,
filling the sky, falling down like clouds,
and also rained incense from the other shore of the sea—
this incense weighed six liǎng and was worth as much as the Sahā world—
as an offering to the Buddha.
After making this offering,
he arose from samādhi and thought:
'Though I used spiritual powers to make offerings to the Buddha,
it is not as good as making an offering with my own body.'
Immediately he applied all fragrant substances—candana, agarwood, turushka, pīlìjiī, aloeswood, gum incense,
and drank perfume oil made from champaka flowers
for twelve hundred years,
covered his body with fragrant oil,
and before Rìyuè Jìngmíngdé Fó,
wrapped himself in divine precious garments,
poured fragrant oil over himself,
and by means of the power of his vow, his body became naturally luminous,
radiating light everywhere throughout eighty billion Ganges rivers of worlds.
Among them, all the Buddhas simultaneously praised him, saying:
'Excellent! Excellent! Good man!
This is true diligence;
this is the true Dharma-offering to the Tathāgata.
Even offerings of flowers, incense, necklaces, burning incense, powdered incense,
spreading incense, divine fabrics, banners, canopies, and incense from the far shore of the sea—
even offerings of all such things,
cannot surpass this;
even if lands, cities, wife and children were given away,
that could not compare.
Good man! This is the foremost giving,
supreme among all almsgiving,
because it is the Dharma-offering to the Tathāgatas.'"
After these words were spoken, everyone fell silent.
His body was enveloped in flames for one thousand two hundred years;
after this had passed,
his body was then entirely consumed.
"When all sentient beings rejoiced to see the Bodhisattva make such an offering of Dharma,
and after their lives ended,
they were reborn in the land of Rìyuè Jìngmíngdé Fó,
sitting cross-legged in the royal family of Jìngdé Wáng,
suddenly born by transformation.
Then, for the sake of his father, he spoke a verse, saying:
'Great King, you must now know,
when I practiced there,
I immediately obtained all the manifestations of the samādhi of revealing all bodies.
Diligently practicing great vigor,
abandoning the body I loved,
I made offerings to the World-Honored One
in quest of unsurpassed wisdom.'
After reciting this verse,
he addressed his father, saying:
'Rìyuè Jìngmíngdé Fó is still present in the world.
I have previously made offerings to the Buddha,
and have obtained the dhāraṇī of understanding all sentient beings' languages.
I have further heard the Lotus Sūtra, eight hundred thousand myriads of koṭis and nayutas of verses such as Jīnjiāluó, Pínpóluó, and Āchùpó.
Great King! I shall now return to make offerings to this Buddha.'
Having said this, he immediately sat upon the seven-jeweled platform,
rose into the air, ascending to the height of seven Tāla trees,
went to where the Buddha was,
bowed with his head at the Buddha's feet,
joined his ten fingers,
and with verses praised the Buddha:
'Your form is exceedingly marvelous,
radiant light shines throughout the ten directions.
I previously made offerings,
now again I come in person to venerate you.'
At that time, when all sentient beings rejoiced to see the Bodhisattva had finished reciting this verse,
they said to the Buddha:
'World-Honored One! The World-Honored One still abides in the world.'
At that time, Rìyuè Jìngmíngdé Fó
addressed Yīqiè Zhòngshēng Xǐ Jiàn Púsà:
'Good son! My time for nirvāṇa has come,
the extinction will soon arrive.
You ought to prepare beds and seats,
for tonight I shall enter parinirvāṇa.'
He further instructed Yīqiè Zhòngshēng Xǐ Jiàn Púsà:
'Good son! I entrust the Buddha Dharma to you and all the great Bodhisattva disciples,
along with the teaching of Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.
I also give to you the three thousand great thousand worlds adorned with treasures, jeweled platforms, and the attendant deities;
I completely entrust these to you.
After my parinirvāṇa, all my relics I also entrust to you;
you should cause them to be distributed and widely venerated,
and erect many thousands of stupas.'
Having thus instructed Yīqiè Zhòngshēng Xǐ Jiàn Púsà, Rìyuè Jìngmíngdé Fó
entered nirvāṇa after the night had passed.
At that time, when Yīqiè Zhòngshēng Xǐ Jiàn Púsà saw the Buddha's extinction,
they were grieved and distressed,
longing yearnfully for the Buddha;
they then used pāṭalika sandalwood from this side of the ocean as firewood, offering it to the Buddha's body, and burned it.
After the fire was extinguished,
they gathered up the relics,
made eighty-four thousand jeweled reliquaries,
using them to erect eighty-four thousand stupas,
each three worlds high,
with finials beautifully adorned,
hung with banners and canopies, suspending jeweled bells.
At that time, Yīqiè Zhòngshēng Xǐ Jiàn Púsà again thought to himself:
'Although I have made these offerings,
my heart is still unsatisfied;
I will now make further offerings to the relics.'
He then addressed the great Bodhisattva disciples and the assembly of gods, dragons,
yaksas, and all the multitude:
'All of you should single-mindedly contemplate;
I will now make offerings to the relics of Rìyuè Jìngmíngdé Fó.'
After saying this,
he stood before the eighty-four thousand stupas and burned his arm adorned with a hundred merits
for seventy-two thousand years as an offering,
causing innumerable seekers of the Śrāvaka path, countless asaṃkhyeya beings,
to give rise to the aspiration for Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi,
and all to attain the samādhi of manifesting all forms of bodies.
Then all the Bodhisattvas, gods, humans, and asuras,
saw he was without arms,
and, distressed with sorrow, said:
'This Yīqiè Zhòngshēng Xǐ Jiàn Púsà is our teacher,
the one who taught and transformed us,
yet now he has burned his arms,
leaving his body incomplete.'
At that time, Yīqiè Zhòngshēng Xǐ Jiàn Púsà, in the midst of the great assembly, made this vow:
'For relinquishing my two arms,
I shall surely obtain a golden-colored Buddha body.
If this is truly not false,
may my two arms be restored as before.'
After making this vow,
they were naturally restored,
brought about by the profound merit and wisdom of this Bodhisattva.
At that time, the three thousand great thousand worlds quaked in six ways,
heavenly flowers of treasures rained down,
and all gods and humans experienced unprecedented wonders."
The Buddha addressed Sù Wánghuá Púsà:
"What do you think?
Was Yīqiè Zhòngshēng Xǐ Jiàn Púsà a different person?
He is now Yàowáng Púsà.
The bodies he relinquished as offerings
were thus numberless, hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas.
Sù Wánghuá!
If someone arouses the thought to attain Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi,
and can burn a finger, even a toe,
to make offerings to a Buddha-stūpa,

this surpasses offering one’s country and cities, wife and children, and even the mountains, forests, rivers, pools, and treasured possessions of the three thousand great thousand realms as offerings;
and if someone should fill the three thousand great thousand worlds with the seven treasures and offer them to a Buddha,
as well as to great Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Arhats,
the merit they would attain is not equal to upholding this Lotus Sūtra,
even as little as four lines of verse.
Their blessing is the greatest.
Sù Wánghuá!
Just as among all rivers and streams,
the ocean is the greatest of the waters;
so too, this Lotus Sūtra,
among all the sutras spoken by the Tathāgatas, is the deepest and greatest.
Again, like among earth mountains, Black Mountain, the Lesser Iron Ring, the Great Iron Ring, and the ten jeweled mountains,
of all these mountains,
Mount Sumeru is the greatest;
so too, this Lotus Sūtra,
among all scriptures, is supreme.
Again, among all the stars,
the Moon Deva is supreme;
so too, this Lotus Sūtra,
among hundreds of thousands of myriads of scripture teachings, is the most illuminating.
Again, just as the Sun Deva can dispel all darkness;
likewise, this Sūtra can dispel all unwholesome darkness.
Again, among minor kings, the Wheel-turning Sage King is supreme;
so too, this Sūtra, among all scriptures, is the most esteemed.
Again, just as Śakra is the lord among the Trāyastriṃśa devas;
so too, this Sūtra is the king among scriptures.
Again, just as the great Brahmā King is the father of all beings;
so too, this Sūtra is the father of all sages and saints, learners, those beyond learning, and all who give rise to the mind of a Bodhisattva.
Again, among all ordinary people, Śrota-āpanna, Sakṛdāgāmin, Anāgāmin, Arhat, and Pratyekabuddha are the highest;
likewise, this Sūtra, whether spoken by a Tathāgata, a Bodhisattva, or a Śrāvaka,
among all scriptures and teachings, is the foremost.
One who can uphold this scripture is also likewise, among all beings, supreme.
Among all Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, the Bodhisattva is the highest;
so too, this Sūtra, among all scriptures and teachings, is the highest.
Just as the Buddha is King of all Dharmas; so too, this Sūtra is king among all scriptures.
Sù Wánghuá!
This Sūtra is able to save all sentient beings;
this Sūtra can cause all sentient beings to be free from suffering and affliction;
this Sūtra can greatly benefit all sentient beings,
completely fulfilling their aspirations.
Like a cool pond able to quench the thirst of all who lack water,
like the cold gaining fire,
like the naked gaining clothing,
like merchants finding a leader,
like a child finding a mother,
like a traveler obtaining a boat,
like the sick finding a healer,
like the dark acquiring a lamp,
like the poor finding treasures,
like the people gaining a king,
like a merchant finding the sea,
like a torch dispelling darkness;
so too, this Lotus Sūtra,
can cause sentient beings to be free from all suffering and pain,
able to untie all the bonds of birth and death.
If someone hears this Lotus Sūtra,
writes it themselves or has others write it,
the merit thus acquired, measured with Buddha-wisdom, is boundless.
If one writes out this sūtra,
and offers flowers, incense, necklaces, burning incense, powdered incense, ointment incense, banners, canopies, and robes,
as well as various lamps—ghee lamps, oil lamps, all kinds of fragrant oil lamps,
candana oil lamps, sumana oil lamps, balālaka oil lamps, pāriśika oil lamps, navamālikā oil lamps—
the merit gained is also immeasurable.
Sù Wánghuá!
If anyone hears this "Account of the Past Deeds of the Medicine King Bodhisattva" chapter,
they too will acquire immeasurable, boundless merit.
If any woman hears this "Account of the Past Deeds of the Medicine King Bodhisattva" chapter,
and is able to uphold it,
she will exhaust her female form,
and will not receive it again.
If in the future, five hundred years after the passing of the Tathāgata,
there is any woman who hears this scripture,
and cultivates in accordance with it,
at the end of her present life,
she will be immediately reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss,
with Āmítuófó and the great assembly of Bodhisattvas surrounding her abode,
born within a lotus flower, upon a jeweled seat,
no longer troubled by greed and desire,
nor by anger, stupidity,
nor again by pride, jealousy, or any defilement,
attaining the Bodhisattva’s spiritual powers and the forbearance of the unarisen Dharma.
After attaining this forbearance,
her faculty of sight will be purified,
and with this purified faculty of sight,
she will see seven million two thousand koṭis nayutas Ganges-sands in number of Buddhas, the Tathāgatas.
At that time, all the Buddhas praised from afar, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! Good man!
You are able, within the Dharma of Shìjiā Móuní Fó,
to uphold, recite, and contemplate this sūtra,
and to explain it to others.
The merit and virtue you obtain is immeasurable and boundless;
fire cannot burn it, water cannot wash it away.
Your merit, even if explained together by a thousand Buddhas, cannot be exhausted.
Now you are already able to vanquish all demonic thieves,
destroy the army of saṃsāra,
and utterly crush and eliminate all remaining resentful enemies.
Good man!
Hundreds of thousands of Buddhas by their supernatural powers all protect you.
Among gods and humans in all the world, there is no one like you,
except for the Tathāgata.
As for the various Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and even Bodhisattvas,
in wisdom and meditative absorption, none are your equal."
Sù Wáng Huá!
This Bodhisattva thus accomplishes the power of such merit and wisdom.
If there are people who hear this chapter on the former deeds of the Bodhisattva Yàowáng,
and are able to rejoice and praise it,
these people, in their present lifetime, will always emit the fragrance of blue lotus flowers from their mouths,
and from every pore on their bodies, the scent of ox-head candana will constantly arise.
The merit they obtain is as described above.
Therefore, Sù Wáng Huá!
Entrust this chapter on the former deeds of the Bodhisattva Yàowáng to you.
In the five hundred years after my extinction,
extensively propagate and circulate it in the world of Yánfútí,
and do not let it be cut off,
so that evil demons, demon people, gods, dragons, yaksas, kūbhanḍas, and so on do not find an opportunity.
Sù Wáng Huá!
You should, by the power of your supernatural abilities, protect this sūtra.
Why is this?
This sūtra is the good medicine for illness among the people of Yánfútí.
If people are ill and hear this sūtra,
their illnesses will then vanish, and they will neither age nor die.
Sù Wáng Huá!
If you see someone upholding this sūtra,
you should take powdered incense in a dish of blue lotus flowers
and scatter it as an offering upon that person.
After scattering,
give rise to this thought, saying:
'This person will soon sit upon the grass in the place of awakening,
vanquish all demonic armies,
sound the Dharma conch and beat the great Dharma drum,
and rescue all beings from the sea of aging, sickness, and death.'
Therefore, those who seek the Buddha Way, upon seeing someone upholding this scripture,
should thus give rise to a respectful mind."
When this chapter on the former deeds of the Bodhisattva Yàowáng was taught,
eighty-four thousand Bodhisattvas attained the dhāraṇī of understanding all sentient beings' languages.
Duōbǎo Tathāgata, within the jeweled stūpa, praised the Bodhisattva Sù Wáng Huá, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! Sù Wáng Huá!
You have accomplished inconceivable merit,
such that you can question Shìjiā Móuní Fó about such matters,
bringing benefit to boundless sentient beings."
The Wondrous Dharma Lotus Sūtra, Scroll Six
The Wondrous Dharma Lotus Sūtra, Scroll Seven
Translated under imperial order by the Tripiṭaka Master of the Kingdom of Kuizhi in Later Qin,
Jīumóluóshí
At that time, Shìjiā Móuní Fó emitted great light from the flesh-crown mark,
and also emitted the white curled hair light from between his brows,
shining everywhere throughout one hundred and eighty million nayutas of Buddha worlds in the east, as many as the sands of the Ganges River.
Beyond this number, there was a world named Jìngguāng Zhuāngyán,
in whose country was a Buddha called Jìng Huá Sù Wáng Zhì Tathāgata,
Worthy of Offerings, Truly Omniscient, Perfect in Conduct and Understanding, Well-Gone, World Knower, Supreme Man,
Trainer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, World-Honored One,
surrounded and venerated by countless and boundless great assemblies of Bodhisattvas as he taught the Dharma.
The white curled hair light of Shìjiā Móuní Fó illumined that country.
Then, in the entire country of Jìngguāng Zhuāngyán,
there was a Bodhisattva named Miào Yīn,
who had long cultivated the roots of many virtues,
made offerings and closely served immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddhas,
and had fully achieved profound wisdom.
He had obtained the Samādhi of Wondrous Banner Appearance, the Lotus Sūtra Samādhi, the Samādhi of Pure Virtue,
the Sù Wáng Play Samādhi, the Samādhi of Non-Condition, the Samādhi of the Seal of Wisdom,
the Samādhi of Understanding All Living Beings' Languages,
the Samādhi of Gathering All Merits, the Samādhi of Purity,
the Samādhi of Supernatural Play,
the Samādhi of Wisdom Torch, the Samādhi of Majestic Adornment King,
the Samādhi of Pure Radiance, the Samādhi of Pure Storehouse,
the Samādhi of Non-Duality, the Samādhi of Sun Revolution,
and thus hundreds of thousands of millions of samādhis as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River.
The light of Shìjiā Móuní Fó shone upon his body,
whereupon he addressed Jìng Huá Sù Wáng Zhì Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One! I shall go to the Saha World, to make obeisance and draw near,
and make offerings to Shìjiā Móuní Fó,
and to meet Mañjushrī Dharmarāja Son Bodhisattva,
Yàowáng Bodhisattva,
Yǒngshī Bodhisattva,
Sù Wáng Huá Bodhisattva,
Shàng Xíng Yì Bodhisattva,
Zhuāngyán Wáng Bodhisattva,
Yàoshàng Bodhisattva."
At that time, Jìng Huá Sù Wáng Zhì Buddha spoke to Miào Yīn Bodhisattva:
"Do not look down upon that world or give rise to thoughts of inferiority.
Good man! That Saha World is uneven, with hills and valleys,
it is full of earth and stones and foulness,
and the Buddha's body there is lowly and small, and the community of Bodhisattvas are likewise of small stature.
But your body is forty-two thousand yojanas tall,
while mine is six million eight hundred thousand yojanas;
your body is most upright,
meriting hundreds of thousands and millions of blessings,
its radiance and beauty are extraordinary;
therefore, when you go,
do not look down on that world—
not on the Buddha, the Bodhisattvas, nor the land—by giving rise to thoughts of inferiority."
Miào Yīn Bodhisattva addressed his Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One! Now as I go to the Saha World, it is all through the power of the Tathāgata,
the play of the Tathāgata's supernatural might,
and the adornment of the Tathāgata's merit, virtue, and wisdom."
Then Miào Yīn Bodhisattva, without rising from his seat or moving his body,
entered samādhi.
By the power of samādhi,
not far from the Dharma seat at Gṛdhrakūṭa Mountain,
he transformed and produced eighty-four thousand precious lotus flowers,
each with stems of Jambūnada gold,
leaves of silver,
stamens of vajra,
and Utpala jewels as their thrones.
At that time, Mañjushrī Dharmarāja Son saw these lotuses
and said to the Buddha:
"World-Honored One!
For what reason does this auspicious sign manifest first?
There are so many thousands and millions of lotus flowers,
with stems of Jambūnada gold,
leaves of silver,
stamens of vajra,
and Utpala jewels as their thrones."
Then Shìjiā Móuní Fó addressed Mañjushrī:
"This Miào Yīn Bodhisattva-mahāsattva
now wishes to come from the land of Jìng Huá Sù Wáng Zhì Buddha
together with eighty-four thousand Bodhisattvas
in retinue to arrive at this Saha World,
to make offerings and draw near to me,
and also wishing to make offerings and listen to the Lotus Sūtra."
Mañjushrī addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
What are the good roots this Bodhisattva has cultivated?
What merit has he practiced?
Such that he possesses such great supernatural power?
What samādhis does he practice?
Please tell us the names of these samādhis,
we too wish to diligently cultivate them;
by cultivating these samādhis,
we can behold the size and aspect of that Bodhisattva,
his deportment—advancing and withdrawing.
We only beseech the World-Honored One, by his supernatural ability, to cause that Bodhisattva to come,
and let us see him."
Then Shìjiā Móuní Fó told Mañjushrī:
"This long-extinct Duōbǎo Tathāgata
will now reveal his form for your sakes."
At that time, Duōbǎo Buddha told that Bodhisattva:
"Good man! Come, Mañjushrī Dharmarāja Son wishes to see your body."
Then, Miào Yīn Bodhisattva vanished from that land,
together with the eighty-four thousand Bodhisattvas, and set forth.
In every land they passed through, there was a sixfold quaking,
all rained down seven-jeweled lotuses;
hundreds of thousands of heavenly music played spontaneously without being struck.
This Bodhisattva's eyes were like vast leaves of the blue lotus,
and if hundreds of thousands and millions of moons were merged, his countenance would still surpass them in beauty.
His body was of true gold color,
adorned with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of merits,
his majesty and vigor were blazing,
his radiance shining,
his marks fully complete,
like the adamantine frame of Nārāyaṇa.
He entered a seven-jeweled platform,
ascended in the air,
rising to the height of seven Tāla trees from the earth,
surrounded reverently by all the Bodhisattvas,
and thus came to this Saha World, at Gṛdhrakūṭa Mountain.
Having arrived,
he descended from the seven-jeweled platform,
took necklaces worth hundreds of thousands,
carried them to Shìjiā Móuní Fó,
bowed down to his feet with his head,
offered up the necklaces,
and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
Jìng Huá Sù Wáng Zhì Buddha inquires after the World-Honored One,
asking whether you are free of illness and distress,
in good health and at ease,
practicing peacefully,
are your four elements in harmonious balance?
Are worldly affairs bearable?
Are sentient beings easy to save?
Do they not have excessive greed, hatred, delusion, jealousy, and arrogance?
Do they not fail in filial piety toward parents,
lack respect for śramaṇas, harbor wrong views, impure thoughts,
and are they able to restrain the five desires?
World-Honored One!
Can sentient beings subdue the various demonic enemies?
Is the long-extinct Duōbǎo Tathāgata now present in the seven-jeweled stūpa listening to the Dharma?
He also inquires after Duōbǎo Tathāgata:
Is he at peace, free of distress, able to bear to remain long?
World-Honored One!
I now wish to see the body of Duōbǎo Buddha.
I only pray that the World-Honored One will show him to me so that I may behold him."
At that time, Shìjiāmóuní Fó said to Duōbǎo Fó:
“This Miàoyīn Púsà wishes to meet.”
Then Duōbǎo Fó said to Miàoyīn:
“Excellent, excellent!
You are able to come here to make offerings to Shìjiāmóuní Fó, to listen to the Lotus Sūtra, and to see Wénshūshīlì and others.”
At that time, Huádé Púsà addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-honored One!
What wholesome roots has this Miàoyīn Púsà planted,
what merits has he cultivated,
to possess such spiritual power?”
The Buddha told Huádé Púsà:
“In the past, there was a Buddha named Yúnléiyīnwáng Duōtuó Ājiāduó, Āluóhè, Sānmiǎosānfótuó.
The country was called Manifests All Worlds.
The kalpa was named Joyful to See.
For twelve thousand years, Miàoyīn Púsà made offerings of one hundred thousand kinds of music to Yúnléiyīnwáng Fó,
and respectfully presented eighty-four thousand seven-jeweled alms bowls.
As a result of these causes and effects,
he is now reborn in the land of Jìnghuásùwángzhì Fó and has such spiritual power.
Huádé!
What do you think?
At that time, in the assembly of Yúnléiyīnwáng Fó, this Miàoyīn Púsà—the one who made musical offerings and presented precious vessels—
was he anyone else?
This present Miàoyīn Púsà Mahāsattva is the very same.
Huádé!
This Miàoyīn Púsà has already made offerings and drawn close to innumerable Buddhas,
long cultivating the roots of virtue,
encountering hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of Buddhas equal to the sands of the Ganges River.
Huádé!
You see only the body of Miàoyīn Púsà here,
but this bodhisattva manifests various forms everywhere, expounding this sūtra for all beings—
sometimes manifesting as Brahmā,
sometimes as Shakra,
sometimes as the Lord of Freedom,
sometimes as the Great Lord of Freedom,
sometimes as the Celestial General,
sometimes as Vaiśravaṇa Heavenly King,
sometimes as a Wheel-Turning Sage King,
sometimes as various lesser kings,
sometimes as an elder,
sometimes as a layman,
sometimes as a high official,
sometimes as a brāhmaṇa,
sometimes as bhikṣu, bhikṣuṇī, upāsaka, or upāsikā,
sometimes as the wife of an elder or layman,
sometimes as the wife of a high official,
sometimes as the wife of a brāhmaṇa,
sometimes as a young boy or young girl,
sometimes as a celestial, nāga, yasha, gandharva, asura, garuḍa, kinnarā, mahoraga, human or non-human,
to expound this sūtra.
In all hells, among hungry ghosts, animals, and places of suffering,
all can be rescued and delivered.
Even in the king’s inner palace,
he transforms into a female form and expounds this sūtra.
Huádé!
It is Miàoyīn Púsà who is capable of saving the beings of the Sahā World;
Miàoyīn Púsà manifests these various bodies, in this Sahā World,
expounding the sūtra to all sentient beings,
his spiritual powers, transformations, and wisdom lacking nothing.
Using many kinds of wisdom, this bodhisattva shines on the Sahā World,
enabling all beings to attain understanding according to their abilities;
in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions, it is likewise so.
If one can be liberated by means of a śrāvaka form,
he appears as a śrāvaka to expound the Dharma;
if one can be liberated by means of a pratyekabuddha form,
he appears as a pratyekabuddha to expound the Dharma;
if one is to be liberated by a bodhisattva form,
he appears as a bodhisattva and expounds the Dharma;
if one is to be liberated by a Buddha form,
he appears as a Buddha and expounds the Dharma.
In such various ways, following what is required for liberation, he appears in that form,
even to the extent of demonstrating entry into parinirvāṇa for those who require liberation thereby,
manifesting nirvāṇa.
“Huádé!
Miàoyīn Púsà Mahāsattva is perfected in great spiritual powers and wisdom—
his conduct is thus.”
At that time, Huádé Púsà addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-honored One!
This Miàoyīn Púsà has deeply planted wholesome roots.
World-honored One!
In what samādhi does this bodhisattva abide,
that he can thus manifest and transform as needed to liberate beings?”
The Buddha told Huádé Púsà:
“Virtuous man!
That samādhi is called Manifesting All Physical Forms;
Miàoyīn Púsà abides in this samādhi,
and thus can greatly benefit innumerable beings.”
When this chapter about Miàoyīn Púsà was spoken,
the eighty-four thousand who had come together with Miàoyīn Púsà all attained the samādhi of Manifesting All Physical Forms;
and innumerable bodhisattvas of this Sahā World likewise attained this samādhi and dhāraṇī.
Then Miàoyīn Púsà Mahāsattva, after making offerings to Shìjiāmóuní Fó and the Duōbǎo Buddha Stūpa,
returned to his own land,
where every land he passed through experienced six types of tremors,
rained jeweled lotus flowers,
and produced hundreds of thousands of millions of musical performances.
Having returned to his own country,
with eighty-four thousand bodhisattvas
encircling him, he arrived at the place of Jìnghuásùwángzhì Fó,
and said to the Buddha:
“World-honored One!
I visited the Sahā World to benefit beings,
and saw Shìjiāmóuní Fó,
as well as the Duōbǎo Buddha Stūpa,
paying homage and making offerings;
also, I met with Wénshūshīlì, the Dharma Prince Bodhisattva,
as well as with Yàowáng Púsà,
Déqínjīngjìn Lì Púsà,
Yǒngshī Púsà, and others,
and enabled these eighty-four thousand bodhisattvas to attain the samādhi of Manifesting All Physical Forms.
When this section about the coming and going of Miàoyīn Púsà was expounded,
forty-two thousand heavenly sons attained the forbearance of non-arising dharmas,
and Huádé Púsà attained the Lotus Sūtra samādhi.”
Guānshìyīn Púsà, with the heart of Śuòjiāluó capable of transformative response without limit, freely exercises supernatural
powers, traveling everywhere in the Dharma Realm, entering worlds as fine as dust motes to teach and deliver, perfectly possessing
auspicious marks and vast vows like the ocean. Whenever there is a karmic connection and the mind is made pure, as soon as
one calls upon the name, a response is given; whatever aspiration or wish, it is fulfilled accordingly. This Universal Gateway Chapter of the
Lotus Sūtra is the true method for saving those from suffering and distress. If a person can
habitually contemplate this sūtra, even as the thought first arises, he immediately beholds the supreme mark of great compassion, and is able
to extinguish all suffering. Its merit is inconceivable. I, the Emperor, reflect that the Way of Heaven rewards good and brings disaster upon evil;
therefore the Buddha reveals retribution for good and evil, so that people do good and dare not commit evil.
Heaven and hell are all created by people themselves; nothing is outside the mind. Thus,
those who do good ascend to heaven; those who do evil fall into hell. Loyal ministers,
filial children, auspicious people, and chaste gentlemen—their hearts are already with the Buddha, therefore divine spirits protect them, their karmic obstacles
are all extinguished. Thus, in life they do not violate the law, and in death they do not fall into avīci hell. However,

the cruel and wicked only do evil—abandoning the Five Relationships as if they were worn-out shoes, treading upon the law as if drinking sweet wine, preferring to feed the rākṣasas, holding no reverence for the Buddha. Yet human nature is fundamentally good;
those who do evil are only misled by the biases of temperament; if they can but change their heart and thinking, cultivate reflection
and fearfulness, then in a single instant evil can turn to good. Doing good makes one a good person;
and the heavy offenses of the past, like dust in the vast sky or a flake of snow on a glowing furnace, are melted and
cleansed away. Even if there were retribution, where could it be applied? I often contemplate this, only fearing those
in the world make mistakes without realizing or seeking to amend them, content to abandon themselves; for this reason, I have publicly
proclaimed this sūtra, so that all good people and gentlemen may forever strengthen their hearts for restraint, and broadly accumulate
countless blessings, for how could the merits of doing good have any limits!
The first day of the fifth month, ninth year of Yǒnglè
The Lotus Sūtra, Universal Gateway of Guānshìyīn Púsà
Chapter of the Sūtra
Translated in long prose by Kumārajīva, the Tripiṭaka Master of the Yáo Qín dynasty,
and the verse section by Śramaṇa Shénàjuéduō from Uttara India of the Sui dynasty.
At that time, Wújìnyì Púsà immediately rose from his seat,
baring his right shoulder,
joining his palms toward the Buddha,
and said:
“World-honored One!
Guānshìyīn Púsà—
for what reason is he named Guānshìyīn?”
The Buddha told Wújìnyì Púsà:
“Virtuous man!
If there are innumerable hundreds of thousands of millions of beings suffering various agonies,
hearing of this Guānshìyīn Púsà,
and single-mindedly reciting his name,
Guānshìyīn Púsà immediately listens to their cries,
and all obtain deliverance.
If any uphold the name of Guānshìyīn Púsà,
even if they enter a great fire,
the fire will not burn them,
because of the awesome spiritual power of this bodhisattva.
If they are swept away by great water,
and call upon his name,
they will immediately reach safety.
If there are hundreds of thousands of millions seeking gold, silver, lapis lazuli, carnelian, agate, coral, amber, pearls, and other jewels,
who enter great seas,
and if a dark wind blows their ship
casting them adrift to the land of rākṣasas,
among them, if even one person recites the name of Guānshìyīn Púsà,
then all such people will be delivered from the dangers of the rākṣasas.
For this reason, he is called Guānshìyīn.
If again, someone faces mortal danger,
and calls on the name of Guānshìyīn Púsà,
whatever weapons are raised against him immediately break in pieces, thus he gains deliverance.
If the Three Thousand Great Thousand Worlds
were filled with yasha and rākṣasas, desiring to torment people,
yet upon hearing anyone call the name of Guānshìyīn Púsà, these fierce demons
could not so much as look at him with evil eyes,
much less harm him.
Even if someone,
guilty or innocent, is bound with shackles and chains,
and calls on the name of Guānshìyīn Púsà, all such bindings will break, and he will be set free.
If the Three Thousand Great Thousand Worlds
were filled with hostile bandits,
and among them a caravan leader
guides merchants carrying heavy treasure, passing through perilous roads,
and a person among them cries out:
‘All you virtuous men! Do not fear!
You should whole-heartedly recite the name of Guānshìyīn Púsà.
This bodhisattva can bestow fearlessness upon all beings.
If you recite his name,
you will be freed from these bandits.’
The merchants, upon hearing this,
all cry out together:
‘Homage to Guānshìyīn Púsà!’
Because of reciting his name,
they are all delivered.
Wújìnyì!
If there are sentient beings who are greatly attached to sensual desire,
by constantly and respectfully contemplating Guānshìyīn Púsà,
they will be able to free themselves from desire.
If they are greatly prone to anger,
by constantly and respectfully contemplating Guānshìyīn Púsà,
they will be able to free themselves from anger.
If they are greatly deluded and ignorant,
by constantly and respectfully contemplating Guānshìyīn Púsà,
they will be able to free themselves from ignorance.
Wújìnyì!
Guānshìyīn Púsà possesses such great supernatural power,
benefiting many,
therefore sentient beings should constantly keep this in mind.
If a woman wishes to have a son,
and makes offerings and worships Guānshìyīn Púsà,
she will give birth to a son endowed with merit, virtue, and wisdom;
if she wishes to have a daughter,
she will give birth to a daughter who is dignified and beautiful.
With roots of virtue planted in previous lives,
such a daughter will be loved and respected by all.
Wújìnyì!
Guānshìyīn Púsà has such power that
if there are sentient beings who respectfully worship Guānshìyīn Púsà,
the merit will never be lost in vain.
Therefore all sentient beings should uphold and maintain the name of Guānshìyīn Púsà.
"Wújìnyì!
If there are people who uphold the names of sixty-two billions of Ganges sands' worth of Bodhisattvas,
and further, for the rest of their lives, make offerings of food, clothing, bedding, and medicine,
what do you think?
Would these good men and good women gain much merit?"
Wújìnyì replied:
"Very much,
World Honored One!"
The Buddha said:
"If there is another person who upholds the name of Guānshìyīn Púsà,
even for a single moment pays homage and makes offerings,
the merit of these two is equal and without distinction,
and for hundreds of thousands of millions of eons it cannot be exhausted.
Wújìnyì!
Upholding the name of Guānshìyīn Púsà
grants such limitless and boundless merit and benefit."
Wújìnyì Púsà addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World Honored One! Guānshìyīn Púsà,
how does he travel in this Sahā World?
How does he speak the Dharma for sentient beings?
What is the power of skillful means, and how is this achieved?"
The Buddha told Wújìnyì Púsà:
Good man!
If in any land there are beings who can be liberated by means of a Buddha's body,
then Guānshìyīn Púsà immediately manifests a Buddha's body and preaches the Dharma for them;
if they can be liberated by means of a Pratyekabuddha's body,
he immediately manifests as a Pratyekabuddha and preaches the Dharma for them;
if they can be liberated by means of a Śrāvaka's body,
he immediately manifests as a Śrāvaka and preaches the Dharma for them;
if they can be liberated by means of a Brahmā King's body,
he immediately manifests as a Brahmā King and preaches the Dharma for them;
if they can be liberated by means of an Indra's body,
he immediately manifests as Indra and preaches the Dharma for them;
if they can be liberated by means of a guardian deity's body,
he immediately manifests as that deity and preaches the Dharma for them;
if they can be liberated by means of a Mahābrahmā's body,
he immediately manifests as Mahābrahmā and preaches the Dharma for them;
if they can be liberated by means of the body of a heavenly general,
he immediately manifests as a heavenly general and preaches the Dharma for them;
if they can be liberated by means of the body of Bìshāmén,
he immediately manifests as Bìshāmén and preaches the Dharma for them;
if they can be liberated by means of a small king's body,
he immediately manifests as a small king and preaches the Dharma for them;
if they can be liberated by means of an elder's body,
he immediately manifests as an elder and preaches the Dharma for them;
if they can be liberated by means of a layperson's body,
he immediately manifests as a layperson and preaches the Dharma for them;
if they can be liberated by means of a minister's body,
he immediately manifests as a minister and preaches the Dharma for them;
if they can be liberated by means of a brāhmaṇa's body,
he immediately manifests as a brāhmaṇa and preaches the Dharma for them;
if they can be liberated by means of monks, nuns, upāsakas, or upāsikās, he immediately manifests as a monk, nun, upāsaka, or upāsikā and preaches the Dharma for them;
if they can be liberated by means of the bodies of the wives of elders, laypersons, ministers, or brāhmaṇas,
he immediately manifests as a woman and preaches the Dharma for them;
if they can be liberated by means of young boys or girls,
he immediately manifests as young boys or girls and preaches the Dharma for them;
if they can be liberated by means of the bodies of gods, dragons, yaksas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans or non-humans,
he manifests as all of these and preaches the Dharma for them;
if they can be liberated by means of a Vajra-Wielder's body,
he immediately manifests as a Vajra-Wielder and preaches the Dharma for them.
"Wújìnyì!
It is in this manner that Guānshìyīn Púsà perfects such merit,
using various forms,
to travel through all lands and liberate sentient beings.
Therefore, all of you should single-mindedly make offerings to Guānshìyīn Púsà.
This Guānshìyīn Mahāsattva, in times of terror and urgent difficulty, can bestow fearlessness,
therefore, in this Sahā World, he is called the Giver of Fearlessness."
Wújìnyì Púsà addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World Honored One!
I now wish to make offerings to Guānshìyīn Púsà."
He immediately removed the exquisite pearl necklace from his neck,
worth a hundred thousand taels of gold,
and offered it, saying:
"Noble one! Accept this Dharma gift of precious jewels and necklace."
At that time, Guānshìyīn Púsà was unwilling to accept it.
Wújìnyì again addressed Guānshìyīn Púsà, saying:
"Noble one! Out of compassion for us,
please accept this necklace."
Then the Buddha told Guānshìyīn Púsà:
"You should have compassion for Wújìnyì Púsà and the four assemblies,
as well as the gods, dragons, yaksas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans and non-humans,
and accept this necklace."
Immediately, Guānshìyīn Púsà, out of compassion for the four assemblies,
and for gods, dragons, humans and non-humans,
accepted the necklace,
and divided it into two parts:
one part he offered to Shìjiāmóní Fó,
and the other part to the stupa of Duōbǎo Fó.
"Wújìnyì,
Guānshìyīn Púsà, with such sovereign spiritual power, roams in the Sahā World."
At that time, Wújìnyì Púsà asked in verse:
"The World Honored One, adorned with wondrous marks,
I now wish to ask again,
for what reason is this son of the Buddha
named 'Guānshìyīn'?
The Honored One adorned with all wondrous marks
responded in verse to Wújìnyì:
'Listen to the conduct of Guānyīn,
who responds well to every direction;
his vast vow as deep as the sea,
over countless eons, inconceivable;
he serves many thousands of millions of Buddhas,
and brings forth a great, pure vow.
I now briefly tell this for you:
those who hear his name and see his body,
if they hold him in their hearts and do not let thoughts pass in vain,
can eliminate all suffering.
Suppose one conceives a harmful intent,
and is pushed into a great pit of fire,
by mindful recitation of Guānyīn's power,
the fire-pit will turn into a pond.
Or when adrift on a vast sea,
threatened by dragons, fish, and demons,
by mindful recitation of Guānyīn's power,
the waves cannot drown them.
Or on the summit of Mount Sumeru,
if pushed and made to fall by others,
by mindful recitation of Guānyīn's power,
one will dwell in the air as if the sun in empty space.
Or if pursued by evil men,
and fall down from Mount Vajra,
by mindful recitation of Guānyīn's power,
not even a single hair will be harmed.
If beset on all sides by enemies or thieves,
each wielding blades to harm,
by mindful recitation of Guānyīn's power,
they will all give rise to a compassionate mind.
Or when suffering under a tyrant,
at the point of execution and life nearly over,
by mindful recitation of Guānyīn's power,
the blade will immediately break to pieces.
If imprisoned in fetters and locks,
with hands and feet bound in chains and shackles,
by mindful recitation of Guānyīn's power,
they will suddenly be freed and released.
If one is cursed or given poisonous potions,
desiring to harm the body,
by mindful recitation of Guānyīn's power,
the harm will return to its originator.
Or when encountering evil rākṣasas,
poisonous dragons and demons,
by mindful recitation of Guānyīn's power,
none will dare cause harm.
If surrounded by evil beasts,
with fierce fangs and claws, terrifying,
by mindful recitation of Guānyīn's power,
they will swiftly flee in all directions.
Vipers and scorpions,
whose noxious breaths are like smoke and fire,
by mindful recitation of Guānyīn's power,
upon hearing the sound, will turn and withdraw.
Clouds, thunder, and lightning flash,
hail rains down and storms pour,
by mindful recitation of Guānyīn's power,
all will at once be dispersed.
When beings are beset by hardships,
with limitless suffering pressing upon them,
the wondrous wisdom and power of Guānyīn
can save the world from suffering.
Perfected in miraculous powers,
widely cultivating wisdom and skillful means,
in all the lands of the ten directions,
there is not a realm where he does not appear.
Among all the various evil destinies—
hells, ghosts, and animals—
and the sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, and death,
he gradually causes them all to be extinguished.
True contemplation, pure contemplation,
vast and great wisdom contemplation,
compassionate contemplation and loving-kindness contemplation,
always wished for, always gazed upon.
Unstained, pure radiance,
the sun of wisdom disperses all darkness,
subdues calamities of wind and fire,
universally illumines all the world.
With a mournful form admonishing like thunder’s peal,
With a mind of compassion, wondrous as great clouds,
He sends down the Dharma rain as sweet dew,
Quenching and extinguishing the flames of affliction.
In disputes and contentious trials in official places,
In fearsome battle lines and military ranks,
Think on the power of Guān Yīn,
All hostilities and enmity will then disperse.
Wondrous voice, Guānshìyīn,
Brahmā’s voice, the voice of ocean-tide,
Surpassing the sounds of this world,
Therefore one should ever keep him in mind,
And with every thought let no doubt arise.
Guānshìyīn, pure and sacred,
In suffering, distress, and mortal danger,
Can serve as refuge and reliance,
Perfect in all merit and virtue,
With compassionate eyes regarding all beings,
A sea of blessings gathered beyond measure,
Therefore one should pay him homage.” ’ ”
At that time, the Bodhisattva Chídì immediately rose from his seat, and addressed the Buddha, saying: “Bhagavān!
If there are sentient beings who hear of the sovereign deeds of Guānshìyīn Púsà, manifesting universally
the Door of Everywhere, revealing miraculous powers—one should know that such persons possess boundless merit.”
When the Buddha spoke this Universal Gate Chapter, among the assembly of eighty-four thousand sentient beings, all gave rise
to the supreme, unequalled mind of Anuttarā Samyaksaṃbodhi.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Yàowáng immediately rose from his seat,
bared his right shoulder,
joined his palms and faced the Buddha,
and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Bhagavān! If good men or good women are able to receive and uphold the Lotus Sūtra—
whether reading, reciting, penetrating its meaning,
whether copying and transcribing the sūtra—
what kind of blessings do they obtain?”
The Buddha said to Yàowáng:
“If there are good men or good women
who make offerings to eight million myriad nayuta as many Buddhas as grains of sand in the Ganges River,
what do you think—
would the merit obtained thereby be great or not?”
“Immeasurably great, Bhagavān.”
The Buddha said:
“If good men or good women
can, with respect to this sūtra,
even receive and uphold just one four-line verse,
reading, reciting, understanding its meaning, and practicing as taught,
their merit is exceedingly great.”
At that time, the Bodhisattva Yàowáng said to the Buddha:
“Bhagavān!
Now I will give a dhāraṇī spell protector to those who preach the Dharma,
so as to safeguard them.”
Then he spoke this spell, saying:

Zhelidi (6) Shami (goat's bleat) (7) Sheli (pheasant's call) Douwěi (8) Shāndì (9)

“Bhagavān! This dhāraṇī sacred spell
has been spoken by as many Buddhas as sixty-two billion Ganges’ sands.
If anyone should harm this Dharma teacher,
it is as if they harm all these Buddhas.”
Then Shìjiāmóuní Fó praised the Bodhisattva Yàowáng, saying:
“Excellent, excellent, Yàowáng!
Because you have compassion and wish to protect this Dharma teacher,
you have spoken this dhāraṇī, bringing much benefit to sentient beings.”
At that time, the Bodhisattva Yǒngshī said to the Buddha:
“Bhagavān!
I also, to protect those who read, recite, and uphold the Lotus Sūtra, shall speak a dhāraṇī.
If this Dharma teacher attains this dhāraṇī,
then whether yàchā, luóshā, fù dān nà, jí zhē, jiū pán chá, or hungry ghosts, etc.,
are seeking an opportunity to harm them, none will find any advantage.”
Thereupon, before the Buddha, he spoke the spell, saying:

“Cuó lì (read as shì luó) (1) Móhē cuó lì (2) Yù zhī (3) Mù zhī (4) ā lì (5) ā luóbādì (6) Niè lì dì (7) Niè lì duō bādì (8) Yī zhì (read as zhū lǐ) nǐ (read as nǚ shì) (9) Wéi zhì nǐ (10) Zhǐ zhì nǐ (11) Niè lì qún nǐ (12) Niè lí qún bādì (13)
“Bhagavān!
This dhāraṇī sacred spell
was spoken by Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
all rejoicing accordingly.
If anyone harms this Dharma teacher,
it is as if they harm all these Buddhas.”
At that time, Vaiśravaṇa Tiān Wáng, the guardian of the world, said to the Buddha:
“Bhagavān!
I too, out of pity for sentient beings and to protect this Dharma teacher,
shall proclaim a dhāraṇī.” At once he spoke the spell, saying:
“Ālí (1) Nàlí (2) Bì nàlí (3) Ā nàlú (4) Nà lǐ (5) Jūnà lǐ (6)
“Bhagavān! With this divine spell I protect the Dharma teacher,
and I myself will surely protect the one who upholds this sūtra,
so that within a hundred yōjana there will be no calamity or harm.”
At that time, Chíguó Tiān Wáng was present in the assembly,
with ten thousand myriad nayuta of gandharvas, respectfully encircling him,
approached the Buddha,
and with joined palms said to the Buddha:
“Bhagavān!
I also with a dhāraṇī divine spell
shall protect one who upholds the Lotus Sūtra.”
And immediately spoke the spell, saying:
Ā jiā nì (1) jiā nì (2) qú lì (3) gān tuólì (4) zhān tuólì (5) mó dēng qí (6) cháng qiú lì (7) fú lóu shā nǐ (8) è dì (9)
“Bhagavān!
This dhāraṇī divine spell,
has been spoken by forty-two billion Buddhas.
If anyone harms this Dharma teacher,
it is as if they harm all these Buddhas.”
At this time, there were ten rākṣasī women:
one named Lánbó, two named Pílánbó, three named Qūchǐ, four named Huáchǐ, five named Hēichǐ,
six named Duōfà, seven named Wúyànzú, eight named Chíyīngluò,
nine named Gāodì, ten named She Who Takes the Vital Essence of All Beings,
these ten rākṣasī,
together with Hārītī and her children and retinue,
all went to the Buddha and in one voice said to the Buddha:
“Bhagavān!
We also wish to protect those who read, recite, and uphold the Lotus Sūtra,
removing any harm or misfortune.
If anyone seeks the faults of the Dharma teacher,
let them find no opportunity.”
Thereupon before the Buddha, they spoke this spell, saying:
Yītílǚ (1) Yītímǐn (2) Yītílǚ (3) Ātílǚ (4) Yītílǚ (5) Nílǚ (6) Nílǚ (7) Nílǚ (8) Nílǚ (9) Nílǚ (10) Lóuxī (11) Lóuxī (12) Lóuxī (13) Lóuxī (14) Duōxī (15) Duōxī (16) Duōxī (17) Dōuxī (18) Bìxī (19)
“Rather may it be on top of my own head than bring distress upon the Dharma teacher.
Whether yàchā, luóshā, hungry ghosts, fù dān nà, jí zhē, pítuóluó,
jiān tuó, wūmó lèjiā, ā bá mó luó, yàchā jí zhē, rén jí zhē, or fevers
lasting one day, two days, three days, four days, up to seven days,
or chronic fevers,
in male form, female form,
boy form, girl form,
even in dreams, do not bring distress.”
Thereupon before the Buddha, they spoke these verses:
“If you do not follow my spell,
and trouble those who preach the Dharma,
your head shall split into seven pieces,
like the branches of the arālī tree.
It is like the offense of killing one’s parents,
like the disaster of pressing oil,
like cheating with weights and measures,
or the offense of Devadatta breaking the Saṃgha.
Who offends this Dharma teacher
will surely meet with such calamities.”
Having spoken this verse, the rākṣasī said to the Buddha:
“Bhagavān!
We too shall personally protect those who uphold, read, recite, and practice this sūtra,
to grant them peace and safety,
to free them from misfortune and harm,
and to neutralize all poisons.”
The Buddha said to the rākṣasī:
“Excellent, excellent!
If you can but protect those who uphold even the name of the Lotus Sūtra,
the blessings are immeasurable—
how much more so for protecting those who perfectly uphold it,
make offerings of the sūtra scrolls—
flowers, incense, necklaces, powdered incense, paste incense, burning incense, banners and canopies, music,
and burn all kinds of lamps—ghee lamps, oil lamps, various aromatic oil lamps,
sūmànā flower oil lamps, zhānbó flower oil lamps, póshījiā flower oil lamps, yōupōluó flower oil lamps,
and a hundred thousand different offerings such as these.
Gāodì! You and your retinue should protect such a Dharma teacher.”
When this Dhāraṇī Chapter was spoken,
sixty-eight thousand people attained the forbearance of non-arising of dharmas.
At that time, the Buddha said to the great assembly:
“In the distant past,
countless, boundless, inconceivable asaṃkhyeya kalpas ago,
there was a Buddha named Yúnléiyīn Sùwánghuázhì Duótuó Ājiāduò, Ā luóhàn, Sānmiǎosān fótuó,
in the country called Guāngmíng Zhuāngyán, in the kalpa named Xǐjiàn.
At that time, there was a king under his Dharma, named Miàozhuāngyán.
The king’s consort was named Jìngdé, and they had two sons:
one named Jìngzàng, and the other named Jìngyǎn.
These two sons had great spiritual power, merit, and wisdom,
having long cultivated the Bodhisattva path—
namely, dāna pāramitā, śīla pāramitā, kṣānti pāramitā, vīrya pāramitā,
dhyāna pāramitā, prajñā pāramitā, upāya pāramitā, compassion, loving-kindness, joy, and equanimity,
even up to the thirty-seven aids to enlightenment,
all fully comprehended and mastered.
They also attained the Bodhisattva’s pure samādhi,
the Sun and Stars samādhi, and the Radiant Clarity samādhi,
the Pure Color samādhi,
the Pure Illuminating samādhi,
the Long Adornment samādhi,
the Great Power Treasury samādhi—
all these samādhis they thoroughly understood and mastered.
At that time, that Buddha, wishing to guide King Miàozhuāngyán,
and out of compassion for sentient beings,
preached the Lotus Sūtra.
At that time, the two sons Jìngzàng and Jìngyǎn went to their mother,
joined the ten nails of their fingers in palms and said:
‘May mother go to see Yúnléiyīn Sùwánghuázhì Buddha.
We also wish to attend and follow, be close to, make offerings, and pay respects.
Why is this?
Because among all gods and humans, this Buddha is preaching the Lotus Sūtra, and we should listen and receive it.’
The mother said to her sons:
‘Your father accepts the doctrines of external paths, is deeply attached to brahmin practices;
you should go and speak to your father and go together with him.’
Jìngzàng and Jìngyǎn joined the ten nails of their fingers in their palms and said to their mother:
‘We are Dharma princes, yet are born into a family with wrong views.’
The mother said to her sons:
‘You should feel concern for your father and display a miraculous transformation;
if he sees it,
his mind will surely become pure, and perhaps he will listen to us and allow us to go to see the Buddha.’
At this, the two sons remembered their father,
leaped into the open air, rising seven tāla trees high,
and manifested various supernatural transformations—
walking, standing, sitting, and lying down in midair;
from the upper body, water issued,
from below, fire arose;
from below, water issued,
from above, fire arose;
sometimes showing a great body filling the sky, then becoming small again,
and small becoming great;
vanishing in the air, suddenly reappearing on the ground;
entering the earth as if it were water, and walking upon water as if it were land.
They displayed such various supernatural transformations, causing their father, the king, to bring forth pure faith and understanding.
Then, when the father saw the divine powers of his sons,
his heart rejoiced greatly, as never before,
and joining his palms, he addressed his sons:
“You, who is your teacher, and whose disciples are you?”
The two sons replied:
“Great King!
That Yúnléiyīn Sùwáng Huázhì Buddha
now sits beneath the seven-jeweled bodhi-tree, upon the Dharma throne,
teaching the Lotus Sūtra expansively among the multitude of heavenly and human beings in the world.
He is our teacher; we are his disciples.”
The father said to his sons:
“I also wish to see your teacher.
Let us go together.”
Thereupon the two sons descended from the sky,
came to their mother, joined their palms, and said to her:
“The king, our father, now has faith and understanding,
and is able to give rise to the aspiration for Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.
We have performed the Buddha’s work for our father,
and now hope that our mother will permit us
to leave home and practice the Way at the place of that Buddha.”
Then the two sons, wishing to further declare their intent,
spoke in verse to their mother:
“We pray our mother will let us leave home to become monks.
Buddhas are extremely hard to encounter,
and we wish to follow the Buddha’s teaching.
Just like the udumbara flower, so rare to meet a Buddha,
and deliverance from all difficulties is also difficult.
Please permit us to leave home.”
The mother replied at once:
“I permit you to leave home.
And why? Because meeting a Buddha is hard.”
Thereupon the two sons addressed their parents:
“Excellent, father and mother!
Let us now go and visit Yúnléiyīn Sùwáng Huázhì Buddha,
to draw near and make offerings.
And why?
Because meeting a Buddha is as rare as the udumbara blossom,
or as a one-eyed turtle encountering a hole in floating wood.
Through the deep merit and blessing of our past lives,
we have been born in the era of the Buddha’s teaching.
Therefore, father and mother, you should allow us to leave home.
And why?
Because buddhas are hard to encounter, and the time is difficult to meet.”
At that time, in the inner palace of King Miàozhuāngyán, eighty-four thousand ladies-in-waiting
were all capable of upholding the Lotus Sūtra.
Bodhisattva Jìngyǎn had long achieved mastery of the samādhi of the Lotus Sūtra;
Bodhisattva Jìngzàng, over countless hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas, had mastered the samādhi that severs all evil destinies,
wishing that all sentient beings be freed from evil destinies.
The king’s consort attained the Samādhi of All the Buddhas’ Assemblies,
able to know the secret treasury of all buddhas.
“Thus did the two sons, by the power of skillful means, skillfully transform their father,
causing his mind to have faith and understanding,
and to rejoice in the Buddha-dharma.
Thereupon King Miàozhuāngyán, together with his ministers and retinue,
Lady Jìngdé, along with the palace ladies and her retinue,
the king’s two sons, along with forty-two thousand others,
all together went to the Buddha’s place at one time.
Having arrived,
they bowed their heads to the Buddha’s feet,
circumambulated him three times,
and stood to one side.
At that time, that Buddha taught the Dharma to the king,
instructing, guiding, benefiting, and delighting him.
The king rejoiced greatly.
Then King Miàozhuāngyán and his queen removed their jeweled necklaces from their necks,
worth hundreds of thousands,
and scattered them upon the Buddha.
In the sky, they transformed into a jewel-pavilion upheld by four pillars,
within which there was a great jeweled couch covered with hundreds of thousands of heavenly garments,
and upon it the Buddha sat in meditation, radiating great light.
At that time, King Miàozhuāngyán reflected:
‘The Buddha’s body is rare,
supremely dignified and extraordinary,
endowed with the foremost subtle and marvelous appearance.’
Then Yúnléiyīn Sùwáng Huázhì Buddha addressed the fourfold assembly:
‘Do you see King Miàozhuāngyán standing before me with joined palms?
This king, in my Dharma, will become a monk,
diligently cultivating and supporting the Buddha’s Dharma,
and will become a buddha,
by the name Sāluóshùwáng,
in a country called Great Light,
during a kalpa called Great Lofty King.
That Sāluóshùwáng Buddha will have countless bodhisattvas and śrāvakas,
and his land will be equitable and harmonious,
with such merits as these.’
The king immediately entrusted the kingdom to his younger brother,
and, together with the queen, his two sons, and their retinue,
left home to cultivate the Way in the Buddha’s Dharma.
“After the king renounced household life,
for eighty-four thousand years he applied himself diligently to practicing the sublime Lotus Sūtra.
After that time,
he attained the Samādhi of the Adornment of All Pure Merits,
and ascended into the air, rising seven tāla trees high,
and addressed the Buddha:
‘World-Honored One! My two sons have already accomplished the Buddha’s work,
by means of supernatural powers transforming my mistaken mind,
enabling me to dwell peacefully in the Buddha-dharma,
so that I have been able to see the World-Honored One.
These two sons are my good friends,
in order to arouse my good roots from past lives and to benefit me, they were born into my family.’
At that time, Yúnléiyīn Sùwáng Huázhì Buddha said to King Miàozhuāngyán:
‘So it is, so it is!
Just as you have said.
If good men and good women, because of planting good roots,
obtain good friends throughout every lifetime,
those good friends are able to act as buddhas do,
instructing, guiding, benefiting, and delighting,
leading one to Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Great King, know that a good friend is a great condition,
for it is they who lead and guide one to see the Buddha
and to awaken the aspiration for Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Great King, do you see these two sons?
These two sons have served and made offerings to sixty-five hundred thousand million nayutas of Ganges-sands buddhas,
drawing near with respect,
and have upheld the Lotus Sūtra in the presence of those buddhas,
out of compassion for beings with wrong views, causing them to abide in right views.’
King Miàozhuāngyán then descended from the air and said to the Buddha:
‘World-Honored One, the Tathāgata is most rare,
for, by virtue of merit and wisdom,
the flesh protuberance atop his head radiates splendidly,
his eyes are long, broad, and violet-blue in color,
the white tuft between his brows is as the autumn moon,
his teeth white, even, and always shining,
his lips red and beautiful like the bimba fruit.’
Then King Miàozhuāngyán,
after praising the Buddha’s immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of merits,
before the Tathāgata, joined his palms single-mindedly,
and again said to the Buddha:
‘World-Honored One, this is unheard of.
The Tathāgata’s Dharma is fully accomplished in inconceivable, subtle merits and virtues,
and his teachings and practices are peaceful, secure, joyful, and wholesome.
From this day forth I will no longer follow my own mind, nor give rise to wrong views, pride, wrath, or any evil mindset.’
When these words were spoken, he bowed to the Buddha and departed.”
The Buddha spoke to the great assembly:
“What do you think?
Was King Miàozhuāngyán someone other than you know?
Today, he is Huádé Bodhisattva;
his consort Jìngdé is now the Bodhisattva Guāngzhào Zhuāngyán Xiàng before the Buddha.
Out of compassion for King Miàozhuāngyán and his retinue,
she was born among them.
The two sons are now the Bodhisattva Yàowáng and the Bodhisattva Yàoshàng.
These two bodhisattvas, Yàowáng and Yàoshàng, have accomplished such great merits,
have already planted the roots of merit in the presence of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of buddhas,
and have achieved inconceivable and excellent merits.
If anyone knows the names of these two bodhisattvas,
all the heavenly and human beings of the worlds should pay them reverence.”
When the Buddha expounded the chapter on King Miàozhuāngyán’s former deeds,
eighty-four thousand people were freed from dust and defilement,
and attained the pure Dharma eye amongst the teachings.
Then Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, with the power of sovereign supernatural ability, famous for his majesty and virtue,
together with countless, boundless great bodhisattvas,
came from the east.
All the countries they passed through quaked, rained jeweled lotus flowers,
and made countless hundreds of thousands of billions of various kinds of music.
Moreover, countless devas, nāgas, yaksas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, men and non-humans, encircled in a great assembly,
each displaying the power of majestic supernatural abilities,
arrived at Mount Qízhúé in the Sahā World,
bowed their heads at the feet of Shìjiāmóuní Buddha,
and circumambulated him seven times to the right;
then said to the Buddha:
“World-Honored One, in the buddha land of Bǎowēidé Shàngwáng Buddha,
from afar I heard that the Lotus Sūtra is being expounded in this Sahā World,
so together with countless hundreds of thousands of millions of bodhisattvas I have come to listen and receive it.
May the World-Honored One please expound it.
If good men and good women, after the Tathāgata’s extinction,
wish to obtain this Lotus Sūtra, how can they do so?”
The Buddha said to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva:
“If good men and good women accomplish four things, then after the Tathāgata’s extinction,
they will be able to obtain this Lotus Sūtra:
Firstly, to be protected and kept in mind by all buddhas;
secondly, to plant the roots of all merits;
thirdly, to enter the assembly of right concentration;
fourthly, to give rise to the heart of rescuing all sentient beings.
Good men and good women, if they accomplish these four things,
then after the Tathāgata’s extinction, they are certain to obtain this sūtra.”
At that time, Pǔxián Púsà addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One! In the latter five hundred years, amid a defiled and evil world,
whosoever upholds this scripture,
I shall guard and protect,
removing their decline and afflictions,
and enabling them to attain peace and safety.
Let none who seek a chance to spy or harm them find opportunity,
whether they be Māra, sons of Māra, daughters of Māra,
people of Māra, those possessed by Māra, yakṣas, rākṣasas,
kumbhāṇḍas, piśācas, kiṃnaras, futannas,
vetālas, and the like—those who trouble people—none shall find an opening.
Whether walking or standing,
reciting this sūtra,
at that time, I will ride the six-tusked white elephant king,
accompanied by a great assembly of bodhisattvas, and approach their place,
manifesting my own body,
offering reverence and protection,
and consoling their minds,
all also for the sake of revering the *Fǎhuá Jīng*.
If someone sits and contemplates this sūtra,
then again I shall ride the white elephant king and appear before them.
If they should forget or lose even a single line or verse of the *Fǎhuá Jīng*,
I will instruct and recite it together with them, causing them to regain mastery.
At that time, any who uphold and recite the *Fǎhuá Jīng* shall see my person,
and be filled with great joy,
advancing further in diligence.
By seeing me,
they will immediately attain samādhi and dhāraṇī,
named Xuán Dhāraṇī,
Hundred Thousand Million Myriadfold Xuán Dhāraṇī,
Dharma-Sound Skillful Means Dhāraṇī,
and attain such dhāraṇīs as these.
“World-Honored One! If, in the generations after the last five hundred years, in that defiled and evil age,
bhikṣus, bhikṣunīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, those who seek,
those who uphold, recite, or transcribe, desiring to cultivate and study this *Fǎhuá Jīng*,
for twenty-one days should practice single-minded diligence.
When twenty-one days are fulfilled,
I shall ride the six-tusked white elephant,
surrounded by innumerable bodhisattvas,
manifesting myself in a body pleasing to all beings,
appearing before them to preach the Dharma,
show, teach, benefit, and gladden,
and also bestow upon them the dhāraṇī mantra.
In obtaining this dhāraṇī,
there will be no nonhuman able to bring them harm,
nor will they be led astray by women— some manuscripts have: [or be disturbed].
My own body shall ever protect such people.
I only request the World-Honored One to permit me to recite this dhāraṇī mantra.”
Then, before the Buddha, he recited the mantra, saying:
“Ā tán dì (tú mài fǎn) (1) Tán tuó pó dì (2) Tán tuó pó dì (3) Tán tuó jiū shě lì (4) Tán tuó xiū tuó lì (5)
Xiū tuó lì (6) Xiū tuó luó pó dǐ (7) Fó tuó bō xiān ní (8) Sà pó tuó luó ní ā pó duō ní (9)
Sà pó pó shā ā pó duō ní (10) Xiū ā pó duō ní (11) Sēng qié pó lǚ chǎ ní (12)
Sēng qié niè qié tuó ní (13) Ā sēng qí (14) Sēng qié bō qié dì (15) Dì lì ā duò sēng qié dōu lüè (lú zhē fǎn) ā luó dì pó luó dì (16)
Sà pó sēng qié sān mó dì qié lán dì (17) Sà pó dá mó xiū bō lì chà dì (18)
Sà pó sà duǒ lóu tuó jiāo shě lüè ā xìng qié dì (19) Xīn ā pí jí lì dì dì (20)
“World-Honored One! Should there be a bodhisattva who hears this dhāraṇī,
know that this is the power of Pǔxián’s supernatural abilities.
If, in Jambudvīpa, the *Fǎhuá Jīng* is practiced and upheld,
one should think thus:
‘This is altogether due to the sovereign power of Pǔxián.’
If there are any who accept, recite, and properly recall it,
understand its meaning, and practice as taught,
one should know that these people practice the conduct of Pǔxián,
and in the presence of immeasurable and boundless Buddhas, have deeply planted good roots,
being caressed atop the head by the Thus-Come Ones’ hands.
If they only transcribe it,
then at life’s end, they will be born in the Trāyastriṃśa heaven,
where eighty-four thousand goddesses will come with myriad music to welcome them.
They will don a jeweled crown of seven treasures and rejoice among the heavenly maidens;
how much more so those who accept, recite, and properly recall it,
understand the meaning, and cultivate as taught.
If there are any who uphold and recite, and comprehend its meaning,
at the end of life,
they will be greeted hand-in-hand by a thousand Buddhas,
so that they have no fear, fall into no evil paths,
and are immediately reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven, in the presence of Mílè Púsà.
Mílè Púsà, possessed of thirty-two marks, dwells surrounded by a great assembly of bodhisattvas,
and has hundreds of thousands of millions of goddesses as retinue;
they will be born there among them,
gaining merits and benefits such as these.
Therefore, the wise should, with single-mindedness, write this themselves,
or have others write it,
and uphold, recite,
and properly recall and practice as taught.
“World-Honored One,
now by the power of my supernatural abilities, I shall protect this sūtra,
and after the Thus-Come One’s parinirvāṇa, in Jambudvīpa, will cause it to widely circulate,
ensuring it is never extinguished.”
At that time, Shìjiā Móuní Fó praised, saying:
“Excellent, excellent, Pǔxián!
You are able to protect and assist this sūtra,
enabling many beings to gain peace and benefit.
You have accomplished inconceivable merit,
profound, great compassion,
from time immemorial giving rise to the aspiration for Anuttarā Samyaksaṃbodhi,
and can thus make such a supernatural vow to guard this sūtra.
I, too, by my supernatural abilities, will protect those who uphold the name of Pǔxián Púsà.
Pǔxián!
Should any uphold and recite,
properly recall, practice, and transcribe this *Fǎhuá Jīng*,
know that such a person will see Shìjiā Móuní Fó,
as if hearing this scripture from the Buddha’s very mouth;
know that this person makes offerings to Shìjiā Móuní Fó;
know that this person is praised by the Buddha as excellent;
know that this person has the head caressed by the hand of Shìjiā Móuní Fó;
know that this person is protected beneath the robe of Shìjiā Móuní Fó.
Such a person will no longer be attached to worldly pleasures,
will not delight in the texts or calligraphy of heretics,
nor take pleasure in associating with such people or those of evil ways—
be they butchers, keepers of pigs, sheep, chickens, dogs, hunters,
or traffickers in women—
such a person’s mind will be upright and sincerely mindful,
possessed of the power of good fortune,
untroubled by the three poisons,
and not afflicted by jealousy, arrogance, perverse pride, or overwhelming pride.
Such a person will be content with little, knowing satisfaction,
and will be able to cultivate the conduct of Pǔxián.
Pǔxián!
If, five hundred years after the Thus-Come One’s nirvāṇa,
someone sees another upholding and reciting the *Fǎhuá Jīng*,
they should think this:
‘This person will soon reach the bodhimaṇḍa,
defeat the hosts of Māras,
attain Anuttarā Samyaksaṃbodhi,
turn the Dharma wheel,
beat the Dharma drum,
blow the Dharma conch,
rain the Dharma rain,
and sit enthroned on the lion seat amidst the assembly of gods and men.’
“Pǔxián!
If, in the generations to come, there are those who accept and recite this scripture,
such people will not again be attached to clothing, beds, food, or means of livelihood,
and whatever they wish will not be in vain;
even in this present life they shall obtain its recompense.
If anyone belittles them, saying,
‘You are a madman,
vainly doing these things—
in the end, you will gain nothing!’
the retribution for such a sin will be to lack eyesight in every lifetime;
if there are those who make offerings or praise them,
they will obtain the immediate fruit in this very life.
If anyone, seeing someone upholding this sūtra,
points out their faults,
be they real or unreal,
such a person will suffer white leprosy in this life.
If any ridicule them,
they will in each life have sparse and missing teeth,
ugly lips, flat noses, twisted hands and feet,
eyes askew,
a foul-smelling body,
evil sores, pus and blood,
dropsy, shortness of breath, and various grievous diseases.
Therefore, Pǔxián!
When seeing someone who upholds this scripture,
one should rise and greet them from afar,
as if revering the Buddha.”
When these Pǔxián’s Encouragement and Exhortation passages were spoken,
numerous as the sands of the Ganges, immeasurable bodhisattvas attained a hundred thousand myriad Xuán Dhāraṇī;
and as many bodhisattvas as dust motes in a great trichiliocosm acquired the Path of Pǔxián.
When the Buddha proclaimed this sūtra,
Pǔxián and all those bodhisattvas,
Shèlìfú and all the śrāvakas,
as well as gods, dragons, humans, and nonhumans,
the entire assembly, all felt great joy,
received and upheld the Buddha’s words,
paid reverent homage, and withdrew.

*The Wondrous Dharma Lotus Flower Sūtra*, Volume — below this, the Dūnhuáng manuscript has: “In the third year of Shengyuan, the pure and faithful devotee Zhāng Jūnchè devotedly copied, in remembrance of his late younger sister, these fifteen characters as a secret colophon” [Dūn], seven = eight [Dūn Bǐng], seven — below, the Dūnhuáng manuscript has: “In the third year of Shengyuan, the pure and faithful devotee Zhāng Jūnchè devotedly copied, in remembrance of his late younger sister, these fifteen characters as a secret colophon” [Dūn], seven
After Qín shāmén Sēngruì composed
on the Lotus Sūtra, he wrote: The Lotus Sūtra is the secret treasury of all Buddhas, and the true essence of all sūtras. The use of "Lotus"
as its name illuminates its source; calling it "Fēntuólì" praises its excellence in flourishing.
Since that which it expounds is so profound, and its meaning so subtle, if those of penetrating understanding do not transmit it,
seldom does anyone gain access to its gate. Indeed, just as the essence of a hundred flowers, medicinal herbs, and trees is the root of all fruits, so the eighty-four thousand stores of the Dharma
are the origins of the fruits of the Way. Therefore, it is used as a metaphor. Among all flowers,
the lotus is preeminent. Before it blooms, it is called qūmóluó; as it blooms about to wither, it is called jiāmóluó;

at its peak in the middle, it is called fēntuólì. The unbloomed is a metaphor for the Two Vehicles, the withering represents Nīruódé, but its splendid brilliance alone is sufficient to illustrate this scripture. As for the Prajñā Sūtras,
their depth knows no limit—thus, those who cultivate the Way turn to them; their vastness leaves nothing uncontained—thus, those who pursue the vehicle use them to cross over.
Yet in general, their great achievement lies in fitting transformation; in meeting needs, one cannot but employ skillful means. The skillful means of transformation, though illuminating for others,
are insufficient for the True Essence, all of which belong to the Lotus Sūtra. This is as it should be. Delving into its subtle intent,

it is grand and profound, encompassing a great range; how could it merely speak of the truth returning to the root or simply distinguish divergent paths and be done? Rather, it truly clarifies the principle of Great Enlightenment,
enveloping both past and present. It says the Buddha's lifespan is immeasurable—countless eons cannot describe its length;
his emanations are innumerable—ten thousand forms are not enough to express his essence. Thus, the fixed lifespan
reveals its transcendence of measure, the emanations reveal its unreality, Pǔxián manifests its incompleteness,

Duōbǎo illuminates its indestructibility. Thus, surpassing the ancient with this present, ten thousand ages become like one day; comprehending the myriad transformations through the mysterious, a thousand paths converge to a single track. Such being so,

successive lives are not enough to hope for its persistence, nor can eternal quiescence be spoken of as its extinction. If one seeks the subtle doctrine and severs the past, one loses merit in the root of non-being; if one reins the mind in samādhi, one forgets distinctions between the two grounds. Although the sūtra has circulated in this land for nearly a hundred years,
translators have been ignorant of its subtle stream, and the spiritual gate has remained unopened; those who discuss it have missed its standard

and rarely have any trodden its mysterious path; though they have diligently explored until white-haired, still none have glimpsed its gate. Yáo Sōng, Minister Inspector of Qín and Left General, Marquis of Ānchéng,
emulated the rhythms of the mysterious gate, set his heart above the world, poured sincerity into this scripture, had utmost trust and faith. Always striving to
pursue its text, he deeply recognized the errors of previous translators. Having met the Dharma Master Jiūmóluó, he

transmitted and copied it, pointing out its essential truth, as if soaring into the highest heavens, standing atop Kūnlún and gazing down. At that time, over eight hundred monks receiving, understanding,
and comprehending it—all were outstanding talents from various regions, the heroes of the age. That year was the eighth year of Hóngshǐ,
the year of Quail Fire.
Madam Zhāng of the state of Lǔ, on the anniversary

of her late husband, the Grand Tutor and Grand Chancellor Lord Lǐ Yuǎn, reverently donated pure wealth, one string of coins, to the scriptural collection office of Kāiyuán Monastery, Fúzhōu, for the engraving of phoenix-letter cases of the *Sūtra of the Wonderful Dharma Lotus Blossom*, seven fascicles, and the *Lotus Samādhi* and others,
hoping this supreme merit may help the deceased transcend and be reborn in the Pure Land. At the time, on the fifteenth day of the first month,
the twenty-first year of Shàoxīng, this was respectfully recorded.
